  • Coverage by RFC

A review of 449 RFCs covering BGP, IS-IS, MPLS, LDP, RSVP-TE, PCEP, PIM, BFD, pseudowires, measurement protocols and supporting IP and security specifications. Each finding names the RFC and section, quotes the text briefly, explains the contradiction, ambiguity or error, and gives the status of any existing erratum. Findings that look like errata not yet reported carry a proposed report in the RFC Editor's format (Original Text, Corrected Text, Notes). The review was done in two passes on 2026-11-09: a first pass over the most-used protocol specifications and an automated check of all texts, and a second pass that read the remaining texts.

Summary

1456 open findings in 410 RFCs; 171 match an existing erratum report; 648 are proposed new errata. 30 further findings are resolved by a later RFC in the set, or re-targeted to the RFC that replaces theirs, and are listed separately (Resolved by later RFCs); they are not counted below.

Resolved by later RFCs

Findings on a text that a later RFC in this set updates or obsoletes, where the later RFC settles the point. Each was checked against the updating RFC; findings that a later RFC only changes, or whose text the later RFC repeats, stay open and carry a "Later RFCs" note. "Re-targeted" marks a finding on an obsoleted RFC whose text the successor repeats and where the same point is recorded against the successor under its own id.

IDRFC, sectionIssue as foundOutcomeResolution
RA-0111RFC 2385 4.3"32-byte words" should be "32-bit words".ResolvedRFC 5925 (obsoletes RFC 2385) gives the Data Offset correctly in 32-bit words.
RA-0430RFC 4360 7Section 7, IPv4 address specific registry paragraph.ResolvedRFC 7153 (updates RFC 4360) reorganises the Extended Community registries (Sections 2 and 5); this paragraph no longer governs allocations.
RA-0431RFC 4360 7Section 7, Type range table.ResolvedRFC 7153 (updates RFC 4360) replaces the range table with its own registries (Sections 2 and 5).
RA-0450RFC 5701 3Section 2 ties the sub-types to the IPv4 Address Specific Extended Community registry, while Section 3 creates a separate "IPv6 Address Specific Extended Community" registry with First Come First Served allocation, so a sub-type could be allocated in one registry and not, or differently, in the other.ResolvedRFC 7153 Section 3 (updates RFC 5701) removes the requirement that IPv6 Address Specific sub-types match the IPv4 ones and creates separate IPv6 registries.
RA-0529RFC 5308 5In a two-level domain the up/down bit is never set in Level 2 LSPs (RFC 5302 3.1, RFC 5305 4.1), so "Level 2 down prefix" can only arise from a future multi-level extension or a misbehaving router;ResolvedRFC 7775 (updates RFC 5308), Sections 2 and 3.4: 'Level 2 down prefix' is withdrawn as an error and the preference order for TLVs 236 and 237 is restated, with internal and external routes of a level treated equally.
RA-0533RFC 5316 3.3.5An IPv6 TE Router ID is 16 octets;ResolvedRFC 9346 (obsoletes RFC 5316), Section 3.5.2: the IPv6 TE Router ID sub-TLV is 16 octets.
RA-0535RFC 5316 3.3.2The remote ASBR ID sub-TLVs are defined for the inter-AS reachability TLV (141);ResolvedRFC 9346 (obsoletes RFC 5316), Sections 3.5.1 and 3.5.2: the TE Router ID sub-TLVs 'MAY both be present in an IS-IS Router CAPABILITY TLV'; the sentence is corrected.
RA-0573RFC 3036 3.5.1.2.2Cross-reference names a section that does not exist.ResolvedRFC 5036 (obsoletes RFC 3036) removes the sentence.
RA-0053RFC 6790 5.2The Entropy Label Capability attribute is described only as "of value 28";ResolvedRFC 7447 (updates RFC 6790) deprecates the BGP Entropy Label Capability attribute.
RA-0621RFC 4447 5.3.3, 1Ingress/egress roles of PE1 and PE2 in 5.3.3 contradict Section 1.Re-targetedRFC 8077 (obsoletes RFC 4447) repeats the text in Section 6.2.3; recorded as RA-1073.
RA-0623RFC 4447 6.1Section 6.1 never says which PW types "these PWs" are;Re-targetedRFC 8077 (obsoletes RFC 4447) repeats the text in Section 7.1; recorded as RA-1074.
RA-0625RFC 4447 5.3.2PW info length: unclear whether sub-element Type and Length octets are counted.Re-targetedRFC 8077 (obsoletes RFC 4447) repeats the text in Section 6.2.2; recorded as RA-1075.
RA-0626RFC 4447 6.3A Generalized PWid FEC (0x81) has no PW ID field;Re-targetedRFC 8077 (obsoletes RFC 4447) repeats the text in Section 6.5; recorded as RA-1076.
RA-0244RFC 6073 14.5, 7.4.1Length of sub-TLV 0x06 is 14 octets per Section 7.4.1, not 12.ResolvedRFC 7267 Section 6 (updates RFC 6073) sets the length of sub-TLV 0x06 to 14.
RA-0661RFC 3471 12Value 51 (L2SC) is defined in Section 3.1.1 but missing from the IANA list.ResolvedRFC 7074 Section 5 (updates RFC 3471) revises the Switching Types registry, which lists 51 Layer-2 Switch Capable (L2SC); the omission remains only in the text of RFC 3471 Section 12.
RA-0828RFC 1122 4.2.5, 4.2.3.2TCP summary: delayed-ACK rule marked MUST (text SHOULD); two rows cite nonexistent 4.2.3.14.ResolvedRFC 9293 (which obsoletes the TCP material of RFC 1122): the delayed-ACK rule is a SHOULD in both Section 3.8.6.3 and the Appendix B summary, and the summary cites existing sections.
RA-0831RFC 1122 4.2.2.6TCPhdrsize includes TCP options, so whether the MSS a peer advertises already allows for options (and whether the advertised value should be reduced for options) is read both ways;ResolvedRFC 9293 Section 3.7.1 (which obsoletes the TCP material of RFC 1122) and RFC 6691 Section 2: the MSS option value ignores IP and TCP options, and the sender reduces the data length for the options it sends.
RA-1272RFC 1141 DescriptionThe incremental update equation gives -0 (0xFFFF) instead of +0; corrected by RFC 1624 Eqn. 3.ResolvedRFC 1624 Section 3 (updates RFC 1141) gives the corrected incremental update (Eqn. 3), which avoids the 0x0000 / 0xFFFF error.
RA-0837RFC 1858 3.2.1, 4.2Security gap: The document presents "IF FO=1 and PROTOCOL=TCP then DROP PACKET" as the general algorithm and calls the direct TMIN test on zero-offset fragments unnecessary.ResolvedRFC 3128 Section 3 (updates RFC 1858) requires the test on zero-offset fragments (transport length below the minimum) in addition to dropping fragments with offset 1.
RA-0843RFC 2253 3Grammar rejects one-letter attribute type names used in the document's own examples.ResolvedRFC 4514 (obsoletes RFC 2253), Section 3 and Appendix B: the attribute type uses <descr> from RFC 4512, which allows short names of length 1.
RA-0844RFC 2253 2.4, 3Section 2.4 lets a generator emit "=" anywhere and "#" anywhere except at the start of a value without escaping, but the grammar's stringchar excludes every "special", including "=" and "#", so such output is not parseable by a strict parser built from Section 3.ResolvedRFC 4514 (obsoletes RFC 2253): the string grammar admits '=' and '#' inside a value, only a leading '#' is escaped (Section 2.4), and the LDAPv2-only forms are removed.
RA-0854RFC 3174 7.2The value 1 equals shaNull in the enumeration of sha1.h, so the reported error is wrong. The shift needs a (uint32_t) cast on each byte.ResolvedRFC 6234 (updates RFC 3174) replaces the sample code (Section 8).
RA-0904RFC 6125 6.2.1, 1.8DNS-ID rule calls a configured name a "derived domain"; Section 1.8 calls it a "delegated domain".ResolvedRFC 9525 (obsoletes RFC 6125) no longer uses 'derived domain' or 'delegated domain'; its Section 6 rules replace this text.
RA-0905RFC 6125 6.4.3, 7.2Partial-label wildcards may be matched, but the rules do not say whether '' may match the empty string (does "baz" match "baz"?), whether more than one '' in a label is allowed, or whether a wildcard immediately above a public suffix (".com", "*.co.uk") may be matched.ResolvedRFC 9525 (obsoletes RFC 6125) allows the wildcard only as the complete left-most label (Section 6.3), so partial-label matching no longer arises.
RA-0906RFC 6125 10.2Wrong recommendation number in the X.520 reference.ResolvedRFC 9525 (obsoletes RFC 6125) does not carry this reference.
RA-0921RFC 7525 6.5Revocation list item 3 duplicates item 2.ResolvedRFC 9325 (obsoletes RFC 7525) replaces the revocation guidance (Section 7.5); the list is not carried over.
RA-0922RFC 7525 4.4, 4.3, 3.4Count of issues and "as required by Section 4.2" wrong; 1024-bit DHE option conflicts with 4.3.ResolvedRFC 9325 (obsoletes RFC 7525) rewrites the Diffie-Hellman and cipher-suite guidance; the miscounted list and the 1024-bit option are not carried over.
RA-0421RFC 8200 4, 4.3, 4.2Section 4 (with its NOTE) makes Hop-by-Hop processing at transit nodes optional and configuration-driven, while Section 4.3 still describes the header as information for "every node".ResolvedRFC 9673 (updates RFC 8200), Sections 5.1 and 5.2: a router that does not process the Hop-by-Hop Options header MUST forward the packet normally and MUST NOT drop it solely because it carries the header; options it does not process are skipped as for action bits 00, and the 01, 10 and 11 actions become 'MAY discard, if so configured'. Not covered by RFC 9673: the 'every node' wording of RFC 8200 Section 4.3, and the same question for the other extension headers (erratum 5933). RFC 9673 itself raises new points (RA-1218 to RA-1221).
RA-0947RFC 8446 4.2.10"PSK cipher suite" is a TLS 1.2 concept that does not exist in TLS 1.3.ResolvedRFC 9846 (obsoletes RFC 8446), Section 4.3.10: 'In order to accept early data, the server MUST have selected the first key offered'; the PSK cipher-suite wording is gone.
RA-0948RFC 8446 4.4.2.3Wrong cross-reference for acceptable certificate signature algorithms.ResolvedRFC 9846 (obsoletes RFC 8446) removes the sentence; Section 4.5.1.2 refers to Section 4.3.3 (Signature Algorithms) for acceptable certificate signature algorithms.

Most significant findings

Contradictions and errors with interoperability impact, whether or not an erratum exists:

  • RA-0077 RFC 8231 8.5 (Error-Type 19 value 1, Error-Type 20 value 1): The IANA text for PCErr 19/1 and 20/1 puts an LSP object in a message whose grammar has no place for it (verified errata 5970, 6231).
  • RA-0016 RFC 4724 4.2: "A route previously marked as stale MUST be deleted" on consecutive restarts is easy to misread; implementations keep or flush different sets of routes.
  • RA-0089 RFC 7761 4.4.2, 4.11: The RP's Keepalive Timer after a Register-Stop differs between the pseudocode and the text by 25 s with default timers (verified erratum 5342).
  • RA-0037 RFC 5305 3, 4: Clamping path metrics at MAX_PATH_METRIC contradicts ISO 10589's "unreachable above MaxPathMetric".
  • RA-0041 RFC 5310 3.3: Key preparation differs from RFC 2104 HMAC for keys longer than the digest but not longer than the block size, so such keys do not interoperate between implementations.
  • RA-0007 RFC 4271 5 (vs RFC 7606 5.1): Two encoding rules for path attribute order that a sender cannot both satisfy.
  • RA-0084 RFC 8664 4.3.1 vs 5.2.1: Even with erratum 6753, the NT field is "ignored" in one section and validated in another.
  • RA-0093 RFC 5880 6.7.3, 6.7.4: Authentication sequence state updated before the digest check (verified errata 7082, 7083): a security gap in implementations that follow the original text.
  • RA-0071 RFC 4875 8.2: Two paragraphs give different RESV_CONFIRM rules for a merging transit LSR (erratum 2485, held).
  • RA-0036 RFC 5120 7.1: Every multi-topology router is required to be in MT #0, which excludes routers that run only another topology (for example IPv6 only, MT #2).
  • RA-0105 RFC 4861 6.2.1: The default MinRtrAdvInterval violates the MUST in the same definition for small MaxRtrAdvInterval (verified erratum 3154).
  • RA-0133 RFC 8538 4.1, 9: The mandatory stale-route timer has no defined start or restart condition, so repeated resets can keep stale routes indefinitely (security).
  • RA-0145 RFC 9494 4.2: The LLGR consecutive-restart rule overrides RFC 4724 4.2 without saying so.
  • RA-0120 RFC 7311 3.4.3, 3.2: Capping the AIGP value at the maximum 64-bit value produces a value that receivers must discard.
  • RA-0184 RFC 9350 13.1 vs 8: Saturating overflowing flex-algorithm metrics makes prefixes unreachable downstream, unlike the clamp of RFC 5305.
  • RA-0232 RFC 8320 4.1: The S-bit values for advertise and withdraw are swapped.
  • RA-0290 RFC 5441 12, 15.3: The IANA section gives bit 4 for a flag that the body and the registry define as bit 28.
  • RA-0222 RFC 7349 6.1, 2.3: TLV Length values omit the 8-octet Cryptographic Sequence Number.
  • RA-0216 RFC 6389 6, 9: The LAN upstream hash differs from the RFC 6388 procedure it claims to reuse.
  • RA-0287 RFC 8169 3.1: PTP sub-TLV Length, field sizes and figure disagree.
  • RA-0238 RFC 4448 4.6: "source MAC address" where the destination MAC address is meant.
  • RA-0261 RFC 2961 4.5: The published wrap-safe identifier comparison is not wrap-safe in C.
  • RA-0934 RFC 8032 6: The example code does not reduce x^2 modulo p before testing for zero, so a point is decoded wrongly; confirmed by running the code.
  • RA-0868 RFC 4862 5.4, 5.1: The list of Duplicate Address Detection exceptions restates the rule at a different requirement level, leaving unclear whether every address must be tested.
  • RA-0762 RFC 4610 3, 4, 5.1: Register copying among Anycast-RP members is not described for a source directly connected to a member that is also the DR.

Method and limits

Scope. 449 RFC texts, grouped into nine areas. The texts were taken as published (plain-text RFCs); errata were not applied to them. A few related texts (IANA registries for PCEP, RSVP and RSVP-TE, one Internet-Draft and NIST SP 800-38D) were used as references only and are not analysed.

Automated checks, all 449 RFCs. Every text was scanned by script for: references to sections that do not exist in the same document; mixed-case or non-RFC 2119 keyword forms ("MAY NOT", "MUST not", "SHOULD not"); leftover placeholders ("TBD", "TBA", "XXX"); and packet diagrams whose field boundaries do not fall on bit boundaries. Every hit was read in context; most were false positives (references to other documents split across lines, IANA wording, bit-ruler artefacts) and were dismissed. Confirmed ones are findings. Mixed-case or non-keyword forms occur in 23 RFCs (RFC 1191, 1812, 2212, 3212, 3473, 3479, 3719, 3787, 4090, 4105, 4271, 4446, 4447, 4448, 4656, 4875, 5130, 5305, 5308, 5357, 8338, 8439, 9350); they are listed once (RFC 1191) unless the case changes the meaning, as with "MAY NOT" in RFC 4271.

First pass. The protocol cores and their most-used extensions (56 RFCs) were read in the sections where implementers have to make choices: state machines, error handling, timers and constants, encodings and their figures, IANA tables, and the interaction with the RFCs they update or are updated by. Findings RA-0001 to RA-0110 come from this pass.

Second pass. The RFCs the first pass had only scanned were read by four reviewers working in parallel on separate lists, with the same rules: every normative section of a long RFC (all sections with MUST or SHOULD, state machines, encodings, timers, error handling, IANA and security considerations), and the whole text of a short one. Findings RA-0111 to RA-0423 come from this pass.

Third pass. Every RFC that the first two passes had read only in part, read through, lightly or by automated checks alone was then read in depth by four reviewers on separate lists, leaving 40 core specifications that had so far been read only in the sections where implementers make choices. Findings RA-0424 to RA-0979 come from this pass. For the cryptographic specifications, the published test vectors of RFC 7748, RFC 8017, RFC 8032 and RFC 8439 were recomputed with independent code, and the example code of RFC 8032 Section 6 was run to confirm the defects reported against it.

Fourth pass. Those 40 core specifications were then read in full, every section, by four reviewers on separate lists. A later check of the reading records showed that 39 RFCs marked "deep" in the second pass had been read only in part; they, and five RFCs whose record named no sections, were then read again in full by four reviewers (findings RA-1318 onwards), so that all 449 RFCs have been read at the "deep" level (see Coverage). Findings RA-0980 to RA-1194 come from this pass.

Added texts. Five RFCs added to the set later (RFC 4023, RFC 6310, RFC 6478, RFC 7771 and RFC 9673) were read in full, every section, with the same method and checked against the same errata database; findings RA-1195 to RA-1222 come from this reading.

Updating RFCs. Every finding was then checked against the RFCs in the set that update or obsolete the RFC it is about (from the "Updates:" and "Obsoletes:" headers of all texts in the set, and the "Updated by" / "Obsoleted by" data on the RFC Editor errata pages). Findings that an updating RFC settles are listed under Resolved by later RFCs and are not counted as open; findings whose text a successor repeats, or that an updating RFC changes without settling, stay open with a "Later RFCs" note. Twenty-seven updating or obsoleting RFCs that this check found missing were then added to the set and read in full by three reviewers with the same method (findings RA-1223 to RA-1317); the check was repeated over all 449 texts. Ten further updating RFCs identified from the RFC index were then added and read in full. Updating RFCs that are still not in the set were not checked. Finally, the status, obsoletes / obsoleted-by and updates / updated-by data of every RFC were taken from the RFC Editor's RFC index and shown in each RFC's header line below; the check against later RFCs was repeated with that data. Proposed errata against an RFC that is obsoleted or Historic carry a status note, since such reports may be held or rejected for that reason.

Duplicates. Where more than one pass produced findings for the same RFC, records with the same section were compared by quote and issue. Nine RFCs had findings from the first two passes, 28 had findings from the third pass and an earlier one, and the 40 RFCs of the fourth pass all had earlier findings; no record duplicated another, so all were kept. The ids are stable across passes.

Errata. Every finding was matched against the RFC Editor's complete errata database (8163 reports, retrieved 2026-11-09; 191 of the 449 RFCs have at least one report). For each finding, the reports on the same RFC were compared by section and by the quoted text, the corrected text and the notes; candidate pairs were then judged by hand. A finding either matches one or more reports (cited by id, status and type), is related to a report that does not cover its point (cited as related), or has no report on the point. Rejected reports are cited when they raised the same question; the verifier's notes are taken into account. Drafted errata that duplicate an existing report are no longer proposed; the summary counts them. Proposed errata are new reports in the RFC Editor's format; none has been filed, and several are clarifications that would normally be "Held for Document Update".

Limits. Quotes are kept to one or two lines and may be abridged with "..."; line breaks are removed. Findings come from reading, not from testing implementations. "Ambiguity" means the text supports more than one reasonable reading, not that implementations are known to differ, unless the issue says so. No finding for an RFC means that nothing was found at the depth stated, not that the RFC is free of problems.

BGP, L3VPN, MVPN and BGP-LS

73 RFCs in this area (73 deep); 183 findings, 62 of them proposed errata.

RFC 1997: BGP Communities Attribute

Depth: deep. Errata: 3 errata: 2 held, 1 rejected. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 7606, RFC 8642.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-0424COMMUNITIES attribute"The community attribute values ranging from 0x0000000 through 0x0000FFFF and 0xFFFF0000 through 0xFFFFFFFF are hereby reserved.""0x0000000" has seven hex digits (0x00000000 is meant). The opening sentence of the section is garbled ("This document creates the COMMUNITIES path attribute is an optional transitive attribute"), and NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED says "peers in other members autonomous systems".editorialerratum 3890 (Held for Document Update), editorial
RA-0425Aggregation"If a range of routes is to be aggregated and the resultant aggregates attribute section does not carry the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute, then the resulting aggregate should have a COMMUNITIES path attribute which contains all communities from all of the aggregated routes."The rule says nothing about the case where the aggregate does carry ATOMIC_AGGREGATE, and copying "all communities" includes the well-known NO_EXPORT / NO_ADVERTISE / NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED of any single component, which then restricts the whole aggregate; whether that is intended is not stated. The document also gives no handling for an attribute whose length is not a multiple of 4 (filled later by RFC 7606 7.8).ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point

RA-04273"The value of the Length of Next Hop Network Address field on a MP_REACH_NLRI attribute shall be set to 16, when only a global address is present, or 32 if a link-local address is also included in the Next Hop field."Only the sender is specified. The document does not say what a receiver does with other lengths, with a 16-octet next hop that is itself link-local, with a 32-octet field whose second address is not link-local (or whose first is), or with a link-local address learned from a peer that does not share the subnet. It also says a speaker advertising to an internal peer "may" remove the link-local address, which reads as optional even in the case where the "if and only if" rule just above requires it to be kept. Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 7313.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum

RA-00075 (vs RFC 7606 5.1)"The sender of an UPDATE message SHOULD order path attributes within the UPDATE message in ascending order of attribute type."RFC 7606 5.1 (which updates RFC 4271) says MP_REACH_NLRI / MP_UNREACH_NLRI (types 14 / 15) "SHALL be encoded as the very first path attribute", which breaks ascending order for every UPDATE that carries ORIGIN (1), AS_PATH (2) and so on. RA-00088.2.2 (OpenSent, event 25)"In response to any other event (Events 9, 11-13, 20, 25-28), the local system: - sends the NOTIFICATION with the Error Code Finite State Machine Error,"Taken literally, a received NOTIFICATION (event 25) in some states is answered with a NOTIFICATION, against sections 6 and 6.4 and RFC 6608.contradictionnone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point
RA-00099.2.2.2"Routes that have different MULTI_EXIT_DISC attributes SHALL NOT be aggregated."The aggregation rules cover only ORIGIN, AS_PATH, NEXT_HOP, MED, ATOMIC_AGGREGATE and AGGREGATOR; nothing says what to do with communities, LOCAL_PREF or later attributes, or which MED to keep when aggregation is forced by configuration. Later RFCs: RFC 9774 (updates RFC 4271) forbids AS_SET in new aggregates, which changes the AS_PATH rule; the other gaps remain.ambiguitynone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point
RA-00109.1.2.1"BGP speakers SHOULD exclude unresolvable routes from the Phase 2 decision.""Resolvable" is defined recursively against the Routing Table without saying whether BGP routes may resolve BGP next hops or what happens when the resolving route changes.ambiguitynone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point
RA-00116.3"If the NEXT_HOP attribute is semantically incorrect, the error SHOULD be logged, and the route SHOULD be ignored.""Ignored" does not say whether a previously stored path for the same prefix from that peer is kept or removed.ambiguitynone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point
RA-09809.1.2, 9.1.2.1"If the NEXT_HOP attribute of a BGP route depicts an address that is not resolvable ... the BGP route MUST be excluded from the Phase 2 decision function. / BGP speakers SHOULD exclude unresolvable routes from the Phase 2 decision."Section 9.1.2 makes the exclusion of routes with unresolvable NEXT_HOPs a MUST; Section 9.1.2.1, which defines resolvability and introduces itself with "As indicated in Section 9.1.2", restates it as a SHOULD. Implementations that do not resolve next hops (route reflectors and route servers off the forwarding path) rely on the SHOULD; the MUST forbids them.contradictionnone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09816.5, 4.2, 8.2.2"If a system does not receive successive KEEPALIVE, UPDATE, and/or NOTIFICATION messages within the period specified in the Hold Time field of the OPEN message"Section 4.2 requires the Hold Timer to use the smaller of the configured and received Hold Time and to measure the time between "successive KEEPALIVE and/or UPDATE messages"; Section 6.5 measures the period "specified in the Hold Time field of the OPEN message" (the peer's proposal, not the negotiated value) and adds NOTIFICATION to the messages that count. The FSM of 8.2.2 restarts the HoldTimer only on KeepAliveMsg and UpdateMsg in Established (Events 26 and 27), and a received NOTIFICATION closes the connection anyway. Messages from later extensions (ROUTE-REFRESH, RFC 2918) are covered by none of the three texts.contradictionnone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09828.1.5, 8.2.2"Event 19: BGPOpen ... Optional Attribute Status: 1) The DelayOpen optional attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE. 2) The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD not be running."With DelayOpen set to TRUE, the FSM sends its OPEN when the DelayOpenTimer expires (Connect and Active states, Event 12) and moves to OpenSent, where the peer's OPEN is then processed as Event 19 ("resets the DelayOpenTimer to zero"). Event 19 therefore occurs routinely with DelayOpen TRUE, against its stated attribute status; the condition that distinguishes Event 19 from Event 20 is only whether the DelayOpenTimer is running. "SHOULD not" is also written in mixed case.contradictionnone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09836.3"either the IP address in the NEXT_HOP MUST be the sender's IP address that is used to establish the BGP connection, or the interface associated with the NEXT_HOP IP address MUST share a common subnet with the receiving BGP speaker."The second alternative is garbled: an IP address has no "associated interface" from the receiver's point of view, and a subnet is shared with an interface, not with a "speaker". The intended rule appears to be that the NEXT_HOP address lies on a subnet directly attached to the receiving speaker (the one the session runs over, or any attached subnet?). It is also unstated whether the check applies to single-hop EBGP sessions over loopbacks or to route-server clients, and the receiver action (route "SHOULD be ignored") leaves a single-hop EBGP route with an off-subnet third-party NEXT_HOP unusable but silently present in nobody's table.ambiguitynone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09844.3, 5.1.2, 6.2, 8.2.2, 9.1.2.2, 9.2.1.1, Security Considerations"The path segment type is a 1-octet length field with the following values defined:"The segment type is not a length field; likewise "The path segment value field contains one or more AS numbers, each encoded as a 2-octet length field". Other slips not covered by errata: 5.1.2 "prepends its own AS number as the last element of the sequence (put it in the leftmost position ...)" (it becomes the first, leftmost element); 6.2 "Unsupported Optional Parameters" (subcode name is singular); OpenSent text "A CollisionDetectDump event occurs" (the event is OpenCollisionDump, Event 23); 9.1.2.2 e "If the NEXT_HOP hop for a route" and "for n = all routes in still under consideration"; 9.2.1.1 "the procedure describe in this section" and the garbled sentence "Any technique that ensures that the interval ... will be at least MinRouteAdvertisementIntervalTimer, and will also ensure that a constant upper bound on the interval is acceptable"; Security Considerations "each should key also be chosen" and "ACSII".editorialnone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09858.2.2 (Active state, Event 18)"If the local system receives a TcpConnectionFails event (Event 18), the local system: - restarts the ConnectRetryTimer (with the initial value), ... - changes its state to Idle."In Active state a TCP failure restarts the ConnectRetryTimer and then moves to Idle, where Event 9 (ConnectRetryTimer_Expires) is ignored ("Any other event (Events 9-12, 15-28) received in the Idle state does not cause change"). The restarted timer has no effect, so the text either intends to stay in Active (as the parallel OpenSent action "changes its state to Active" suggests) or the restart is superfluous. Implementations transcribing the table differ in whether the peer leaves Idle without a new start event.ambiguitynone: RFC has 21 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0007 (RFC 4271, Section 5 (vs RFC 7606 5.1); type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The sender of an UPDATE message SHOULD order path attributes
   within the UPDATE message in ascending order of attribute type.

Corrected Text
--------------
   The sender of an UPDATE message SHOULD order path attributes
   within the UPDATE message in ascending order of attribute type,
   except that the MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute, if
   present, is encoded first (see RFC 7606, Section 5.1).

Notes
-----
   RFC 7606 Section 5.1 (which updates this document) requires
   MP_REACH_NLRI
   MP_UNREACH_NLRI to be the very first path attribute, which
   conflicts with ascending order whenever lower-numbered attributes
   are present. Suggested as Held for Document Update for a future
   revision of RFC 4271.

Proposed erratum RA-0980 (RFC 4271, Section 9.1.2, 9.1.2.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   BGP speakers SHOULD exclude unresolvable routes from the Phase 2
   decision.

Corrected Text
--------------
   BGP speakers MUST exclude unresolvable routes from the Phase 2
   decision.

Notes
-----
   The two sections state the same requirement with different
   keywords. (Alternatively the MUST of Section 9.1.2 could become
   SHOULD; the working group should say which is intended. Deployed
   route reflectors and route servers commonly do not resolve next
   hops.)

Proposed erratum RA-0981 (RFC 4271, Section 6.5, 4.2, 8.2.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If a system does not receive successive KEEPALIVE, UPDATE, and/or
   NOTIFICATION messages within the period specified in the Hold
   Time field of the OPEN message, then the NOTIFICATION message
   with the Hold Timer Expired Error Code is sent and the BGP
   connection is closed.

Corrected Text
--------------
   If a system does not receive successive KEEPALIVE and/or UPDATE
   messages within the negotiated Hold Time (see Section 4.2), then
   the NOTIFICATION message with the Hold Timer Expired Error Code
   is sent and the BGP connection is closed.

Notes
-----
   Section 4.2 defines the Hold Timer as the smaller of the local
   and received Hold Time and counts KEEPALIVE and UPDATE messages;
   the FSM (Section 8.2.2, Events 26 and 27) agrees. Section 6.5
   refers to the Hold Time field of the received OPEN and includes
   NOTIFICATION.

Proposed erratum RA-0982 (RFC 4271, Section 8.1.5, 8.2.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   1) The DelayOpen optional attribute SHOULD be set to FALSE. 2)
   The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD not be running.

Corrected Text
--------------
   1) The DelayOpenTimer SHOULD NOT be running.

Notes
-----
   After DelayOpenTimer_Expires (Event 12) the local system sends
   its OPEN and enters OpenSent; the OPEN subsequently received is
   Event 19 even though DelayOpen is TRUE. Only the state of the
   DelayOpenTimer separates Event 19 from Event 20.

Proposed erratum RA-0983 (RFC 4271, Section 6.3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   or the interface associated with the NEXT_HOP IP address MUST
   share a common subnet with the receiving BGP speaker.

Corrected Text
--------------
   or the NEXT_HOP IP address MUST belong to a subnet that is
   directly connected to the receiving BGP speaker through the
   interface over which the BGP connection is established.

Notes
-----
   The text attributes an "interface" to the NEXT_HOP address and a
   "subnet" to the speaker. The intended condition is presumably
   that the NEXT_HOP is on a subnet the receiver shares with the
   sender (as for "first party" and "third party" NEXT_HOPs in
   Section 5.1.3).

Proposed erratum RA-0984 (RFC 4271, Section 4.3, 5.1.2, 6.2, 8.2.2, 9.1.2.2, 9.2.1.1, Security Considerations; type: Editorial):

Original Text
-------------
   The path segment type is a 1-octet length field with the
   following values defined:

Corrected Text
--------------
   The path segment type is a 1-octet field with the following
   values defined:

Notes
-----
   In Section 4.3 the segment type and the AS numbers are described
   as "length" fields; only the path segment length is a length. The
   remaining typographical errors listed do not change the protocol.

RA-09866, 13.1"a router in the backbone MUST NOT accept a labeled packet from any adjacent non-backbone device unless ... 1. the label at the top of the label stack was actually distributed by that backbone router to that non-backbone device"Section 13.1 restates the same rule differently: a labeled packet may be accepted if its top label "has a label value that the receiving system has distributed to a system beyond that neighbor". Section 6 (MUST) accepts only labels distributed to the adjacent device itself; 13.1 (should) also accepts labels distributed further away. Section 6 also has a second condition (the label makes the packet leave the backbone before lower labels or the IP header are inspected) that 13.1 folds into its condition 1 with "or". An implementer filtering labels per neighbour cannot satisfy both texts for multi-hop label distribution (for example inter-AS option b or carriers' carriers through an intermediate device).contradictionnone: RFC has 5 errata, none on this point
RA-09874.3.3, 4.3.5"Note that this technique will not work properly if some client PE has a VRF with an import Route Target that is not one of its export Route Targets."The second route-reflector partitioning method of 4.3.3 fails for exactly the topology 4.3.5 recommends for hub-and-spoke VPNs (spoke VRFs import "Hub" and export "Spoke"), but 4.3.5 does not refer back to this limitation, and 4.3.3 says Join and Prune "are also non-disruptive" with this procedure without that qualification. RA-09887, 8"Every CE whose site is not in a transit VPN can use the same ASN. Loop prevention is then left to the Site of Origin rule of Section 8, which is written with lower-case "must never be redistributed" while Section 7 makes the Site of Origin attribute optional ("it may assign a Site of Origin attribute").ambiguitynone: RFC has 5 errata, none on this point

RFC 4456: BGP Route Reflection: An Alternative to Full Mesh Internal BGP (IBGP)

Depth: deep. Errata: 2 errata: 1 held, 1 rejected. Status: Draft Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 1966, RFC 2796. Updated by: RFC 7606.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00148"When an RR reflects a route, it MUST prepend the local CLUSTER_ID to the CLUSTER_LIST."The RFC does not say what a receiver does with an IBGP route that carries ORIGINATOR_ID without CLUSTER_LIST, or CLUSTER_LIST without ORIGINATOR_ID (only a reflector could have added either). The erratum asking this was rejected as a question for the working group, so it stays open. RFC 7606 7.9 / 7.10 only cover malformed lengths.ambiguityerratum 3898 (Rejected), technical
RA-00155"The Non-Client peer must be fully meshed"Plural intended ("Non-Client peers").editorialerratum 3778 (Held for Document Update), editorial
RA-09915, 6"An RR reflects routes between these groups, and may reflect routes among client peers."Section 5 makes reflection among clients optional ("may"), while Section 6 says the RR "must do the following", including for a route from a Client peer: "Reflect to all the Non-Client peers and also to the Client peers." Implementations commonly offer a switch to disable client-to-client reflection (for clients that are fully meshed), which Section 5 allows and Section 6 forbids. Section 6 also does not say whether "all the Clients" includes the client the route was received from.contradictionnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-0991 (RFC 4456, Section 5, 6; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   2) A route from a Client peer: Reflect to all the Non-Client
   peers and also to the Client peers.

Corrected Text
--------------
   2) A route from a Client peer: Reflect to all the Non-Client
   peers and also to the other Client peers, unless reflection among
   clients has been disabled by configuration (e.g., because the
   clients are fully meshed).

Notes
-----
   Section 5 says an RR "may reflect routes among client peers";
   Section 6 lists it among the steps the RR "must" do. Disabling
   client-to-client reflection is common practice where clients are
   fully meshed.

RFC 4724: Graceful Restart Mechanism for BGP

Depth: deep. Errata: 3 errata: 1 verified, 2 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 4271. Updated by: RFC 8538.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00164.2"To deal with possible consecutive restarts, a route (from the peer) previously marked as stale MUST be deleted."The sentence means that when the session fails again before the peer re-advertised a route, routes still stale from the previous restart are deleted, not re-marked. "Consecutive restarts" is not defined (before End-of-RIB? within the Restart Time?).ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-00174.2, 5"See Section 8 for a description of this behavior in terms of the BGP finite state machine."Section 8 is the Security Considerations; the FSM changes are in section 5. Erratum 7915 (verified) adds that the RFC changes the RFC 4271 FSM and should have been marked "Updates: 4271".errorerratum 7915 (Verified), technical; erratum 4193 (Held for Document Update), editorial
RA-00184.2"To put an upper bound on the amount of time a router retains the stale routes, an implementation MAY support a (configurable) timer"Without that timer a peer that reconnects but never sends End-of-RIB keeps stale routes forever; the RFC sets no default.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-00197"Since with this proposal a new connection can cause an old one to be terminated, it might seem to open the door to denial of service"Security gap: Section 7 discusses only the new-connection case. An on-path attacker can send a forged NOTIFICATION making the peer retry without the GR capability (RFC 5492 fallback), silently disabling graceful restart. The RFC does not mention it.errorerratum 6217 (Held for Document Update), technical
RA-09924.2, 5""Acting accordingly" in this context means that the previous TCP session MUST be closed, and the new one retained. (4.2) / - changes its state to Connect. (5)"Section 4.2 requires the new connection to be retained, but the replacement Established-state text in Section 5 drops the old connection and moves the FSM to Connect after Event 16 / 17 has already been consumed. In RFC 4271 the Connect state only sends an OPEN on a further Event 16 / 17 and drops the connection when the ConnectRetryTimer (which Section 5 starts) expires, so the text does not say how the new, already established TCP connection is carried into OpenSent. Implementers must infer that the new connection is processed as if Event 16 / 17 had occurred in the Connect state. The same section also does not address the case where the old session's connection is the one in the other direction, which RFC 4271 6.8 collision handling would otherwise resolve in favour of the Established session.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09934, 4.2, 5"It is noted that the normal BGP procedures MUST be followed when the TCP session terminates due to the sending or receiving of a BGP NOTIFICATION message."Section 4.2 applies the Receiving Speaker procedures whenever the speaker "detects termination of the TCP session", but Section 5 changes only Event 18 (TcpConnectionFails) and the new-connection case. HoldTimer_Expires (Event 10) still sends a NOTIFICATION in RFC 4271 and, by Section 4, therefore follows the normal procedures, so a peer whose restart is detected only by hold-timer expiry loses all its routes. The suggested default "Restart Time ... less than or equal to the HOLDTIME" makes this the expected case for restarts that leave no TCP reset. RFC 8538 later extends Graceful Restart to hold-timer expiry, but only where the N bit is exchanged.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-09943, 4.1, 4.2"To re-establish the session with its peer, the Restarting Speaker MUST set the "Restart State" bit in the Graceful Restart Capability of the OPEN message."The RFC does not say for how long after a restart the R bit stays set. A restarting speaker whose session to one peer fails again after selection deferral has ended (or after End-of-RIB) would, read literally, keep setting R, so the peer would not wait for its End-of-RIB (Section 3: "its peer MUST NOT wait for the End-of-RIB marker") although no deadlock is possible any more; conversely, clearing R too early can cause the deadlock R exists to avoid.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0016 (RFC 4724, Section 4.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   To deal with possible consecutive restarts, a route (from the
   peer) previously marked as stale MUST be deleted.

Corrected Text
--------------
   To deal with possible consecutive restarts, a route (from the
   peer) that is still marked as stale from a previous restart (that
   is, it has not been re-advertised by the peer since that restart)
   MUST be deleted when the TCP session terminates again.

Notes
-----
   Clarification only. The original sentence does not say when the
   deletion happens or which routes are meant; it is easily read as
   "delete all stale routes" or as not applying until the Restart
   Time expires.

Proposed erratum RA-0992 (RFC 4724, Section 4.2, 5; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   - starts the ConnectRetryTimer with the initial value, and -
   changes its state to Connect.

Corrected Text
--------------
   - processes the new TCP connection as if Event 16 or Event 17 had
   occurred in the Connect state (that is, sends an OPEN message,
   sets the HoldTimer to a large value and changes its state to
   OpenSent).

Notes
-----
   Section 4.2 says the previous TCP session is closed "and the new
   one retained". The replacement text in Section 5 ends in the
   Connect state and starts the ConnectRetryTimer, but in RFC 4271
   the Connect state proceeds only on a further Event 16/17, which
   has already occurred. The intended handling of the new connection
   should be stated.

Depth: deep. Errata: 5 errata: 1 verified, 4 held. Status: Draft Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 2858. Updated by: RFC 7606.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00204"(MP_UNREACH_NLRI, AFI:) identifies the set of Network Layer protocols to which the address carried in the Next Hop field must belong"MP_UNREACH_NLRI has no Next Hop field; the AFI/SAFI only qualify the withdrawn routes. Copy-and-paste from section 3.errorerratum 1573 (Verified), technical

RA-00237, 8"... the speaker MUST delete all the BGP routes received from that neighbor whose AFI/SAFI is the same as the one carried in the incorrect ... attribute."Silent on an MP attribute for a family that was never negotiated, and offers two incompatible reactions (reset or "AFI/SAFI disable") for a malformed one. RA-09969"SAFI values 5 through 63 are to be assigned by IANA ... / SAFI values 67 through 127 are to be assigned by IANA, using the "First Come First Served" policy"The registration rules leave SAFI 4 and SAFI 64 to 66 in no range: they were already in use (labelled unicast, tunnel, VPLS, MDT) but are neither listed as assigned nor reserved, so the text does not define their status. RFC 5004: Avoid BGP Best Path Transitions from One External to Another

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-04403, 5"if neither Path A nor Path B is eliminated by the route selection algorithm prior to Step f) -- BGP identifier comparison (Section 9.1.2.2, [BGP]) -- we propose that the existing best path (Path A) be kept as the best path"The rule is stated for a pair (current best A, challenger B) and is not a total order over all candidate paths: it does not say what happens when the current best is withdrawn or loses at an earlier step and several external paths then tie up to step f, nor how it combines with deterministic-MED grouping. Implementations commonly substitute "prefer the oldest external path", which is not the same rule: an older path that was not best (it lost at an earlier step that has since changed) can displace the current best, a transition the RFC is meant to avoid. The exemption for "peers with an identical BGP identifier" (parallel sessions) must also be applied for the outcome to match.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 5492: Capabilities Advertisement with BGP-4

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 rejected. Status: Draft Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 3392. Updated by: RFC 8810.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00243"In this case, the speaker SHOULD attempt to re-establish a BGP connection with the peer without sending to the peer the Capabilities Optional Parameter."A speaker that needs capabilities (for example to exchange only IPv6 routes, or four-octet AS numbers) gains nothing from a session without them, and the fallback is the downgrade path an attacker can trigger with a forged NOTIFICATION (see RFC 4724). The erratum asking to make the retry a local choice was rejected because the SHOULD already allows it; the text gives no guidance on when not to retry.ambiguityerratum 3882 (Rejected), technical
RA-04453"The decision to send the message and terminate the peering is local to the speaker. If terminated, such peering SHOULD NOT be re-established automatically."It is not stated which speaker the SHOULD NOT applies to. The terminating speaker can refrain from connecting, but the receiver of the Unsupported Capability NOTIFICATION normally runs its automatic restart (RFC 4271 8.1.1 IdleHoldTimer, DampPeerOscillations) and will keep trying; whether the receiver is also expected to stop, and what "automatically" means when the cause is fixed by configuration on either side, is not defined. The result is either a permanently down session or repeated rejected attempts. Errata: Rejected erratum 3882 concerned whether to retry at all; it does not say which speaker the SHOULD NOT binds.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point (related: erratum 3882 (Rejected), technical); proposed erratum below

RFC 6368: Internal BGP as the Provider/Customer Edge Protocol for BGP/MPLS IP Virtual Private Networks (VPNs)

Depth: deep. Errata: 2 errata: 2 verified. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 7606, RFC 9494.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01185"If its Partial flag is set and its Neighbor-Complete flag is clear, the UPDATE is treated as a route withdraw as discussed in [OPT-TRANS-BGP]."The "Neighbor-Complete flag" is defined only in an expired Internet-Draft cited informatively ([OPT-TRANS-BGP]), so the rule cannot be applied from the published RFCs. RFC 7606 Section 7.16 replaces the paragraph with plain treat-as-withdraw and removes the reference; RFC 6368 readers need that update to implement the section. The malformation list (length below 4, MP_REACH / MP_UNREACH inside, malformed inner attributes) is unchanged.errornone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-13186, 4"The approach taken by this document is to rewrite the NEXT_HOP attribute at the VRF import/export boundary. PE routers take into account the PE-PE IGP distance calculated by the customer network IGP, when selecting between routes advertised from different PEs."The PE-PE distance is computed by the service provider's IGP; the customer network IGP does not run between PEs and does not know PE addresses. Section 4 says so: the IGP metric of a PE-received route "SHOULD be the metric to the remote PE address, expressed in terms of the service provider metric domain". This is the same customer/provider slip that verified errata 4309 (Section 7) and 7834 (Section 5) correct elsewhere in the document. Section 4 also states that "customer network IGP metrics SHOULD always be considered higher ... than local site metrics", where the comparison intended is between PE-received routes (provider metrics) and routes from local CEs (local site metrics).errornone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-13195, 3, 9"In other words, the BGP path attributes are "pushed" into this attribute, which operates as a stack, when the route is received by the VPN and "popped" when the route is advertised in the PE-to-CE direction."The attribute is described as a stack, but the document never says what happens when a route received from a CE already carries an ATTR_SET (for example a CE that is itself a PE of a carrier's-carrier or nested VPN): whether the received ATTR_SET is pushed inside the new one (nesting, with a pop restoring it), replaced, or treated as malformed. ATTR_SET may contain "any BGP attribute that can occur in a BGP UPDATE message" except MP_REACH / MP_UNREACH, so nesting is allowed by the encoding, and no depth or size limit is given (Section 9 only says implementations "must consider the issues of input validation and resource management"). The malformed test "the included attributes are malformed themselves" then applies recursively without bound.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-1318 (RFC 6368, Section 6, 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   PE routers take into account the PE-PE IGP distance calculated by
   the customer network IGP, when selecting between routes
   advertised from different PEs.

Corrected Text
--------------
   PE routers take into account the PE-PE IGP distance calculated by
   the provider network IGP, when selecting between routes
   advertised from different PEs.

Notes
-----
   Section 4 states that the metric of a PE-received route is the
   metric to the remote PE "expressed in terms of the service
   provider metric domain". The customer IGP has no knowledge of
   PE-PE distances. Errata 4309 and 7834 correct the same
   customer/provider confusion in Sections 7 and 5.

RFC 6793: BGP Support for Four-Octet Autonomous System (AS) Number Space

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 4893. Updates: RFC 4271.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00258"If the BGP4-MIB [RFC4273] is supported, there are no additional manageability concerns that arise from the use of four-octet AS numbers"RFC 4273 types AS numbers as Integer32 (0..65535), so it cannot carry four-octet AS numbers.errorerratum 4538 (Held for Document Update), technical
RA-09973, 4.1"it MUST use the AS number encoded in the Capability Value field ... in lieu of the "My Autonomous System" field of the OPEN message."Section 3 says the My Autonomous System field carries AS_TRANS "if and only if the speaker does not have a (globally unique) two-octet AS number", which implies it otherwise equals the capability's AS. Neither section says what a receiver does when the two disagree (My Autonomous System neither AS_TRANS nor equal to the capability value, or AS_TRANS with a mappable capability value), nor what to do with a capability whose length is not 4. One implementation silently uses the capability value; another rejects the OPEN (Bad Peer AS); a third uses whichever matches its configuration.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09984.2.3"taking as many AS numbers and path segments as necessary from the leading part of the AS_PATH attribute, and then prepending them to the AS4_PATH"The counts are made "using the method specified in Section 9.1.2.2 of [RFC4271]", where an AS_SET counts as one whatever its size, but the construction step then speaks of taking "AS numbers". When the boundary falls in or on a leading AS_SET, it is not said whether the whole set is taken (as one counted unit) or some of its members, and whether a partially needed AS_SET is taken at all; the merged path then differs between implementations in length and in its loop-detection content.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-09994.2.2, 6"The NEW BGP speaker MUST also send the AS path information in the AS4_PATH attribute ... except for the case where all of the AS path information is composed of mappable four-octet AS numbers only."The exception is defined over all of the AS path information, while the AS4_PATH excludes confederation segments. When the only non-mappable AS numbers are in AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE / AS_CONFED_SET segments (to an OLD confederation peer), the MUST yields an AS4_PATH with no segments, which Section 6 declares malformed ("less than 6"). The exception should be stated over the path information outside confederation segments. Section 7 calls such a configuration a misconfiguration, but the encoding rule still has to be well defined.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-0997 (RFC 6793, Section 3, 4.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   When a NEW BGP speaker processes an OPEN message from another NEW
   BGP speaker, it MUST use the AS number encoded in the Capability
   Value field of the "support for four-octet AS number capability"
   in lieu of the "My Autonomous System" field of the OPEN message.

Corrected Text
--------------
   When a NEW BGP speaker processes an OPEN message from another NEW
   BGP speaker, it MUST use the AS number encoded in the Capability
   Value field of the "support for four-octet AS number capability"
   in lieu of the "My Autonomous System" field of the OPEN message.
   If the "My Autonomous System" field is neither AS_TRANS nor equal
   to the AS number in the Capability Value field, the speaker [MUST
   reject the OPEN with Bad Peer AS | SHOULD log the inconsistency
   and use the capability value].

Notes
-----
   Section 3 defines when My Autonomous System is AS_TRANS, implying
   it otherwise equals the capability value, but no receiver
   behaviour is given for an inconsistent pair, or for a capability
   length other than 4. Implementations differ (accept the
   capability value vs. reject the OPEN).

RA-04515.1.1, 5.2.10"0x80-0x8F Experimental Use (see RFC 3692) / 0x0A Layer2 Info Extended Community"Type 0x80 lies in the range reserved for "Experimental Use (see RFC 3692)", and RFC 3692 says such values are not to be shipped in products or relied on for interoperability; yet 5.2.10 creates a permanent First Come First Served sub-type registry under that Type and records Flow Specification actions and the Layer2 Info community, which are deployed. A reader cannot tell whether 0x80 values are experimental (may collide, not to be relied on) or ordinary assignments. The note about RFC 5575 addresses only the transitive / non-transitive mismatch of traffic-rate, not this one. In addition, the IPv6-Address-Specific registries (5.3) use a single FCFS range 0x00-0xFF for the second octet, unlike the 0x00-0xBF / 0xC0-0xFF split that Section 2 gives "each" Sub-Type registry, and the Four-Octet registry names sub-type 0x10 "Cisco VPN Identifier" where the other registries say "Cisco VPN-Distinguisher". Later RFCs: RFC 9184 Section 2 (updates RFC 7153) moves types 0x80 to 0x82 to First Come First Served and drops 'Experimental Use' from the sub-type registry names, which settles the main point; the IPv6-Address-Specific registry ranges and the naming points are not addressed.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata

RFC 7311: The Accumulated IGP Metric Attribute for BGP

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01203.4.3, 3.2"In all the computations discussed in this section, the AIGP value MUST be capped at its maximum unsigned value 0xffffffffffffffff."Section 3.2 says that an AIGP attribute whose first AIGP TLV "contains the maximum value 0xffffffffffffffff ... SHOULD be considered to be malformed and SHOULD be discarded". A speaker that caps an overflowing sum as 3.4.3 requires therefore sends a value that every compliant receiver discards, so the route silently loses its AIGP attribute one hop later and, under Section 4.1, is then removed from consideration whenever another route still carries one. Capping at 0xfffffffffffffffe, or withdrawing the attribute, would avoid this; the text does not say which.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-01213.4.3"If D is above a configurable threshold, set the AIGP TLV value to Xattr+D. If D is below a configurable threshold, set the AIGP TLV value to Xattr."D equal to the threshold is not covered. In the non-recursive case the same section requires that "A MUST be increased by a non-zero amount", while here a D below the threshold leaves the value unchanged after a next-hop change; the two rules disagree on whether a next-hop change may leave the AIGP value as received.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-13203.4.3"If the route has an AIGP attribute without an AIGP TLV, then the AIGP attribute MAY be passed along unchanged. / 8. Go to step 4."Step 6 has two cases. Its first case ("does NOT have an AIGP attribute") exits; its second case (the route to XNH has an AIGP attribute that holds no AIGP TLV) neither exits nor changes XNH or Xattr. Step 7 does not apply (there is no AIGP TLV value Y), so step 8 returns to step 4 with the same XNH and the procedure never terminates. The second case also does not say which AIGP attribute is "passed along unchanged": that of the route being redistributed (value A, which would then not be increased although the next hop changed, against the non-zero increase required earlier in the section) or that of the route to XNH.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13214.1, 4.2"remove from consideration all routes that are not tied for the lowest value of A. / such that either: - the two routes have equal AIGP TLV values, or else - neither of the two routes has an AIGP attribute containing an AIGP TLV."After Section 4.1 the remaining routes are tied on A = AIGP TLV value + IGP distance to the next hop, not on the AIGP TLV value. Two routes with TLV values 10 and 20 and next-hop distances 20 and 10 survive 4.1 but meet neither condition of Section 4.2, so it is not defined whether the later "interior cost" tie breaker uses the AIGP-enhanced interior cost or the plain one for them. Section 4.1 also adds "the IGP distance from R to T's next hop" without saying what is used when that next hop is itself resolved through BGP (Section 4.2 defines a recursive cost for exactly that case), and the 64-bit cap of Section 3.4.3 ("In all the computations discussed in this section") does not cover the sum in 4.1, which can overflow.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13223, 3.2"When receiving a BGP Update message containing a malformed AIGP attribute, the attribute MUST be treated exactly as if it were an unrecognized non-transitive attribute."The document says what must not make an AIGP attribute malformed (several TLVs of one type, unknown types) and adds two cases that do (transitive bit set, maximum value), but never defines the structural errors: a TLV Length below 3, a TLV that runs past the end of the attribute, or an AIGP TLV (type 1) whose Length is not 11. Whether such an attribute is discarded, or the valid first AIGP TLV is still used, is left to the implementer.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-13233.4.3"If R1 does not change the next hop of the route, then R1 MUST NOT change the AIGP attribute value of the route. / Suppose R1 changes the next hop of the route from R2 to R1."Only two cases are covered: next hop unchanged, and next hop set to R1 itself. A next hop rewritten by policy to a third address (neither R2 nor R1, for example a route server or a policy "set next-hop") has no rule, although Section 3.4.1 forbids adding AIGP to a route "for which R does not set itself as the next hop". Whether the attribute must then be removed, kept unchanged or increased is not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0120 (RFC 7311, Section 3.4.3, 3.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   In all the computations discussed in this section, the AIGP value
   MUST be capped at its maximum unsigned value 0xffffffffffffffff.

Corrected Text
--------------
   In all the computations discussed in this section, the AIGP value
   MUST be capped at 0xfffffffffffffffe, one less than the maximum
   unsigned value, which Section 3.2 treats as malformed.

Notes
-----

Proposed erratum RA-1320 (RFC 7311, Section 3.4.3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   6.  If the route to XNH is a BGP-learned route that does NOT have
   an AIGP attribute, then exit this procedure and do not pass on
   any AIGP attribute.  If the route has an AIGP attribute without
   an AIGP TLV, then the AIGP attribute MAY be passed along
   unchanged.

Corrected Text
--------------
   6.  If the route to XNH is a BGP-learned route that does NOT have
   an AIGP attribute containing an AIGP TLV, then exit this
   procedure and do not pass on any AIGP TLV.  (If the route being
   redistributed has an AIGP attribute without an AIGP TLV, that
   attribute MAY be passed along unchanged.)

Notes
-----
   In the second case of step 6 the procedure has no exit: step 7
   needs a value Y, and step 8 returns to step 4 with XNH unchanged.
   The intended behaviour is presumably to stop accumulating, since
   a path with a gap must not carry an AIGP value (Section 1: "the
   AIGP attribute does not appear when there are 'gaps' along the
   path").

RA-10002"AFI/SAFI disable: Section 7 of [RFC4760] allows a BGP speaker ... to optionally "ignore all the subsequent routes with that AFI/SAFI received over that session"."RFC 4760 Section 7 first says the speaker "MUST delete all the BGP routes received from that neighbor whose AFI/SAFI is the same", and only then "SHOULD ignore" later routes. The definition here describes the approach as optional and omits the deletion of routes already received, so "AFI/SAFI disable" can be read as only ignoring new routes while keeping stale ones, which is not what RFC 4760 specifies.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-10013 (c), 5.3"If the value of either the Optional or Transitive bits in the Attribute Flags is in conflict with their specified values, then the attribute MUST be treated as malformed and the "treat-as-withdraw" approach used / The attribute flags of the attribute are inconsistent with those specified in [RFC4760]."For MP_REACH_NLRI and MP_UNREACH_NLRI, 3(c) gives treat-as-withdraw for wrong Optional/Transitive bits, while 5.3 makes such an attribute "incorrect", which under RFC 4760 Section 7 and 3(j) / 7.11 leads to session reset or AFI/SAFI disable. The "unless the specification for the attribute mandates different handling" escape in 3(c) does not obviously cover a rule in the same document. Implementations can differ by two levels of severity for the same input.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10027.11"For example, if [RFC5549] is in use, then the next hop would have to have a length of 4 or 16."RFC 5549 Section 3 allows an IPv6 next hop of 16 or 32 octets (global plus link-local) for IPv4 unicast, and 24 or 48 for VPN-IPv4 (RFC 8950, which obsoletes RFC 5549, makes the VPN encoding 24 or 48). A receiver that applies the example literally treats a valid 32-octet next hop as malformed and resets the session or disables the family.errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-10037.5, 7.9, 7.10"if the LOCAL_PREF attribute is received from an external neighbor, it SHALL be discarded using the approach of "attribute discard"""External neighbor" is not defined with respect to confederations. RFC 5065 Section 5.3 keeps LOCAL_PREF across confederation-external (intra-confederation EBGP) sessions and route reflection may span member ASes; a literal reading discards LOCAL_PREF, ORIGINATOR_ID and CLUSTER_LIST received from confederation peers.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10046"a BGP speaker must provide debugging facilities ... At a minimum, such facilities must include logging an error listing the NLRI involved and containing the entire malformed UPDATE message"The requirement is written in lower case in an operational section, so its normative force is unclear. Logging every malformed UPDATE in full, with no rate limit, also lets a remote originator of a malformed transitive attribute (the attack this document addresses, Section 9) fill logs on every router that recognises it; the Security Considerations do not mention this.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0026 (RFC 7606, Section 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   For all path attributes other than those specified as having an
   attribute length that may be zero, it SHALL be considered a
   syntax error for the attribute to have a length of zero.

Corrected Text
--------------
   For all path attributes recognized by the receiver, other than
   those specified as having an attribute length that may be zero,
   it SHALL be considered a syntax error for the attribute to have a
   length of zero. An unrecognized optional attribute of length zero
   is handled as specified in RFC 4271 Section 5 for unrecognized
   attributes.

Notes
-----
   A receiver cannot know whether an unrecognized attribute may have
   length zero; the rule as written either makes every zero-length
   unrecognized attribute malformed (with no stated approach) or
   cannot be applied.

Proposed erratum RA-1000 (RFC 7606, Section 2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   AFI/SAFI disable: Section 7 of [RFC4760] allows a BGP speaker
   that detects an error in a message for a given AFI/SAFI to
   optionally "ignore all the subsequent routes with that AFI/SAFI
   received over that session".

Corrected Text
--------------
   AFI/SAFI disable: Section 7 of [RFC4760] requires a BGP speaker
   that detects an error in a message for a given AFI/SAFI to delete
   all routes with that AFI/SAFI received from the neighbor, and
   allows it to "ignore all the subsequent routes with that AFI/SAFI
   received over that session".

Notes
-----
   Without the deletion, routes received before the error remain in
   the Adj-RIB-In while all later updates (including withdrawals)
   for the family are ignored, leaving them stale for the life of
   the session.

Proposed erratum RA-1002 (RFC 7606, Section 7.11; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   For example, if [RFC5549] is in use, then the next hop would have
   to have a length of 4 or 16.

Corrected Text
--------------
   For example, if [RFC5549] is in use for IPv4 unicast, then the
   next hop would have to have a length of 4, 16, or 32.

Notes
-----
   RFC 5549 Section 3 permits a 16- or 32-octet IPv6 next hop. With
   the example as written a valid UPDATE is treated as malformed,
   with session reset or AFI/SAFI disable as the outcome.

RFC 7607: Codification of AS 0 Processing

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 rejected. Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 4271.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01242, 4"By ensuring that all implementations that see AS 0 in a route ignore that route, we prevent a malicious party from announcing routes containing AS 0"Section 2 sends AS 0 in AGGREGATOR to RFC 7606 and AS 0 in AS4_PATH / AS4_AGGREGATOR to RFC 6793. Both specify "attribute discard" for those attributes (RFC 7606 7.7; RFC 6793 6), so the route itself is kept and only the attribute is dropped. Only AS 0 in AS_PATH leads to treat-as-withdraw. The Security Considerations claim that every route containing AS 0 is ignored therefore holds only for AS_PATH; a route with AS 0 only in AS4_PATH is accepted with the AS_PATH it carries.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-01252"If a BGP speaker receives zero as the peer AS in an OPEN message, it MUST abort the connection and send a NOTIFICATION with Error Code "OPEN Message Error" and subcode "Bad Peer AS""With four-octet AS support the peer AS is carried in the Four-octet AS Number Capability (RFC 6793), with AS_TRANS in My Autonomous System; the text does not say that a capability value of 0 is covered, nor whether a My Autonomous System of 0 is still an error when the capability carries a valid AS.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0124 (RFC 7607, Section 2, 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   By ensuring that all implementations that see AS 0 in a route
   ignore that route, we prevent a malicious party from announcing
   routes containing AS 0 in an attempt to hijack those resources.

Corrected Text
--------------
   By ensuring that all implementations that see AS 0 in the AS_PATH
   of a route ignore that route (and discard AGGREGATOR, AS4_PATH or
   AS4_AGGREGATOR attributes containing AS 0), we prevent a
   malicious party from announcing routes containing AS 0 in an
   attempt to hijack those resources.

Notes
-----
   RFC 7606 Section 7.7 and RFC 6793 Section 6 handle malformed
   AGGREGATOR, AS4_PATH and AS4_AGGREGATOR by attribute discard, not
   treat-as-withdraw.

RFC 7611: BGP ACCEPT_OWN Community Attribute

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01262, 2.3"The functionality SHOULD default to being disabled / ACCEPT_OWN handling SHOULD be controlled by configuration, and if controlled by configuration, it MUST default to being disabled."Section 2 makes "disabled by default" a SHOULD, Section 2.3 a MUST (when configurable). Section 2.1 identifies the source VRF only by RD equality, which is ambiguous where the same RD is configured on more than one VRF of the router.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-04523, 1"the following step is inserted after the LOCAL_PREF comparison step in the BGP decision process"RFC 4271 has no "LOCAL_PREF comparison step" among the tie-breaking rules of 9.1.2.2; LOCAL_PREF enters through the degree of preference of 9.1.1 and the selection of 9.1.2.1. Implementations therefore insert the ACCEPT_OWN preference at different places (before AS_PATH length, or only between routes of equal degree of preference), which changes the outcome when two VPN-IP routes differ in both LOCAL_PREF policy and ACCEPT_OWN. The step is also defined only "if a BGP speaker ... is configured for the extensions"; whether a speaker that does not process ACCEPT_OWN (2.3 default) may still prefer such routes is not said. In Section 1, the rejection of self-originated routes through ORIGINATOR_ID is attributed to "the BGP specification [RFC4271]", whereas ORIGINATOR_ID and that rule are defined in RFC 4456 (not referenced).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 7911: Advertisement of Multiple Paths in BGP

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00303"If a BGP speaker receives a message to withdraw a prefix with a Path Identifier not seen before, it SHOULD silently ignore it."Nothing is said about an UPDATE whose NLRI cannot be parsed because the two sides disagree on whether ADD-PATH applies to a family; with ADD-PATH the 4-octet Path Identifier makes misparsing likely to look valid. RFC 7606 5.3 does not cover it.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-01274"If any other value is received, then the capability SHOULD be treated as not understood and ignored [RFC5492]. / MUST do so by including the information in a single instance of the ADD-PATH Capability.""The capability" can be read as the whole ADD-PATH Capability (all tuples, so one bad tuple disables ADD-PATH for every family) or as the one <AFI, SAFI, Send/Receive> tuple. The section also does not say what a receiver does with more than one instance of the capability, with the same <AFI, SAFI> listed twice, or with a Capability Length that is not a multiple of 4.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-01283, 5"In order to carry the Path Identifier in an UPDATE message, the NLRI encoding MUST be extended by prepending the Path Identifier field"The text and figure cover only the NLRI encoding; that the IPv4 Withdrawn Routes field and MP_UNREACH_NLRI also carry the Path Identifier follows only from Section 5 ("withdraw a prefix with a Path Identifier"). The interaction with label-carrying NLRI (RFC 8277) and other AFI encodings is not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0127 (RFC 7911, Section 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If any other value is received, then the capability SHOULD be
   treated as not understood and ignored [RFC5492].

Corrected Text
--------------
   If any other value is received, then that <AFI, SAFI> tuple
   SHOULD be ignored; the remaining tuples are processed. If the
   same <AFI, SAFI> appears more than once, or the capability
   appears more than once, only the first occurrence is used.

Notes
-----
   As written, a single bad tuple could disable ADD-PATH for all
   families. Handling of repeated instances, repeated <AFI, SAFI>
   tuples and a length that is not a multiple of four is not
   specified.

RFC 7947: Internet Exchange BGP Route Server

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01293, 2.2.2.2"The AS_PATH check described in Section 2.2.2 is normally enabled in order to check for malformed AS paths. ... this check is also used to detect BGP loops; removing the check could potentially cause routing loops to be formed."The check meant is the leftmost-AS check of Section 2.2.2.2 (first AS equals the peer's AS, RFC 4271 6.3). That check does not detect loops; loop detection is the separate own-AS-in-path check of RFC 4271 9.1.2, which is unaffected when the leftmost-AS check is disabled for a route server peer. The security rationale therefore overstates the risk and may lead implementers to disable the wrong check.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-0129 (RFC 7947, Section 3, 2.2.2.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The AS_PATH check described in Section 2.2.2 is normally enabled
   in order to check for malformed AS paths.

Corrected Text
--------------
   The AS_PATH check described in Section 2.2.2.2 (leftmost AS equal
   to the peer's AS) is normally enabled in order to check for
   malformed AS paths. Disabling it does not disable the AS_PATH
   loop detection of Section 9.1.2 of [RFC4271].

Notes
-----
   Loop detection in BGP is performed by checking for the local AS
   in the AS_PATH, which is independent of the leftmost-AS check.

RFC 7948: Internet Exchange BGP Route Server Operations

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 held. Status: Informational.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-04534.8"If the route server receives a BGP route where these addresses are different and where the announcing route server client is in a different AS to the route server client that uses the next-hop address, the BGP route SHOULD be dropped."The check needs the AS of whatever router owns the NEXT_HOP address, but the route server knows only its own clients. A NEXT_HOP pointing to an IXP participant that is not a route server client, or to an unused address on the IXP LAN, has no known AS, and the text does not say whether such a route is dropped or accepted; the hijacking case of Figure 3 is not prevented if AS2 is not itself a client. The test is also described as "matches the interface address of the client", which leaves out clients whose session runs from a different address than the forwarding interface (multiple addresses, IPv6 link-local vs global NEXT_HOP).ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

RFC 8205: BGPsec Protocol Specification

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 8206.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-04544.1, 4.4, 5.2"When originating a new route advertisement and sending it to a BGPsec-capable iBGP peer, the BGPsec speaker omits the BGPsec_PATH attribute."Such an UPDATE carries neither AS_PATH nor BGPsec_PATH. AS_PATH is a well-known mandatory attribute (RFC 4271 5.1.2, 6.3), and RFC 7606 3(d) makes its absence treat-as-withdraw. Section 5.2 relaxes the AS_PATH checks only "for BGPsec UPDATE messages", which Section 3 defines as UPDATEs containing BGPsec_PATH, and it also says the BGPsec_PATH "MUST be present ... when such an UPDATE message is propagated to an internal (iBGP) BGPsec peer". Only 4.4 says an absent BGPsec_PATH from a BGPsec-capable iBGP peer "is equivalent to an empty AS_PATH". The document does not list RFC 4271 or RFC 7606 as updated, so a receiver following them withdraws the route.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-04555, 8.1, 8.3"Thus, a BGPsec speaker MUST completely validate all BGPsec UPDATE messages received from external peers."Section 5 says a speaker "SHOULD validate" UPDATEs from eBGP peers and "MAY temporarily defer validation", 5.1 leaves the use of the result to local policy, and 8.3 suggests "only performing validation on UPDATE messages that, if valid, would be selected as the best path". 8.1 turns this into an unconditional MUST of complete validation; the requirement level for eBGP validation is inconsistent.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-04562.1, 9, 3.2, 6.3, 5.2"The Direction bit (fourth bit) has a value of either 0 or 1"Section 2.1 calls the Direction bit "The fifth bit of the first octet" and Figure 10 lists it as bit 4 (counting from 0); "fourth bit" in Section 9 names a different bit when counted as 2.1 counts.
