RFC 8518: Selection of Loop-Free Alternates for Multi-Homed Prefixes

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 5286.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-12233, 2"If an alternate neighbor N is also one of the prefix originators of prefix P, it is guaranteed that N will not loop back packets destined for prefix P to computing router S. Therefore, N MUST be chosen as a valid LFA"Section 2 models the multi-homed prefix with "D_opt(N,P) = Min (D_opt(N,PO_i) + Cost(PO_i,P)) over all PO_i"; for N itself as an originator that term is Cost(N,P). If N advertises P with a cost larger than its distance to P through S (D_opt(N,S) + D_opt(S,P)), N's own shortest path to P goes back through S, and selecting N "irrespective of the metric advertised by N for the prefix P" (Section 3, step 1.A of the link- and node-protecting procedures) creates a loop. The guarantee holds only if N always delivers P locally whatever its advertised cost, which the document does not state and which Section 4.1 (external prefixes in IS-IS, where the originator may itself prefer another route) does not ensure. The MUSTs ("N MUST be chosen", "router S MUST choose neighbor N") also leave unclear whether the exclusions of RFC 5286 3.5 and 3.5.1 (overload, maximum-cost links, excluded links) and its 3.6 permission not to use an available LFA still apply.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12245.1"But, the primary traffic destined to D2 continues to use the link; hence, irrespective of the reverse metric in this case, the same link MAY be used as a potential LFA for D1."RFC 5286 3.5 says "a router MUST NOT use an alternate next-hop that is along a link whose cost or reverse cost is LSInfinity (for OSPF) or the maximum cost (for IS-IS)", and gives the reason: an operator costs a link out "for maintenance that is not permitting traffic across that link unless there is no other path". Section 5.1 turns this into a MAY based on one TE use of the reverse metric, but gives no way for the computing router to tell a TE reverse metric from a maintenance cost-out, so applying the MAY sends repair traffic over links the operator removed from service. The abstract states that only Section 6 of RFC 5286 is updated, so a reader of RFC 5286 3.5 is not told that the MUST NOT is relaxed. For IS-IS, RFC 5305 Section 3 also says a link with the maximum link metric "MUST NOT be considered during the normal SPF computation", which the D_opt values of the example (N2 to S) do not reflect.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12254.2.1, 4.2.1.2, 4.2.1.4"3. If cost types are type 1, compare costs advertised by alternate ASBR and primary ASBR: A. If costs are the same, then program ECMP FRR and return."For type 1 external metrics the route cost is the distance to the ASBR (or forwarding address) plus the advertised cost (RFC 2328 16.4), so equal advertised type 1 costs do not make the two ASBRs equal-cost; step 4 (type 2) does compare the cost to reach the ASBR / forwarding address before declaring ECMP, step 3 does not. Steps 3.A and 4.C also "program ECMP FRR and return" before step 5, which is where the route type (type 5 against type 7) and the P-bit / forwarding address are compared, although Section 4.2.1.4 says "Type 5 routes always get preference over type 7" and that alternates "should have the same p-bit and forwarding address attributes". Type 7 (NSSA) routes are discussed without any reference to the NSSA specification (RFC 3101) that defines them and their preference rules. When RFC1583Compatibility is enabled, step 1 gives no branch at all (Section 4.2.1.3 describes the intent).errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12263.1"In this case, prefix P MUST inherit the corresponding LFAs of each primary next hop calculated for the router advertising the same."Section 3.1 starts from the RFC 5286 6.1 simplification (the MHP is "solely attached to the router that was its pre-failure optimal point of attachment"), which is a MAY, and then adds a MUST for the case where an ECMP MHP has several optimal points of attachment reached through different primary next hops. It does not say how an implementation that applies the simplification picks "the" optimal attachment point when there are several (the RFC 5286 text assumes one), nor whether the MUST means that each primary next hop's backup has to be the LFA computed for its own attachment router, or only that a valid per-next-hop LFA must exist. "Calculated for the router advertising the same" is also unclear (the router advertising the prefix, or the router reached through that next hop).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-1223 (RFC 8518, Section 3, 2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   1.  If, in addition to being an alternate neighbor, N is also a
   prefix originator of P, A.  Select N as an LFA for prefix P
   (irrespective of the metric advertised by N for the prefix P).

Corrected Text
--------------
   1.  If, in addition to being an alternate neighbor, N is also a
   prefix originator of P, and N's own advertisement of P is its
   shortest path to P (Cost(N,P) < D_opt(N,S) + D_opt(S,P)), A.
   Select N as an LFA for prefix P, subject to the exclusions of
   Sections 3.5 and 3.5.1 of [RFC5286].

Notes
-----
   Applies to step 1 of both the link-protecting and the
   node-protecting procedures in Section 3 and to the paragraph
   after them. Section 2's own formula for D_opt(N,P) includes N's
   advertised cost, so N's shortest path to P can lead back through
   S when that cost is high.

Proposed erratum RA-1224 (RFC 8518, Section 5.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   But, the primary traffic destined to D2 continues to use the
   link; hence, irrespective of the reverse metric in this case, the
   same link MAY be used as a potential LFA for D1.

Corrected Text
--------------
   But, the primary traffic destined to D2 continues to use the
   link; hence, where the operator has configured that the reverse
   metric is used for traffic engineering and not to take the link
   out of service, the same link MAY be used as a potential LFA for
   D1.  This relaxes the rule of Section 3.5 of [RFC5286] only for
   links so configured.

Notes
-----
   The abstract and the "Updates: 5286" header refer to Section 6 of
   RFC 5286 only. RFC 5286 3.5 keeps maximum-cost links out of
   alternates so that a link costed out for maintenance carries no
   traffic unless no other path exists.

Proposed erratum RA-1225 (RFC 8518, Section 4.2.1, 4.2.1.2, 4.2.1.4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   3.  If cost types are type 1, compare costs advertised by
   alternate ASBR and primary ASBR: A.  If costs are the same, then
   program ECMP FRR and return. B.  Else, go to step 5.

Corrected Text
--------------
   3.  If cost types are type 1, compare the total costs (the cost
   to reach the ASBR/forwarding address plus the advertised type 1
   cost) of alternate ASBR and primary ASBR: A.  If the total costs
   are the same, go to step 5 and, if the alternate ASBR passes step
   5, program ECMP FRR and return. B.  Else, go to step 5.

Notes
-----
   Step 4.C (type 2) has the same ordering problem: it programs ECMP
   FRR before step 5. RFC 2328 Section 16.4 computes a type 1
   external path cost as the distance to the ASBR or forwarding
   address plus the advertised cost.

RFC 8570: IS-IS Traffic Engineering (TE) Metric Extensions

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 7810.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00444.5 to 4.7, 11"The length specified was 4, which did not include the RESERVED field shown in the figures."RFC 7810 drew a RESERVED octet that its Length (4) did not count; implementations split on length 4 against 5. RFC 8570 removes the field. A receiver may still meet length-5 sub-TLVs 37 to 39 from old RFC 7810 speakers.errornone: RFC has no errata
RA-01744.6, Appendix A"For a bundled link, available bandwidth is defined to be the sum of the component link available bandwidths. / it used "sum of the component link available bandwidths" when it should have used "sum of the component link residual bandwidths". This has been corrected and clarified."Appendix A states that the definition criticised in erratum 5486 against RFC 7810 has been corrected, but Section 4.6 still carries the RFC 7810 wording verbatim. Either the correction was lost during editing or the appendix is wrong; an implementer cannot tell which definition is intended for bundles (and "sum of the component link residual bandwidths" would equal the residual bandwidth of Section 4.5, which suggests the appendix wording is not right either).contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-01754.4"The basic unit is 0.000003%, where (2^24 - 2) is 50.331642%. This value is the highest packet-loss percentage that can be expressed"The 24-bit field can hold 2^24 - 1, but the text names 2^24 - 2 as the highest expressible value without saying whether 2^24 - 1 is reserved, invalid or simply also "at least" 50.331642%. Implementations clamping to 2^24 - 1 and to 2^24 - 2 coexist; a receiver does not know how to treat 2^24 - 1.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-01763"However, as for the TE case, Interface Address and Neighbor Address sub-TLVs (IPv4 or IPv6) MUST be present."Unnumbered links have no interface or neighbor address and are identified by Link Local/Remote Identifiers (RFC 5307 sub-TLV 4), and links to a pseudonode have no single neighbor address. Read literally, the MUST forbids TE Metric Extensions on such links. Section 4.3 also defines delay variation as "the delay from the local neighbor to the remote neighbor (i.e., the forward-path latency)", a copy of the delay sentence.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-13392, 5"All values (except residual bandwidth) MUST be calculated as rolling averages, where the averaging period MUST be a configurable period of time. / The values advertised in all sub-TLVs (except minimum/maximum delay and residual bandwidth) MUST represent an average"Section 2 requires every value except residual bandwidth, including the minimum and maximum delay of sub-TLV 34, to be a rolling average. Section 5 exempts minimum / maximum delay from averaging and requires them to be the lowest / highest value of the interval (or a filtered representation of them), and it allows any filter "reasonably representative of an average" rather than a rolling average only. A minimum that is a rolling average is not a minimum, so the two MUSTs cannot both be met for sub-TLV 34.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13404.3, 4.1, 4.2"Delay Variation: This 24-bit field carries the average link delay variation over a configurable interval in microseconds, encoded as an integer value. When set to 0, it has not been measured."Zero is given the meaning "not measured", but zero (below one microsecond after rounding) is also a legitimate measured delay variation on a short, lightly loaded link, so a measured value of 0 cannot be expressed, and the text does not say what a sender with a measured 0 sends (1, or omit the sub-TLV) nor how a receiver treats 0 in path computation (unknown, or no variation). The delay sub-TLVs (4.1, 4.2) give no such meaning to 0, so a measured 0 delay is a value there; the reason for the asymmetry is not stated, and an implementation sending "not measured" would rather omit the sub-TLV (Section 8 lets each sub-TLV be disabled).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-13412, 12"This document registers new IS-IS TE sub-TLVs in the "Sub-TLVs for TLVs 22, 23, 141, 222, and 223" registry. / have nested sub-TLVs that permit the TLVs to be readily extended."The registry covers TLVs 22, 23, 141, 222 and 223, but Section 2 names only TLVs 22, 141 and 222 as carriers, and Section 12 registers sub-TLVs 33 to 39 without the per-TLV applicability columns that registry has. Whether the sub-TLVs may appear in TLVs 23 and 223 (IS Neighbor Attribute, RFC 5311) is not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-13424.5, 4.6, 4.7"MUST be the residual bandwidth from the system originating the Link State Advertisement (LSA) to its neighbor. / MUST be the available bandwidth from the system originating this sub-TLV."Section 4.5 uses the OSPF term "Link State Advertisement (LSA)" where IS-IS has Link State PDUs (copied from RFC 7471). Sections 4.6 and 4.7 state the direction only as "from the system originating this sub-TLV", without the "to its neighbor" that 4.5 has, so the direction of the advertised bandwidth is only implied.editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-0174 (RFC 8570, Section 4.6, Appendix A; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   For a bundled link, available bandwidth is defined to be the sum
   of the component link available bandwidths.

Corrected Text
--------------
   (Clarification requested; one possibility:) For a bundled link,
   available bandwidth is defined to be the residual bandwidth of
   the bundle (Section 4.5) minus the measured bandwidth used for
   the actual forwarding of non-RSVP-TE label switched path packets
   over all component links.

Notes
-----
   The text of Section 4.6 matches RFC 7810 Section 4.6, which
   erratum 5486 reported as circular. The appendix's replacement
   wording would make available bandwidth equal to residual
   bandwidth for bundles.

Corrected Text
--------------
   All values (except minimum/maximum delay and residual bandwidth)
   MUST be calculated as averages over a configurable period of time

RA-0180Appendix A, 3"| Type(25) | Length(64) | ... |Len:9+6+10 = 25| # Desc: 2 | / | Type(25) | Length(46) |"The descriptor lengths in the example (25, 25 and 32) exclude the descriptor's own length octet ("9 + 6 + 10": member count and identifiers, Maximum Link Bandwidth sub-TLV, Adj-SID sub-TLV), as Section 3 implies. RFC 8706: Restart Signaling for IS-IS

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 5306.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-10473.2, 3.2.1, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.4.1.2, Tables 2 and 3"The RR and SA flags may both be set in the TLV under the conditions described in Section 3.3.2. All other combinations where multiple flags are set are invalid"A router that is itself (re)starting must still answer a neighbour's RR with RA (Table 2 and Table 3, "RX RR: Send RA"; 3.3.2 "the behavior described in Section 3.2.1 is followed"). A restarting router's IIHs carry RR until its T1 is cancelled, and a starting router "sets the SA bit ... in all IIHs that it sends" (3.4.1.2), but RR+RA and SA+RA are invalid combinations that the receiver "MUST" ignore. When two adjacent routers (re)start at the same time (for example after a shared power failure), the document does not say which flag wins. If the RA is sent alone (3.2.1 b: "with the RR bit clear and the RA bit set"), a starting router's RA IIH has SA clear, which per 3.2.2 ends the neighbour's suppression ("Until an IIH with the SA bit clear has been received") and re-advertises the adjacency until the next SA IIH, causing the churn SA is meant to avoid. If the RA is deferred instead, each restarting router waits for the other's RA to cancel T1, and both fall back to T1 expiry after the retry limit.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-10483.4.1.1, 3.4.1.2, 3.2.3, Tables 1 to 3"When all the T2 timers have expired or been canceled, the timer T3 is canceled / (Table 2) LSP DB Sync | Cancel T2 and T3"The state tables disagree with the text in three places. (1) Table 2 cancels T3 on "LSP DB Sync" of one LSPDB, while 3.4.1.1 cancels T3 only when all T2 timers have ended; for a Level 1/2 router the table ends T3 after the first level. (2) Table 3 clears the overload bit on "T2 expires", for each T2 and unconditionally, while 3.4.1.2 allows clearing only "When all the T2 timers have been canceled" (expiry not mentioned), as a MAY and only if there is no other reason (such as incomplete BGP convergence) to keep it. (3) 3.2.3 a says an IIH "with the PR bit reset will clear the Planned Restart State" and restore the configured Holding Time, while the later paragraph and Table 1 end that state only on an IIH with RR set or with both PR and RR clear; Table 1 has no entry for RR received in Planned Restart State.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-10493.2.2, 6"If the SA bit is set in a false IIH, this could cause suppression of the advertisement of an IS neighbor, which could either continue for an indefinite period"Security gap: The document names the risk but gives the receiver no bound: 3.2.2 requires suppression "Until an IIH with the SA bit clear has been received", with no maximum duration, although a genuine starting router clears SA when its T2 timers end (a typical T2 is 60 s, 3.1). A helper-side limit (for example a multiple of T2), as is done for the PR Holding Time, would bound the damage of a forged or stuck SA. Only authentication is offered as mitigation.errornone: RFC has no errata
RA-10503.3.1, 3.3.2"Therefore, timer T1 is canceled after some predetermined number of expirations (which MAY be 1)."The number of T1 expirations is left open with no default or recommended value (only T1 = 3 s and T2 = 60 s are suggested), and the document does not say whether a T1 cancelled by retry exhaustion counts as "canceled" for the T2 rule of 3.4 ("the timer T1 has been canceled for all the interfaces"). With a retry limit of 1 and no neighbour heard, T2 can end after one T1 interval, well before any neighbour could have sent its CSNPs.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-1047 (RFC 8706, Section 3.2, 3.2.1, 3.3.1, 3.3.2, 3.4.1.2, Tables 2 and 3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The RR and SA flags may both be set in the TLV under the
   conditions described in Section 3.3.2.  All other combinations
   where multiple flags are set are invalid and MUST NOT be
   transmitted.

Corrected Text
--------------
   (The working group should state the intended behaviour.) For
   example: "A router that is itself restarting or starting and
   receives an IIH with RR set sends the acknowledgement in an IIH
   with only the RA bit set (and the Remaining Time and Restarting
   Neighbor System ID fields); a receiver of such an IIH does not
   treat the absence of RR or SA in it as clearing Restart mode or
   adjacency suppression."

Notes
-----
   The case of two adjacent routers restarting or starting at the
   same time is not covered. Tables 2 and 3 require RA in reply to
   RR, Section 3.4.1.2 requires SA in all IIHs of a starting router,
   and Section 3.2 forbids RA+RR and RA+SA. Sending RA alone clears
   SA at the neighbour (Section 3.2.2), which defeats the
   suppression.

Proposed erratum RA-1048 (RFC 8706, Section 3.4.1.1, 3.4.1.2, 3.2.3, Tables 1 to 3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   | LSP DB   | Cancel T2 and   |
    | Sync     | T3              |

Corrected Text
--------------
   | LSP DB   | Cancel T2;      |
    | Sync     | if all T2 ended: cancel T3 |

Notes
-----
   Section 3.4.1.1 cancels T3 only "When all the T2 timers have
   expired or been canceled"; Table 2 cancels it on the
   synchronization of a single LSPDB. Similarly Table 3 clears the
   overload bit on each T2 expiry, while Section 3.4.1.2 permits it
   only when all T2 timers have been canceled.

RA-05572.1.2.1"The check is successful when either: ... HMAC Segments Left is less than or equal to Last Entry, and the destination address is equal to Segment List[Segments Left]. / Text: ... Source address ... Last Entry ... Flags ... HMAC 16 bits following Length ... HMAC Key ID ... All addresses in the Segment List"Security gap: Segments Left (and Tag) are not part of the HMAC Text, and the destination check only requires DA == Segment List[Segments Left]. Where the HMAC is used to enforce traversal of a service or filtering SID, it can be bypassed. The Security Considerations do not mention this limit. Also "HMAC Segments Left" in the second bullet is a wording slip (the HMAC has no Segments Left).errornone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-05582.1.2.1"The HMAC digest is truncated to 32 octets and placed in the HMAC field of the HMAC TLV. For HMAC algorithms producing digests less than 32 octets long, the digest is placed in the lowest-order octets of the HMAC field. Subsequent octets MUST be set to zero""Lowest-order octets" of a field transmitted in network order normally means the last (least significant) octets, but "Subsequent octets MUST be set to zero" implies the digest occupies the first octets followed by zero fill. Implementations can place a 20-octet digest at either end of a 24-octet field and fail to interoperate. The HMAC field length is also only bounded ("multiples of 8 octets, at most 32"), without a rule tying it to the algorithm of the Key ID.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-05594.3.1.1"S06. If local configuration requires TLV processing { / S07. Perform TLV processing (see TLV Processing) / S08. } / S09. max_last_entry = ( Hdr Ext Len / 2 ) - 1"The pseudocode processes TLVs (whose position is derived from Last Entry, TLVs starting after (Last Entry+1)*16 octets of segments) before S10 checks that Last Entry is consistent with Hdr Ext Len. With a Last Entry larger than the header allows, a literal implementation locates TLVs beyond the SRH before the packet is rejected; Section 2.1 only says TLVs exceeding Hdr Ext Len produce a Parameter Problem, not that the Last Entry check comes first. The consistency check should precede TLV processing.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-05606.5, 6.3.3"P7: (A8,S3)(A8,A1) (6.3.3) / P7: (A8,A9)(A9,S7; SL=0) (6.5)"The label P7 is used for two different packets (host 8 to host 1 encapsulated toward S3, and P1 after processing at node 7); packet labels then jump from P9 to P15. The second should have its own label (for example P10).editorialnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0557 (RFC 8754, Section 2.1.2.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   HMAC Segments Left is less than or equal to Last Entry, and the
   destination address is equal to Segment List[Segments Left].

Corrected Text
--------------
   Segments Left is less than or equal to Last Entry, and the
   destination address is equal to Segment List[Segments Left]. Note
   that Segments Left is not covered by the HMAC; the HMAC therefore
   does not prove that the segments preceding the current one were
   traversed.

Notes
-----
   Editorial fix plus a security note; protecting Segments Left
   would need a different construction since it changes at every
   endpoint.

Proposed erratum RA-0558 (RFC 8754, Section 2.1.2.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   For HMAC algorithms producing digests less than 32 octets long,
   the digest is placed in the lowest-order octets of the HMAC
   field.

Corrected Text
--------------
   For HMAC algorithms producing digests less than 32 octets long,
   the digest is placed in the first (leftmost) octets of the HMAC
   field.

Notes
-----
   The following sentence (zero fill of subsequent octets) indicates
   the intended placement.

RFC 8918: Invalid TLV Handling in IS-IS

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 5305, RFC 6232.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-13483.1, 3.4, 4"TLVs in a PDU (other than LSP purges) that are disallowed MUST be ignored and MUST NOT cause the PDU itself to be rejected by the receiving IS. (3.1) / The correct setting for "LSP" is "n". (3.4)"With 3.4 the POI TLV (type 13) is disallowed in LSPs (registry LSP:n), so by 3.1 a POI TLV in an LSP with non-zero Remaining Lifetime MUST be ignored and the LSP MUST NOT be rejected; 4 adds that rejection of an LSP for TLV content "will result in inconsistent LSP Databases". RFC 6233 Section 3, which this document does not update and cites in 4 only for purge acceptance, still says "ISs MUST NOT accept LSPs with a non-zero Remaining Lifetime that contain the POI TLV". 3.4 also rewrites the RFC 6232 sentence from "MUST NOT be found" to "MUST NOT be sent", turning it into a sender-only rule, which agrees with 3.1 but leaves the RFC 6233 receiver rule in place. A receiver following RFC 6233 drops such an LSP while one following this document stores and floods it, which is the LSDB divergence 4 is meant to prevent.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13491, 3.1, 4"PDUs that are valid must be accepted [ISO10589] even if an individual TLV contained within that PDU is not understood or is invalid in some way (e.g., incorrect syntax, data value out of range, etc.). (1)"The Introduction states for all PDUs that an invalid TLV (bad syntax, out-of-range value) does not make the PDU unacceptable, but the normative text covers only two cases: disallowed TLVs in non-purge PDUs (3.1) and non-conforming TLVs in LSPs (4, "MUST NOT cause the LSP itself to be rejected"). Nothing normative says whether an IIH or SNP with a malformed allowed TLV (for example an IP Interface Address TLV whose length is not a multiple of 4, an empty Area Addresses TLV, or a malformed Three-Way Adjacency TLV) is discarded or processed without that TLV. Some of these TLVs are essential to adjacency formation, so both readings occur; the lowercase "must" with a reference to ISO 10589 does not say which ISO rule is meant.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13503.2"the extensions defined by [RFC6232] are not compatible with the behavior defined in [RFC5304]; therefore, they can only be safely enabled when all nodes support the extensions. / it is RECOMMENDED that implementations provide controls for their enablement."The section recommends an enablement control for POI generation (RFC 6232) and for strict purge acceptance (RFC 5304), but RFC 6233 Section 3, which it cites as the current purge acceptance rule, makes POI insertion mandatory for an implementation that implements authentication ("The POI TLV MUST be added"). Whether an implementation with authentication that keeps POI generation disabled (the safe setting this section describes for a mixed network) conforms to RFC 6233 is not said. The section also summarises RFC 6233 only as adding the Purge column; the RFC 6233 rule that a purge with an unregistered TLV is acceptable when it also carries the POI TLV is not restated, so 3.2 reads as "allowed = Purge column y" only.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-13514, 3.3"The definition MUST include what action to take when the format/content of the TLV does not conform to the specification / receiving nodes MUST verify that the TLV conforms to the standard definition."The requirement is placed on the documents that define codepoints, but most existing definitions (for example RFC 5305 for sub-TLVs of TLV 22 and the prefix length of TLV 135) state no such action, and this document, although it updates RFC 5305, does not supply one or a default. A receiver that "MUST verify" conformance therefore still has to choose between ignoring the sub-TLV, the containing TLV entry, or the whole TLV when an older definition is silent; only rejection of the LSP is excluded. "Ignored" in 3.1 / 3.3 also does not say whether an ignored TLV is still kept in the stored and re-flooded LSP (it must be, since the LSP is flooded unchanged, but the text does not say so).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-1348 (RFC 8918, Section 3.1, 3.4, 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   This document also updates the previously quoted text from
   Section 3 of [RFC6232] to be:

Corrected Text
--------------
   This document also updates the previously quoted text from
   Section 3 of [RFC6232] to be: [quoted text unchanged]. Consistent
   with Section 3.1, the sentence in Section 3 of [RFC6233] "ISs
   MUST NOT accept LSPs with a non-zero Remaining Lifetime that
   contain the POI TLV" is replaced by: "A POI TLV received in an
   LSP with a non-zero Remaining Lifetime MUST be ignored; its
   presence MUST NOT cause the LSP to be rejected."

Notes
-----
   Section 3.4 marks the POI TLV LSP:n and Section 3.1 requires
   disallowed TLVs to be ignored without rejecting the PDU, but RFC
   6233 Section 3 keeps a receiver rule that rejects the LSP. The
   document lists only RFC 5305 and RFC 6232 as updated. The working
   group should say which rule applies; the corrected text assumes
   Section 3.1 is intended. This may need a document update rather
   than an erratum.

Proposed erratum RA-1349 (RFC 8918, Section 1, 3.1, 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   PDUs that are valid must be accepted [ISO10589] even if an
   individual TLV contained within that PDU is not understood or is
   invalid in some way (e.g., incorrect syntax, data value out of
   range, etc.).

Corrected Text
--------------
   (Clarification.) State whether the rule applies to all PDU types
   or only to LSPs as in Section 4, e.g.: "LSPs that are valid MUST
   be accepted even if an individual TLV contained within that LSP
   is not understood or is invalid in some way (Section 4). For IIHs
   and SNPs, the treatment of an invalid TLV is defined by the
   document that specifies the TLV."

Notes
-----
   Section 1 speaks of PDUs in general, but the normative
   requirement in Section 4 is limited to LSPs. Implementations
   differ on IIHs with a malformed TLV that is used for adjacency
   formation.

RA-13524 (2)(B), 3"When the IS-IS ASLA sub-TLV has the RSVP-TE application bit set, then the link attributes for the corresponding IS-IS ASLA sub-TLVs MUST be encoded using the respective BGP-LS top-level TLVs (4 (2)(B)) / the attributes advertised within the ASLA TLV take precedence for the applications indicated in the ASLA TLV encoding (3)"An IS-IS ASLA sub-TLV with the RSVP-TE bit and other bits (for example R and S) falls under rule (1) (encode in a BGP-LS ASLA TLV) and rule (2)(B) (encode at top level); the text does not say whether the BGP-LS ASLA copy keeps or clears the RSVP-TE bit. If it keeps it, the Section 3 precedence rule makes the ASLA copy authoritative for RSVP-TE, so the top-level encoding that (2)(B) and Section 3 require ("REQUIRED to be advertised as a top-level TLV when used to carry link attributes specific to RSVP-TE") has no effect for receivers that support this document. The rules also do not say which source wins at top level when both legacy IS-IS sub-TLVs (with or without an L-flag ASLA) and an RSVP-TE-bit ASLA sub-TLV carry values, nor how a zero-length-mask BGP-LS ASLA TLV (rule (2)(E), all applications) ranks against the top-level TLVs for RSVP-TE under the precedence rule, since it "indicates" no specific application.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

"The next rule that applies" also skips over rule (2)(E), which is the rule that keeps item 4 of the "final set" (later cited correctly as "(2)(e)").editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RFC 9350: IGP Flexible Algorithm

Depth: deep. Errata: 2 errata: 1 verified, 1 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 9843, RFC 9917.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-018413.1 vs 8"During the route computation, it is possible for the Flex-Algorithm-specific metric to exceed the maximum value that can be stored in an unsigned 32-bit variable. In such scenarios, the value MUST be considered to be of value 0xFFFFFFFF during the computation and advertised as such."A metric that saturates at 0xFFFFFFFF and is advertised as such in a FAPM is, by Section 8 ("Flex-Algorithm prefix metric larger than MAX_PATH_METRIC ... MUST NOT be considered"), unusable in the next area, while the same overflow in the default algorithm is clamped to MAX_PATH_METRIC (0xFE000000) and stays usable (RFC 5305 3). A prefix reachable at a large cost in algorithm 0 thus becomes unreachable for the flex-algorithm across an ABR. Whether saturating at 0xFFFFFFFF (rather than at MAX_PATH_METRIC) is intended is not stated.contradictionnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-01855.3, 6"If it appears more than once, the IS-IS FAD sub-TLV MUST be ignored by the receiver."Sections 6.1 to 6.5 give receive rules for duplicates but none for a sub-sub-TLV whose Length is not a multiple of 4 (a sender MUST only). Whether such a FAD is invalid (stop participating, 5.3) or only the sub-sub-TLV is ignored is left open; ignoring only an exclude rule changes the computed paths.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-135413.1, 8"The FAPM MUST NOT be advertised with IS-IS L1 or L2 intra-area, OSPFv2 intra-area, or OSPFv3 intra-area routes. / If the FAPM for the Flex-Algorithm is not advertised with the inter-area or external prefix reachability advertisement, the prefix MUST be considered as unreachable for that Flex-Algorithm."With the M-flag, a receiver must decide per prefix advertisement whether it is inter-area (FAPM required, otherwise unreachable) or intra-area (FAPM ignored). OSPF marks this by LSA type; IS-IS has no route-type field, and the document does not say how an IS-IS receiver classifies a prefix: a level 2 prefix that an L1/L2 router propagated from its level 1 area (RFC 5302, no up/down bit, possibly with the R-flag of RFC 7794 or without it) can be read as an L2 intra-area route (reachable without FAPM) or as an inter-area route (unreachable without FAPM). Routers that classify differently compute different flex-algorithm reachability for the same prefix, and the 5.1 "IS-IS L1 or L2 intra-area" wording does not settle it.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-13555.1, 5.3, 15.1"An IS-IS L1/L2 router MAY be configured to regenerate the winning FAD from level 2 ... / A router that is not configured to participate in a particular Flex-Algorithm MUST ignore FAD sub-TLV advertisements for such Flex-Algorithm."Regeneration of the level 2 winning FAD into level 1 (5.1, 15.1) requires the L1/L2 router to run the 5.3 selection for that algorithm, but 5.3 requires a router that does not participate in the algorithm to ignore its FAD advertisements, and 5.3 explicitly allows non-participating routers to advertise FADs. Whether a non-participating L1/L2 router may (or must) select and regenerate the level 2 winning FAD is not stated; if it may not, an operator relying on 15.1 ("configure the FAD in one or multiple routers in level 2") loses the definition in level 1 areas whose border routers do not participate. Also unstated: what the regenerating router advertises (or withdraws) when no level 2 FAD exists any more.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-135613"check if all colors that are part of the include-all rule are also set on the link. If all such colors are not set on the link, the link MUST be pruned from the computation.""If all such colors are not set" can be read as "if none of the colors is set" (prune only links with no listed color, which is the include-any rule) or as "if not all of the colors are set" (prune links missing any listed color). Only the second gives an include-all rule distinct from rule 3. RFC 9917 (which updates RFC 9350) copies the sentence unchanged into its rule registry (12.3, rule 4) and its reverse-affinity rule (11, rule 10).ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-135715.3, 18.4.8"The link can be made the link of last resort by setting the TE metric value in the Flex-Algorithm ASLA delay advertisement for the link to the value of (2^24 - 1) in IS-IS"(a) 15.3 sets the TE metric "in the Flex-Algorithm ASLA delay advertisement"; the TE metric is carried in the ASLA TE Default Metric (IS-IS) / TE Metric (OSPF) advertisement, not the delay one (copy of the preceding paragraph). (b) Table 14 (18.4.8) labels its first column "Bit Number" although it lists sub-TLV type values.editorialnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-1354 (RFC 9350, Section 13.1, 8; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The FAPM MUST NOT be advertised with IS-IS L1 or L2 intra-area,
   OSPFv2 intra-area, or OSPFv3 intra-area routes.

Corrected Text
--------------
   (Clarification needed.) Add: "For IS-IS, a prefix advertisement
   is considered inter-area if it is a level 1 advertisement with
   the up/down bit set, or a level 2 advertisement with the R-flag
   [RFC7794] set that was propagated from level 1; all other
   advertisements are intra-area."

-----

RA-01896, 7.1"When included in the Locator TLV, the state of the X-flag in the Prefix Attributes Flags sub-TLV MUST match the setting of the embedded "X-bit" in any advertisement for the same prefix in TLVs 236 [RFC5308] and 237 [RFC5120]."The SRv6 Locator TLV has no embedded X-bit, so a locator that is not also advertised in TLV 236/237 has only the sub-TLV X-flag; when the Prefix Attribute Flags sub-TLV (only a SHOULD in 7.1) is absent, whether the locator is external is unknown, while the D-flag is carried in the entry itself. The text does not say how a receiver treats a locator without the sub-TLV for external/internal preference.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 9479: IS-IS Application-Specific Link Attributes

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 8919.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01924.2"In cases where conflicting values for the same application/attribute/link are advertised, the first advertisement received in the lowest-numbered Link State Protocol Data Unit (LSP) MUST be used""First ... received" mixes arrival order with LSP order. Within one LSP fragment the order is the TLV order; across fragments the lowest LSP number decides; but "received" suggests that a later-arriving advertisement in a lower-numbered fragment would not replace one already in use. The rule also has an exception for maximum link bandwidth (4.2.1: all values ignored), which a reader of 4.2 alone would miss.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-01934.2, 6.2"Such link attribute advertisements MUST be used by standard applications and/or UDAs when no link attribute advertisements with a non-zero-length Application Identifier Bit Mask and a matching Application Identifier Bit set are present for a given link."The condition is stated per link, not per attribute: if an application has a non-zero-mask ASLA entry for the link that carries only some attributes (for example TE metric), the zero-length entry's other attributes (for example delay) are then not usable by that application. Whether resolution is per link or per attribute is left to the reader, although Section 9 says the change was made to remove interoperability problems.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 9502: IGP Flexible Algorithm in IP Networks

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01946.1, 6.2"If the Algorithms in the IS-IS IPv4 Algorithm Prefix Reachability TLV are outside the Flex-Algorithm range (128-255), the IS-IS IPv4 Algorithm Prefix Reachability TLV MUST be ignored by the receiver."The Algorithm is a field of each prefix entry, and a TLV carries several entries. Read literally, one entry with an out-of-range algorithm makes the receiver drop the valid entries packed in the same TLV, so the set of reachable prefixes depends on how the originator packed them. Ignoring only the offending entry is the more likely intent (the entries remain parseable).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13586.1, 6.2"Optional Sub-TLV-length (1 octet): Number of octets used by sub-TLVs / Optional sub-TLVs (variable length)"Figure 4 draws the Sub-tlv-len octet in every prefix entry, but the field list calls it "Optional", and unlike the Extended IP Reachability TLV (RFC 5305 4.1, where the S bit of the control octet says whether the sub-TLV length is present) the Flags octet of TLV 126 has no bit announcing it. A TLV holds several prefix entries, so a receiver can only find the next entry if it knows whether the octet is there; if it is optional, the encoding cannot be parsed. The number of octets of the Prefix field ("Prefix (variable length)") is also not stated (RFC 5305 packs the prefix into the minimal number of octets). TLV 127 inherits both points ("identical ... except that it has a distinct type").ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13598, 6.4"The IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability advertisement as described in Section 5 includes the MTID value that associates the prefix with a specific topology."Section 5 specifies participation (the IP Algorithm sub-TLV / TLV), which carries no MTID; prefix reachability is Section 6. The OSPFv3 IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability sub-TLV (6.4, Figure 7) also has no MT-ID field, so the statement that the advertisement "includes the MTID value" holds for IS-IS (6.1) and OSPFv2 (6.3) only.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13606.3, 6.4"0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 / +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+ / |E| Reserved |"The Flags field of the OSPFv2 IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability sub-TLV is one octet, but its figure numbers nine bit positions (0 to 8); Table 6 assigns bits 0 to 7. Sections 6.3 and 6.4 also speak of receiving "multiple OSPFv2 [OSPFv3] IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability TLVs" where sub-TLVs are meant, and 6.4 repeats "in an OSPFv3 OSPFv3 IP Algorithm Prefix Reachability Sub-TLV".editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13616.1, 6.2, 12"If a router receives multiple IPv4 Algorithm Prefix Reachability advertisements for the same prefix, from different originators, where all of them do not advertise the same algorithm, it MUST ignore all of them""all of them do not advertise the same algorithm" can be read as "not all advertise the same algorithm" (any disagreement) or "none advertise the same algorithm". The scope of "the same prefix" is also open: advertisements of the prefix in different topologies (MTID) or at different levels are not said to be compared or not. Section 12 relies on this rule as an attack vector (one rogue originator suppresses a prefix), so the reading decides how much a single bad advertisement removes.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RFC 9800: Compressed SRv6 Segment List Encoding

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 8754.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-05674.2""Since the SR source node does not use the third CSID container at full capacity, it sets the 64 least significant bits to zero.""In packed format, CSIDs fill positions from K-1 (least significant) toward 0, as Section 4.2 states and Figure 5 shows (7th and 6th CSID in the low 64 bits, zero in the high 64 bits). The unused part is therefore the most significant 64 bits, not the least significant.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-05686.2 vs 6.4, 4.2.1""S16. Break" / "the next element in the SID list MUST be a REPLACE-CSID container in packed format carrying at least one CSID.""In the REPLACE-CSID compression method, when a REPLACE-CSID flavor SID is followed by a SID that fails ComCheck (for example, a different Locator-Block), the loop breaks. The method then emits that SID as is after a container whose last CSID has the REPLACE-CSID flavor. If that CSID is in position 0 of a full packed container, or is the lone full-format SID (S03 creates no packed container, and S19 pushes only a non-empty one), Section 6.4 rule 3 is violated. The Section 4.2.1 R12-R17 branch then reads position K-1 of the next 128-bit entry without the zero check of R06, so the next DA is built from bits of an uncompressed SID. Section 6.2 says the method's output MUST follow Section 6.4.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-05696.4""with LNL = 16, FL = 16 ... are also marked as using 16-bit compression. When receiving ... a REPLACE-CSID flavor SID with LNFL = 32 ... marks both the SID and its locator as using 32-bit compression.""A SID with LNL = 16 and FL = 16 has LNFL = 32. It matches the 32-bit rule and, if its locator was already marked by an LNL = 16, FL = 0 advertisement, also the 16-bit rule. The outcome depends on the order in which advertisements arrive, and the text does not say what happens when the locator's End SID (FL = 0) is not, or not yet, received.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-05708 vs 6.1""The SR segment endpoint node MUST set the SID Argument bits to 0 when advertising" / "The AL is equal to 128-LBL-LNL-FL.""Section 8 requires the Argument value to be zero, while the SRv6 SID Structure needs to carry the real Argument length (example "AL: 48 (= 128-48-16-16)"). Section 6.1 treats a structure whose AL is not 128-LBL-LNL-FL as invalid, so the SID cannot be compressed. The two requirements sit side by side, and the text does not explicitly say that the Structure's Argument length stays non-zero. "Argument bits to 0" can be misread as AL = 0.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-05714.2, A.6-A.10""If LNFL does not divide into 128 perfectly, a zero pad is added in the least significant bits" / "R17. Set DA.Arg.Index to (128/LNFL - 1).""For an LNFL that does not divide 128, the zero pad in the least significant bits conflicts with "the least significant bit position ... (position K-1)" and with the bit numbering [Index*LNFL..(Index+1)*LNFL-1], which puts position K-1 before the pad. Appendix A writes 128/LNFL - 1 where Section 4.2.1 R17 has floor(128/LNFL) - 1. Only 16-bit and 32-bit LNFL are defined, so the issue does not arise for those lengths.editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RFC 9843: IGP Flexible Algorithms: Bandwidth, Delay, Metrics, and Constraints

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 9350. Updated by: RFC 9917.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01954.1.3.2"The Bandwidth Metric MUST be set to the maximum metric value of 4,261,412,864."In IS-IS the Generic Metric sub-TLV carries a 3-octet metric (Section 2.1: "A metric value of 0xFFFFFF is considered a maximum link metric"), so 4,261,412,864 (0xFE000000, MAX_PATH_METRIC of RFC 5305) cannot be the metric of a link; the value is also not the 0xFFFFFF "last resort" value of Section 2.1. The rule for links below the first threshold therefore has no representable result.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-01964.1.4.2"The Bandwidth Metric MUST be set to the maximum metric value of 4,294,967,296."4,294,967,296 is 2^32 and does not fit the 4-octet metric; Section 2.2 gives 4,294,967,295 (0xFFFFFFFF) as the maximum link metric for OSPF.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-01974.1.3.1, 4.1.3.2"| Flags | Reserved |"In the IS-IS FADRB and FADBT sub-TLV figures the Flags field is drawn about 6 bits wide, while the text defines "Flags (1 octet)"; the Reserved field and the following fields therefore do not start on the bit positions the ruler shows. Meaning is clear from the text (1-octet Flags, 3-octet Reserved).editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13624.1.3.1, 4.1.4.1"When granularity_bw is less than or equal to Total_link_bandwidth, then: Metric calculation: (Reference_bandwidth) / (Total_link_bandwidth - (Modulus of(Total_link_bandwidth, granularity_bw)))"The formula is undefined for two values the encoding allows: a Granularity Bandwidth of 0 (0 <= Total_link_bandwidth always holds, so the "Modulus of (x, 0)" branch is taken, a remainder by zero) and a Total_link_bandwidth of 0 (a link advertising Maximum Link Bandwidth 0: either branch divides by zero). Only a zero Reference Bandwidth is excluded. The operands are IEEE 754 single-precision values in bytes per second, yet "the division used here is integer division" and "Modulus" are not defined for them (truncate each operand to an integer first, or compute in floating point and truncate the quotient; for a fractional granularity the results differ), so routers can derive different metrics for the same link, which breaks the "common understanding" that loop-free Flex-Algorithm forwarding relies on (RFC 9350 4).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13634.1.3.1, 4.1.3.2, 4.1.4.1, 4.1.4.2, 4, 5"If a Generic Metric sub-TLV with a Bandwidth metric-type is advertised for a link, the Flex-Algorithm calculation MUST use the advertised Bandwidth Metric and MUST NOT use the automatically derived metric for that link. / If only some links among the parallel links have advertised the Bandwidth Metric: - The Bandwidth Metric for such links MUST be ignored."The first sentence (repeated in every automatic-calculation section, in Section 4 "overrides this automatic computation" and unconditionally in Section 5 rule 1 "it MUST be used during the Flex-Algorithm calculation") requires the advertised Bandwidth Metric; the Interface Group Mode bullets that follow require the same advertised metric to be ignored when only some parallel links carry one. The text does not say that the Interface Group Mode rule is an exception to the MUST, nor how "parallel links" are delimited (per neighbour pair, per direction, per topology), so an implementation following Section 5 rule 1 and one following the bullets compute different metrics for the same link.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13644.1.4.1, 4.1.4.2"Length (2 octets): ... For this sub-TLV, Length is set to 14. / For this sub-TLV, Length is set to 2 + N*8 octets."Figure 10 (OSPF FADRB) has a 32-bit Flags / Reserved word followed by two 4-octet bandwidths, i.e. 12 octets of value; 14 matches no reading of the figure (Flags 1 + Reserved 3 gives 12; Flags 1 + Reserved 1 gives 10). Figure 11 (OSPF FADBT) has the same 4-octet Flags / Reserved word followed by N pairs of 4-octet threshold and 4-octet metric, i.e. 4 + 8N, not 2 + 8N. Neither text gives the size of the Reserved field, so a receiver validating Length against the figure rejects every conforming sub-TLV built from the text, and vice versa. Also in 4.1.4.2: "Metric value range (1 - 4,294,967,296 (0xFFFFFFFF))" gives 2^32 in decimal (0xFFFFFFFF is 4,294,967,295), the same slip RA-0196 records for rule 1.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-13654.1.3.2, 4.1.4.2"When the computed link bandwidth is greater than or equal to Bandwidth Threshold X and less than Bandwidth Threshold X+1: The Bandwidth Metric MUST be set to Threshold Metric X."The rules assume Bandwidth Threshold 1 < 2 < ... < N, but nothing requires the sender to order the thresholds or tells the receiver what to do when they are not ascending (or are equal, or are NaN / negative IEEE values). With unordered thresholds the intervals overlap or are empty, and the result depends on whether a receiver evaluates rule 1, rule 4 or rule 5 first. The labels "Minimum Link Bandwidth" (Threshold 1) and "Maximum Link Bandwidth" (Threshold N) also reuse the names of the advertised link attribute.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RFC 9885: Multi-Part TLVs in IS-IS

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-01993.2.1, 5"The key consists of the 7 octets of system ID and pseudonode number plus the set of link identifiers that are present."For an Extended IS Reachability MP-TLV the key includes "the set of link identifiers that are present", so a continuation part that does not repeat the link identifier sub-TLVs has a different key (system ID only) and, read literally, describes another link; if it repeats them, a part carrying only some identifiers (for example IPv4 but not Link Local/Remote) again has a different key. Section 5 requires replicated key information but does not say that every part MUST carry all identifier sub-TLVs, nor how a part without identifiers is matched when parallel links to the same neighbour exist.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-02005"The order of arrival and placement of the TLV parts in LSP fragments is irrelevant. / The first occurrence in the lowest numbered LSP is used."Placement is said to be irrelevant, yet the default conflict rule (inconsistent fixed part such as the metric, or a duplicated single-instance sub-TLV) is decided by placement. A sender that moves a part between fragments thereby changes which metric receivers use; the statement of irrelevance holds only for consistent MP-TLVs.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

   link identifiers are used, every part of the MP-TLV MUST carry

-----
   Without that rule, receivers either merge parallel links or split

RFC 3032: MPLS Label Stack Encoding

Depth: deep. Errata: 4 errata: 3 verified, 1 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 3270, RFC 3443, RFC 4182, RFC 5129, RFC 5332, RFC 5462, RFC 5586, RFC 7274, RFC 9017.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00462.3.2"Since an ICMP message is never sent as a result of"Overstates RFC 1122: only ICMP error messages must not be sent in response to ICMP error messages. An LSR generating ICMP for a labelled Echo Request that expires must still be allowed to send Time Exceeded.ambiguityerratum 982 (Verified), editorial
RA-00474.2"hex 8281 (MPLS)."The PPP protocol number 0x8281 is the MPLS Control Protocol (MPLSCP); 0x0281 is MPLS unicast.editorialerratum 2166 (Verified), editorial
RA-10513.5"If the IP datagram is not larger than 1280 octets, and it contains a fragment header, then a. Convert it into fragments"Step 4 makes an LSR fragment an IPv6 datagram in transit, which IPv6 forbids ("fragmentation in IPv6 is performed only by source nodes, not by routers along a packet's delivery path", RFC 8200 Section 4.5). Step 3 also sends a Packet Too Big for a datagram of 1280 octets or less that has no Fragment header; its MTU value (Effective Maximum Frame Payload Size minus N) is then below 1280, and RFC 8201 Section 4 requires hosts to discard such a message, so the datagram is black-holed without the source learning anything. The text also names a "Next-Hop MTU field", which ICMPv6 Packet Too Big does not have (its field is "MTU", RFC 4443 Section 3.2).contradictionnone: RFC has 4 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-10523.4, 3.5"1. Strip off the label stack entries to obtain the IP datagram. 2. Let N be the number of bytes in the label stack"N is defined right after stripping the received label stack, yet step 3b prepends "the same label header that would have been on the original datagram had fragmentation not been necessary", i.e. the outgoing stack after swap, push and pop. When the LSR pushes labels (or pops them), N computed from the received stack gives fragments, and a Next-Hop MTU, that are too large (or needlessly small). The intended N is the size of the outgoing label stack; Section 3.6 ("n is the number of labels that actually get pushed on along the path") supports that reading.ambiguitynone: RFC has 4 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-1051 (RFC 3032, Section 3.5; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   4. If the IP datagram is not larger than 1280 octets, and it
   contains a fragment header, then a. Convert it into fragments,
   each of which MUST be at least N bytes less than the Effective
   Maximum Frame Payload Size.

Corrected Text
--------------
   (Document update.) An LSR MUST NOT fragment a labeled IPv6
   datagram. If the datagram is too big, the LSR sends an ICMPv6
   Packet Too Big message whose MTU field is the Effective Maximum
   Frame Payload Size minus N, provided that value is at least 1280,
   and discards the datagram. A link whose Effective Maximum Frame
   Payload Size minus N is less than 1280 does not meet the IPv6
   minimum link MTU for labeled traffic.

Notes
-----
   RFC 8200 Section 4.5 restricts fragmentation to the source, and
   RFC 8201 Section 4 discards Packet Too Big messages reporting
   less than 1280. Step 3's Packet Too Big for a datagram of 1280
   octets or less without a Fragment header necessarily reports less
   than 1280.

Proposed erratum RA-1052 (RFC 3032, Section 3.4, 3.5; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   2. Let N be the number of bytes in the label stack (i.e, 4 times
   the number of label stack entries).

Corrected Text
--------------
   2. Let N be the number of bytes in the label stack that would be
   transmitted with the datagram had it not been too big (i.e., 4
   times the number of label stack entries of the outgoing label
   stack).

Notes
-----
   Applies to both Section 3.4 step 2 and Section 3.5 step 2. Step
   3b already refers to the outgoing label header; with labels
   pushed at this LSR the received stack is shorter than the
   transmitted one, and fragments sized with the received N exceed
   the link.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-05723.5.1.2.1""If the Message Type is < 0x8000 (high order bit = 0) it is an / error signaled by the Unknown Message Type Status Code.""Section 3.5 defines the first bit as the U bit and the Message Type as the remaining 15 bits, so a Message Type value can never be >= 0x8000; the test is on the U bit, not on the type. 3.5.1.2.2 repeats this for TLVs ("If the TLV type is < 0x8000"), where the type is only 14 bits (U and F precede it). RFC 5036 3.5.1.2.1/3.5.1.2.2 keep the same wording.contradictionnone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-05742.5.4""OPERATIONAL Receive Shutdown msg NON EXISTENT / Action: Transmit Shutdown msg and""LDP has no Shutdown message; shutdown is a Notification carrying the Shutdown Status Code (3.5.1.2.4). The figure also shows "Init msg or Timeout" / "or Timeout" transitions to NON EXISTENT from INITIALIZED/OPENREC/OPENSENT, while the table lists Timeout only for OPERATIONAL. The surrounding text also has "established established". RFC 5036 2.5.4 keeps the table and figure.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-05753.4.4.1""behave as if the containing message has traversed a loop by sending a / Notification message signaling Loop Detected in reply to the sender""For a Label Mapping, 2.8.2 ("signal Loop Detected status to the source") leaves the vehicle open, while Appendix A.1.2 (LMp.8, "Label Release ... Loop Detected Status code") answer a detected loop with a Label Release carrying the Loop Detected status, not with a Notification. The general hop-count rule in 3.4.4.1 does not carve out the Label Mapping case. Same sentence contains "it must must determine". Later RFCs: RFC 5036 (obsoletes RFC 3036) keeps the rule (Section 3.4.4.1); only the doubled word is fixed.contradictionnone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-0576A.1.2""LMp.21 Execute procedure Send_Message (Peer, Label Mapping, FEC, / PrevAdvLabel, SAttributes).""LMp.21 is reached only when LMp.18 found that no label mapping for FEC was previously sent to Peer, so PrevAdvLabel ("The label for FEC, if any, previously advertised") is undefined there. The step needs to allocate a label (as Send_Label does) rather than reuse a previous one. RFC 5036 LMp.21 keeps the text (adds only Note 13 on split horizon).errornone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-05774.1""- Message Types 0x0000 - 0x3DFF. Message types in this range are""The registry rules cover 0x0000-0x3FFF (IETF consensus, vendor-private, experimental) but the Message Type field is 15 bits, so 0x4000-0x7FFF has no allocation policy. For TLVs (14-bit type) the same ranges cover the whole space, so the omission is specific to messages. RFC 5036 4.1 keeps the ranges.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-05783.9""Hold Timer Expired 1 0x00000009 "Events Signaled by ..."""No subsection of 3.5.1.2 ("Events Signaled by Notification Messages") mentions hold timer expiry; 3.5.1.2.3 covers only "Session KeepAlive Timer Expiration" and 2.4/2.5.5 say only that the Hello adjacency is discarded when its hold timer expires, without naming the status code sent when the last adjacency goes and the session is closed. Later RFCs: RFC 5036 (obsoletes RFC 3036) keeps the status code without a procedure; recorded against RFC 5036 as RA-1060.ambiguitynone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-05792.9.2""- The LSR ignores LDP Hellos from any LSR for which a password / has not been configured.""Security gap: Hellos are UDP and are not protected by the TCP MD5 option, so this rule depends on source address only and does not authenticate the Hello; spoofed Hellos from a configured peer address still create adjacencies and trigger TCP connection attempts. TCP MD5 itself is weak (RFC 5925 replaces it with TCP-AO).errornone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point
RA-0580A.1""must send a label request if the conditions in NH.8 hold.""A.1.7 Note 4 should refer to NH.13 (NH.8 is the Label Abort Request step; RFC 5036 corrects it to NH.13). A.1.6 Note 2 "see LRq.3" should be LRq.5 (No Route is sent at LRq.5; LRq.3 tests MsgSource == Next Hop). A.1.15 TO.3 "Send_Label_Request (Peer, FEC)" omits the SAttributes argument used elsewhere. Typos: "[RF3031]" (2.6), "is is to be forwarded" (3.6.1.1), "along the LSR being setup" (3.5.8, should be LSP), "to its LDP signalling" (3.5.5.1, peer missing), "Ifnot" (LRq.3), "Is so" (A.1.1), "Label Label Request" (A.1.7), Host Address FEC described as "address prefix in the Prefix field" (3.4.1).editorialnone: RFC has 3 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0572 (RFC 3036, Section 3.5.1.2.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If the Message Type is < 0x8000 (high order bit = 0) it is an
   error signaled by the Unknown Message Type Status Code. If the
   Message Type is >= 0x8000 (high order bit = 1) it is silently
   discarded.

Corrected Text
--------------
   If the U bit is clear (0), it is an error signaled by the Unknown
   Message Type Status Code. If the U bit is set (1), the message is
   silently discarded.

Notes
-----

   Status note: RFC 3036 is obsoleted by RFC 5036; an erratum report
   against it may be held or rejected for that reason.

RA-05863.4""(tunnel termination), the iTTL is based on the tunnel type (Pipe or / Uniform) of the LSP that was popped.""Section 3 defines three models, but the pop rule covers only Pipe and Uniform; for a Short Pipe LSP without PHP the figure in 3.2.1 implies the Pipe rule (exposed header TTL), but the text does not say so. RFC 3478: Graceful Restart Mechanism for Label Distribution Protocol

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02013.3, 4"Once an LSR releases a label, the LSR SHOULD NOT re-use this label ... for at least the sum of the FT Reconnect Timeout plus Recovery Time / this document requires that labels not be re-used until at least the sum of Reconnect Timeout plus Recovery Time."Section 3.3 states the label hold-down as SHOULD NOT; Section 4 says the document "requires" it. The text also does not say which Recovery Time is meant (the value advertised before or after the neighbour's restart; a helper learns the new one only after reconnecting) nor whether the rule applies to labels released while no restart is in progress (the wording applies to every release towards a GR-capable neighbour).contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-02023.1.2"the LSR would search its MPLS forwarding state for an entry that indicates Label pop (means no outgoing label), and the next hop equal to the next hop for that FEC associated with the entry"For an egress that allocates a unique label per FEC the text says the FEC must be preserved, but the search criterion given is only "Label pop" plus next hop; unlike the corresponding paragraph of 3.1.1 (item (c) "has the same FEC") it does not say to match the FEC, so with several FECs sharing a next hop the entry found is not determined. The phrase "the next hop for that FEC associated with the entry" appears garbled.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-02032, 3.3"the LSR knows that the neighbor is capable of preserving its MPLS forwarding state across the restart (as was indicated by the FT Session TLV in the Initialization message received from the neighbor)"Which field indicates the capability is not stated: Section 2 says an FT Reconnect Timeout of 0 means the sender will not preserve its state, and a Recovery Time of 0 (meaningful only after a restart) means it did not. A helper must infer that "capable" means a non-zero FT Reconnect Timeout in the previous session. The start instants of the "lesser of the Recovery Time ... and Maximum Recovery Time" period at the helper are also not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-02044"LSRs that implement the mechanism described here are subject to to additional denial-of-service attacks"Doubled "to"; heading "Security Consideration" singular. The countermeasure cited is the TCP MD5 option of [LDP], since superseded by TCP-AO (RFC 5925) for LDP (RFC 7349 context); an update would cite both.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0201 (RFC 3478, Section 3.3, 4; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   To reduce this issue, this document requires that labels not be
   re-used until at least the sum of Reconnect Timeout plus Recovery
   Time.

Corrected Text
--------------
   To reduce this issue, Section 3.3 specifies that labels SHOULD
   NOT be re-used until at least the sum of the FT Reconnect Timeout
   plus the Recovery Time advertised by the neighbor.

Notes
-----
   The normative statement in Section 3.3 is SHOULD NOT; Section 4
   overstates it. It is also unclear which advertised Recovery Time
   applies.

Proposed erratum RA-0202 (RFC 3478, Section 3.1.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   In such case, the LSR would search its MPLS forwarding state for
   an entry that indicates Label pop (means no outgoing label), and
   the next hop equal to the next hop for that FEC associated with
   the entry

Corrected Text
--------------
   In such case, the LSR would search its MPLS forwarding state for
   an entry that (a) indicates Label pop (means no outgoing label),
   (b) indicates the next hop equal to the next hop for that FEC,
   and (c) has the same FEC as the one associated with the entry

Notes
-----
   Without matching the FEC, the search is ambiguous when several

RFC 4023: Encapsulating MPLS in IP or Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE)

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 5332.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-11958.1"At the tunnel tail, IPsec outbound processing recovers the contained MPLS-in-IP/GRE packet."The tunnel tail receives the IPsec-protected packet; removing the IPsec protection is inbound processing (RFC 4301 Section 5.2). "Outbound" is the processing the tunnel head applies earlier in the same section.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-11968.1"Thus, the implementation MUST support ESP will null encryption.""will" is a typo for "with". The requirement itself (ESP with NULL encryption, RFC 2410) is clear from context.editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-11971, 8"(... outside the scope of the this document) / The specification encapsulations do not ensure privacy."Section 1 has "the this document"; Section 8 has "The specification encapsulations", which reads as "The specified encapsulations". Neither changes the meaning.editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-11983, 4"(The use of the MPLS-in-IP encapsulation for MPLS multicast packets is not supported by this specification.) / MUST be set to the Ethertype value for MPLS Unicast (0x8847) or Multicast (0x8848)."Both rules were replaced by RFC 5332 Sections 6 and 7: protocol 137 is used "whether or not the encapsulated MPLS packet is an MPLS multicast packet", and 0x8847 is required for every unicast GRE destination, with 0x8848 only for an upstream-assigned top label under a multicast destination. Read alone, Section 4 lets a sender pick 0x8848 for MPLS multicast to a unicast destination, which an RFC 5332 receiver treats as wrong. The two sections are not consistent with each other either: Section 3 excludes multicast, while Section 4 provides a multicast codepoint. No erratum is needed, because RFC 5332 updates this RFC. This is a reader's note.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-11995.1"If IPv4 is used, then the tunnel MUST set the DF bit. / the minimum of (a) an administratively configured value, and, if known, (b) the discovered Path MTU value minus the encapsulation overhead."The requirement is put on "the tunnel" rather than the tunnel head that builds the IPv4 header. The Tunnel MTU is defined as a minimum that includes an administratively configured value, but the text does not say what applies when no value is configured, or when no Path MTU is known either (for example, the outgoing link MTU minus the overhead). Implementations can therefore start with different Tunnel MTUs and fragment or drop differently.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-12008.1"If automatic keying is implemented, IKE in main mode with preshared keys MUST be supported. / then the use of BGP's MD5-based authentication mechanism is satisfactory"Security gap: The mandatory key management is IKEv1 (RFC 2409, obsoleted by RFC 4306 and now RFC 7296), and TCP MD5 (RFC 2385) is called satisfactory although RFC 5925 (TCP-AO) obsoletes it. The IPsec architecture and ESP documents (RFC 2401, 2402, 2406) are only informative references, yet ESP support is a MUST whenever IPsec is used. The security guidance reflects 2005 practice and has not been updated. No erratum applies: this is outdated text, not a mistake at publication.errornone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-1195 (RFC 4023, Section 8.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   At the tunnel tail, IPsec outbound processing recovers the
   contained MPLS-in-IP/GRE packet.

Corrected Text
--------------

   contained MPLS-in-IP/GRE packet.

Notes
-----

   applies IPsec inbound processing.

Depth: deep. Errata: 2 errata: 1 verified, 1 rejected. Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 3032, RFC 4385, RFC 5085. Updated by: RFC 6423, RFC 7026, RFC 7214, RFC 7274.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum

RFC 6138: LDP IGP Synchronization for Broadcast Networks

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Informational. Updates: RFC 5443.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-05964, 5"the updating of the LSA with that link to the pseudonode is postponed until LDP is operational with all the LDP peers on that broadcast interface. / ... after LDP is operational with all neighboring routers on that subnet."The condition for releasing the link is stated two ways: "all the LDP peers on that broadcast interface" (generic text) and "all neighboring routers on that subnet" (OSPF and IS-IS text). These differ when an IGP neighbour on the LAN has no LDP session (LDP not enabled there, or the session down). Section 5 puts "LDP not being configured on some routers" out of scope, and no hold-down or maximum delay is defined (RFC 5443 has one), so with the "all neighboring routers" reading a single neighbour without LDP keeps a non-cut-edge LAN out of the LSDB indefinitely, and a neighbour that joins while the link is withheld restarts the wait. The text also does not say what happens when an LDP session to one LAN neighbour goes down after the link was advertised (withdraw the link again, or leave it).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-0597Appendix A, 4"An interface is considered a "cut-edge" if, during intra-area SPF ... there is no alternate path for the directly connected network. Alternately, a "cut-edge" can be detected by the last run of SPF if there is a lack of connectivity to the router-id of a directly connected peer via an alternate path."The two tests are not equivalent on a LAN with several routers: the first asks whether the network (pseudonode) is reachable by another path, the second whether one peer's router-id is; on a LAN some peers may be reachable by another path and others not. The text does not say which peer is tested, or whether all must be reachable. For IS-IS the router-id of the peer (system ID) and "Dijkstra's algorithm described in Section 16.1 of [OSPF]" are OSPF terms applied to IS-IS without mapping. With two-level IS-IS, whether the test is per level is not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-05987"If the directly connected path has a higher metric than an alternate path with Time to Live (TTL) greater than 255 hops"A path cannot have a TTL greater than 255; "an alternate path longer than 255 hops" (more hops than the maximum TTL) is meant.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

RFC 6370: MPLS Transport Profile (MPLS-TP) Identifiers

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-05996"the SAII is assigned to the end that allocates the PW label for a given direction, and the TAII to the other end. / the LSP from A1 to Z9 would be initiated with a label request from A1 to Z9 ... SAII = A1-{Global_ID::Node_ID::AC_ID}"For the A1-to-Z9 direction the PW label is allocated by Z9 (the receiving end, RFC 4447 downstream label distribution), so by the first rule the SAII for that direction is Z9's AII. The example assigns SAII = A1 for "the LSP from A1 to Z9" and calls the message a "label request"; RFC 4447 signals a PW with a Label Mapping, in which the sender's own AII is the SAII and the label is for traffic towards the sender (Z9 to A1). The two statements give opposite SAII/TAII assignments for the same direction. Also "The LSP from Z9 to A1 would signaled with" lacks "be".contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-06005.3, 7.2.2"For a co-routed bidirectional LSP signaled from A1 to Z9, the mapping to the GMPLS 5-tuple is ... Tunnel_ID = A1-Tunnel_Num / The MPLS-TP LSP_MEP_ID is: Node_ID::Tunnel_Num::LSP_Num"The co-routed Tunnel_ID contains Z9-Tunnel_Num, and Z9's LSP_MEP_ID is built from Z9-Tunnel_Num (7.2.2: "Tunnel_Num is the tunnel number unique to that node"), but the RSVP-TE mapping carries only A1-Tunnel_Num. With signaling, Z9's Tunnel_Num is not exchanged, so A1 cannot learn the MEP_ID that Z9 will use (needed for connectivity verification of mis-merge, Section 8) and the full Tunnel_ID is not known at either end. The text does not say how Z9-Tunnel_Num is assigned or communicated in a signaled environment.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
