RFC 7338: Requirements and Framework for Point-to-Multipoint Pseudowires over MPLS Packet Switched Networks

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Informational.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-06383.2, 3.3"Note: no special configuration is needed for non-Leaf PEs to drop that unwanted traffic because they do not have forwarding information entries unless they process the setup operation for corresponding P2MP PWs"The claim holds when the PW label is upstream-assigned and looked up in the context-specific label space of the P2MP LSP (RFC 5331), because a non-Leaf PE has no entry in that context. Section 3.3 explicitly leaves the choice between upstream- and downstream-assigned labels to the solution; with downstream-assigned PW labels carried on a shared P2MP LSP, a non-Leaf PE looks the PW label up in its own per-platform space, where the same value may be bound to an unrelated FEC, and can mis-deliver the traffic. The requirements therefore need either upstream assignment (or another context) whenever the P2MP LSP reaches PEs outside the PW, or a requirement that solutions prevent such mis-delivery. (Section 3.4.5 also makes VCCV per [RFC5085] a MUST while RFC 5085 is listed as informative.)ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 7361: LDP Extensions for Optimized MAC Address Withdrawal in a Hierarchical Virtual Private LAN Service (H-VPLS)

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 verified. Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02575.1.1, 5.1.2"The U-bit and F-bit [RFC5036] are set to forward if unknown so that potential intermediate VPLS PE-rs devices unaware of the new TLV can just propagate it transparently."With U = 1 a PE-rs that does not know the TLV ignores it and processes the Address Withdraw with an empty MAC list per RFC 4762, i.e. flushes all MACs except those learned from the sender ("flush-all-but-mine"). For the optimized procedure (N = 1, "flush-all-from-me") that is the complement of the requested action, not a harmless fallback; the document relies on "the assumption ... that the MAC Flush TLV is understood by all devices before it is turned on", but the U-bit choice makes a partial deployment silently do the opposite rather than fail. The rationale given (transparent propagation) does not fit LDP, whose Address Withdraw messages are regenerated per session rather than forwarded.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-02585.1.3"When optimized MAC flushing is not supported, a MAC Flush TLV is received with N = 0 in the MAC flush message"A receiver that does not support optimized flushing cannot interpret the TLV at all; the sentence means a TLV received with N = 0 (flush-all-but-mine, the RFC 4762 semantics), whatever the receiver supports. As written it ties the value of N to the receiver's capability.editorialnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-14233.2, 2, 3, 5.1.2, 5.1.3"Note that in the case of negative MAC flushing the list SHOULD be only the MACs for the affected MTU-s. / the MAC Flush TLV MUST be sent in an existing LDP address withdraw message with an empty MAC list"Section 3.2 says the negative ("flush-all-from-me") message SHOULD carry the MAC addresses of the affected MTU-s and describes an empty list only as the fallback. Section 2 defines a "MAC flush message" as an address withdraw "without a MAC List TLV", Section 3 says the solutions "are applicable only to LDP address withdraw messages with empty MAC lists", Section 5.1.2 requires the N = 1 TLV to be sent with an empty MAC list, and Section 5.1.3 tells a receiver of a message with "a valid MAC address list" to "ignore the option and deal with MAC addresses explicitly as per [RFC4762]". A sender following 3.2 therefore produces a message whose N flag every receiver ignores. Sections 2 and 3 also disagree on whether the empty list is an absent MAC List TLV or a MAC List TLV of length 0.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-14243"This is accomplished by sending an LDP address withdraw message -- a new message defined in this document -- from the PE that is no longer connected to the MTU-s with the primary PW."The address withdraw message with a MAC List TLV is defined in RFC 4762 (Section 6.2); this document defines only the MAC Flush Parameters TLV carried in it. The parenthesis, apparently carried over from RFC 4762, says the opposite, and conflicts with Section 5.1.2 ("sent in an existing LDP address withdraw message").errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-14255.2, 7.1"0x0407 | PBB B-MAC List Sub-TLV | [RFC7361] | / 0x0408 | PBB I-SID List Sub-TLV | [RFC7361] |"Erratum 4380 corrects the sub-TLV types in 5.2 to the one-octet values 0x01 and 0x02 that the Sub-TLV Type field of Figure 5.1.1 can hold, but Section 7.1 still registers 0x0407 and 0x0408 in the LDP "TLV Type Name Space", where they occupy top-level LDP TLV code points that no message carries, and no registry for the sub-TLVs of the MAC Flush Parameters TLV is created. RA-14265.2, 5.2.1"Value: One or a list of 24-bit I-SIDs that represent the I-component FIB(s) where the MAC flushing needs to take place. / If the PBB B-MAC List Sub-TLV is not included in a received message, then all B-MAC-to-C-MAC associations in all I-SID FIBs"The sub-TLV values are lists of 48-bit B-MACs and 24-bit I-SIDs, but the text does not say that each element occupies exactly 6 and 3 octets without padding, that Length must be a multiple of 6 (or 3), nor what a receiver does with a Length that is not. -------------

The PathTear BNF also makes the sender descriptor optional, while Section 3.1.5 says matching path state "must match the SESSION, SENDER_TEMPLATE, and PHOP objects"; whether a PathTear without a SENDER_TEMPLATE tears down nothing, or all senders of the session from that PHOP, is not said.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-10863.5"An element of blockade state with flowspec Qb is said to "blockade" a reservation with flowspec Qi if Qb is not (strictly) greater than Qi. ... Then Qb blockades Qi if for some component j, Qb[j] <= Qi[j]."With component-wise ordering, "Qb is not strictly greater than Qi" is false for Qb = (4,4), Qi = (4,2) (Qb >= Qi in every component and differs), so Qi is not blockaded; the example rule ("for some component j, Qb[j] <= Qi[j]") gives j = 1 and blockades Qi. The definition and its example disagree whenever the two flowspecs are equal in some component, which changes which reservations are left out of the merge (KR-II handling) and to which next hops an InPlace ResvErr is forwarded.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10873.2, Appendix B"If DstPort in a session definition is zero, all SrcPort fields used for that session must also be zero. ... Whether a node sends a PathErr / ResvErr for rule 2, and with which code, is therefore undefined. Rule 3 also calls Error Code 08 "Conflicting Sender Port" while Appendix B names it "Conflicting sender ports".ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10883.1.2, 3.1.6, 3.4"A ResvTear message may include a SCOPE object, but it must be ignored. (3.1.6) / May appear in a Resv, ResvErr, or ResvTear message. See Section 3.4. (3.1.2)"Section 3.1.2 points to Section 3.4 for the use of SCOPE in a ResvTear, but Section 3.4 defines SCOPE only for Resv and ResvErr messages and Section 3.1.6 says it must be ignored in a ResvTear. A wildcard-style ResvTear forwarded to several previous hops without a scope can then remove reservation state for senders that were outside the scope of the Resv it undoes.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-1089Security Considerations, 2.8, 3.11.5"Security Considerations See Section 2.8."Security gap: Section 2.8 covers message integrity, user authentication and IPsec data streams only. The protocol's own exposure is not discussed: any host can create path state in every router along a route with a single Path message (Router Alert, diverted under 3.11.5 "Packets received for IP protocol 46 but not addressed to the node must be diverted"), state that persists for the lifetime L and is refreshed by repetition, and wildcard reservations can be used to amplify state. No rate limits or state bounds are recommended.errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0639 (RFC 2209, Section 2 (PATH MESSAGE ARRIVES); type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Otherwise, turn on the Local_Only flag.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Otherwise, if the destination is unicast, turn off the Local_Only
   flag and set fPSB to point to the new PSB; for a multicast
   destination, turn on the Local_Only flag.

Notes
-----
   The multicast-specific steps 2 and 3 are the only places that
   clear Local_Only or set fPSB; step 4 dereferences fPSB.

RA-10914.3"An RSVP Integrity Challenge message will carry a message type of 11. ... An RSVP Integrity Response message will carry a message type of 12."Message type 12 was also assigned to the Bundle message by RFC 2961. RFC 3097 (which updates this RFC) moves Integrity Challenge and Integrity Response to 25 and 26. An implementer working from this document alone uses values that collide with RFC 2961. The RFC carries no "Updated by" pointer in its text, so the conflict is visible only through the RFC index.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10924.3"It is suggested that the cookie be an MD5 hash of a local secret and a timestamp to provide uniqueness (see Section 9)."The length of the Challenge Cookie is not stated in the text. The CHALLENGE object figure draws it as two 32-bit rows (8 octets), while the suggested construction (an MD5 hash) is 16 octets, and nothing says whether the object length may vary or how a receiver handles a cookie of another length. The pointer "(see Section 9)" refers to the References section; the cookie discussion is in Section 10 (Security Considerations). The sentence before also has an unbalanced parenthesis ("see Section 2.5.3 of [4]).") and the object description starts with "he CHALLENGE object". Later RFCs: RFC 3097 Section 3 (which updates this RFC) describes the cookie as 32 bits, a third size.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-10934.3, 7.1"Upon receiving an integrity Challenge message a sender MUST send an Identity object that includes the Kerberos ticket in the integrity Response message"Section 4.3 defines the Integrity Response as "<Common Header> <INTEGRITY> <CHALLENGE>" with no POLICY_DATA (Identity) object, while Section 7.1 requires one when Kerberos keys are used. A receiver that parses the Response strictly per Section 4.3 rejects it; the grammar should allow an optional <POLICY_DATA>.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10942.2, 4.2"List of last N sequence numbers received with this key identifier [REQUIRED at Receiving System]."The Key Identifier is unique only "for a given sender" (2.1), and the security association is identified by the Key Identifier together with the sending system's address. Section 2.2 and the reception rules key the replay state on the Key Identifier alone. Where several senders use the same Key Identifier (Section 4 allows one association for a whole subnet), replay state kept per Key Identifier would reject one sender's messages against another's sequence numbers. The state must be kept per (sending system address, Key Identifier).ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10953, 4.2"Each subsequent message must then have a larger (modulo 2^64) sequence number to be accepted.""Larger modulo 2^64" is not defined. A plain unsigned comparison never accepts a wrapped number; a serial-number comparison (RFC 1982 style, half the space ahead) is presumably meant, but then a receiver whose stored maximum is more than 2^63 behind (for example after a long silence with clock-based numbers, Section 3.2) treats every new number as old.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-10964.1, 4.2"(9) The digest is written into the Cryptographic Digest field of the INTEGRITY object."The field is named "Keyed Message Digest" in the Section 2.1 format; Sections 4.1 (9) and 4.2 (2) call it "Cryptographic Digest". Same field, two names.editorialnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-1092 (RFC 2747, Section 4.3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   It is suggested that the cookie be an MD5 hash of a local secret
   and a timestamp to provide uniqueness (see Section 9).

Corrected Text
--------------
   The Challenge Cookie is 8 octets long. It is suggested that the
   cookie be derived from a hash (for example, the first 8 octets of
   an MD5 hash) of a local secret and a timestamp to provide
   uniqueness (see Section 10).

Notes
-----
   The CHALLENGE object figure shows an 8-octet cookie, but the
   suggested MD5 construction yields 16 octets, and the reference to
   Section 9 (References) should be to Section 10.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum

The document does not require INTEGRITY when tears are exempted, nor discuss the PIN case.errornone: RFC has no errata
RA-06513.1, 3.4, Appendix A"An empty policy element of a certain P-Type is used to delete (rather than a replace) all policy state of the same P-Type. / 14= ERR_PD_MISS : Mandatory PE Missing (Empty PE is in the PD object)"An empty policy element is defined as an explicit delete in 3.4, but Appendix A treats "Empty PE is in the PD object" as the error case of a missing mandatory element, so a PDP receiving an empty element cannot tell whether to purge state or reject the message. Section 3.1 also gives no handling for a Data Offset that is smaller than the object header or points beyond the object.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-06522, 3.2, 4.3"PEP2 PIN PEP2"Figure 1 labels both boundary nodes "PEP2" (A should be PEP1, matching PDP1). RFC 2961: RSVP Refresh Overhead Reduction Extensions

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 5063.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02614.5"if ((int) old_id - (int) new_id > 0) { new value is less than old value; }"The wrap-safe comparison casts each 32-bit identifier to a signed int before subtracting. With 32-bit int the subtraction can overflow (undefined behaviour in C) and for operands on either side of 2^31 gives the wrong sign. The intended serial-number test (RFC 1982 style) is the cast of the difference, (int32_t)(old_id - new_id) > 0, computed on unsigned 32-bit values.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-02624.5"When a node is sending a trigger message, the Message_Identifier value MUST have a value that is greater than any other value previously used with the same Epoch / Note that the 32-bit Message_Identifier value MAY wrap."Once the identifier wraps within one Epoch no new value can be "greater than any other value previously used"; the MUST can only be read as "greater in serial-number arithmetic than the most recent value". The text does not say how far apart in-flight values may be (RFC 1982 requires less than 2^31) nor that the Epoch must change before reuse.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-02635.2, 5.3"When the use of this method is administratively configured, the destination address should be the well known group address 224.0.0.14. / When the destination address of the message is a multicast address, then identified information is added to the message in a MESSAGE_ID SRC_LIST object"The secondary (next-hop) method of 5.3 uses MESSAGE_ID LIST / MCAST_LIST objects, and 5.2 says Srefresh sent to the next hop "MUST NOT include any MESSAGE_ID SRC_LIST objects". When configured to send to 224.0.0.14 the destination is a multicast address, which the later 5.3 rule maps to SRC_LIST objects, whose group is "the message's destination IP address" (wrong for 224.0.0.14). Which object types are allowed, whether a Router Alert is carried (5.2 MUST for session destinations, SHOULD NOT for neighbours) and the IPv6 equivalent of 224.0.0.14 are not specified.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-02646.3, 4.7"/* acknowledged or no reply from receiver for too long: */ do any needed clean up; exit;"The behaviour after Rl unacknowledged transmissions is not specified: whether the state continues to be refreshed by standard refreshes (implied by 4.7, "followed by standard RSVP refreshes"), whether the neighbour should be treated as no longer refresh-reduction capable, and whether later refreshes of that state may still use Srefresh (whose entries the neighbour may not hold).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-02658, 4.5"No new security issues are raised in this document."Security gap: The out-of-order rule (4.5, "Out of order messages SHOULD be ignored, i.e., silently dropped") lets a forged message with the neighbour's addresses, the current Epoch and a high Message_Identifier cause subsequent genuine triggers to be dropped until the identifier catches up; Srefresh NACKs make the receiver resend full state (a small amplification). Both are mitigated only by the INTEGRITY object [RFC2747], which the security section does not mention.errornone: RFC has no errata
RA-02664.5, 3.3"Rapid retransmission rate MUST be based on the exponential exponential back-off procedures defined in section 6."Doubled word "exponential exponential". Section 3.3 "exactly one IP datagram, which is approximately 64K bytes" means the maximum IP datagram size. Section 4.1 uses "Only one MESSAGE_ID object MAY be included" as a limit (MUST NOT include more than one); receiver handling of two MESSAGE_ID objects is not stated.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0261 (RFC 2961, Section 4.5; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   if ((int) old_id - (int) new_id > 0) {

Corrected Text
--------------
   if ((int32_t) (old_id - new_id) > 0) {   /* old_id, new_id:
   uint32_t */

Notes
-----
   The expression as printed is not wrap-safe in C; the difference
   of the unsigned values must be computed first and then
   interpreted as signed 32-bit, as in RFC 1982 serial arithmetic.

RA-11129"Note that the facility backup method requires that a PLR and its selected merge point trust RSVP messages received from each other."Security gap: With facility backup the PLR and the MP exchange RSVP messages directly although they are not RSVP neighbours on a link (Path through the bypass, Resv / PathErr to the RSVP_HOP address, Section 6.4.3). Proposed erratum RA-1112 (RFC 4090, Section 9; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Note that the facility backup method requires that a PLR and its
   selected merge point trust RSVP messages received from each
   other.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Note that the facility backup method requires that a PLR and its
   selected merge point trust RSVP messages received from each
   other. Since a PLR and an MP are in general not RSVP neighbours
   on a common link, implementations that use RSVP message integrity
   [RFC2747] need security associations between every PLR and each
   of its possible merge points (selected by key identifier and
   sender address); without them, an MP cannot distinguish a
   legitimate backup Path from an injected one.

Notes
-----
   RFC 2747 keys are usually provisioned per interface or per
   neighbour; PLR
   MP pairs are neither. The text should at least state the need for
   PLR-MP security associations.

RA-067815.3, 8.3, 9.3"if a PPRO is received when the S bit is set to 0 in the PROTECTION object, the receiving node MUST return a PathErr message with the new error code/sub-code "Routing Problem/PRIMARY_PATH_ROUTE object not applicable"."A secondary LSP is activated by "a modified Path message with the S bit set to 0 in the PROTECTION object" (8.3, 9.3), while 9.3 tells the head-end to include a PPRO in the Path message of the secondary LSP. No text says that the PPRO must be removed from the activating Path message; a head-end that only flips S to 0 makes every PPRO-aware transit node reject the activation with "PRIMARY_PATH_ROUTE object not applicable", exactly when recovery is needed.contradictionnone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-067916.2, 19"Otherwise, this node MUST return a PathErr message with the new error code/sub-code "LSP Admission Failure/Bad Association Type".""LSP Admission Failure" is a sub-code (4) of "Admission Control Failure" (code 1); Section 19 registers the value as "Admission Control Failure/Bad Association Type" (5). The next sentence says "terminating nodes receiving a Path message with a PROTECTION object requiring association ... MUST include an ASSOCIATION object", which a receiving node cannot do; the requirement is on the Path message (its sender).errornone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-06806.2, 7.2, 5.1"This node MUST reliably send a Notify message, including the MESSAGE_ID object, to the other end-node (A or D, respectively). This (switchover response) Notify message MUST also include a MESSAGE_ID_ACK object"The switchover request carries "Notify Error/LSP Failure", but no error code/sub-code is given for the switchover response (6.2 step 2, 7.2 step 2), so a receiver cannot tell a response from a new request except by the MESSAGE_ID_ACK. For 1+1 unidirectional protection, Section 5 says "No coordination is required" and recommends the N bit "since no protection-switching signaling is assumed", yet 5.1 sets the O bit after a process that "assumes the tail-end node has notified the head-end node", with no mechanism defined.ambiguitynone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point
RA-068115.3, 15.4, 16"when the LSP Protection Type value is set to 0x02 (without Rerouting Extra-Traffic) / PRROs SHOULD be present"0x02 is "Rerouting without Extra-Traffic"; "PRROs" should be "PPROs"; 15.4 says "these n secondary working LSPs" for the secondary protecting LSPs P[1..n] and spells "SLRG"; Section 16 repeats "The ASSOCIATION object is used to associate LSPs with each other." Errata: Erratum 1935 covers "PRROs"; the other slips listed are not in any erratum.editorialerratum 1935 (Verified), editorial

RFC 5063: Extensions to GMPLS Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) Graceful Restart

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 2961, RFC 3473.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02775.3.1, 4.2"Received Path state containing a MESSAGE_ID object whose Epoch value matches the Epoch received in the most recent Hello message is considered as updated after the upstream neighbor has restarted."Hello messages carry no Epoch: the Hello grammar of Section 4.2 is <Common Header> [<INTEGRITY>] <HELLO> [<RESTART_CAP>] [<CAPABILITY>], and the Epoch of RFC 2961 is carried only in MESSAGE_ID objects of other messages. The rule for excluding already-updated Path state from RecoveryPath Srefresh messages therefore refers to a value the downstream neighbour does not have; the intended reference is presumably the Epoch of the MESSAGE_ID objects received from the restarted neighbour after its restart.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-02781, 4.5.1"the downstream RSVP neighbor MUST send a RecoveryPath message for each LSP associated with the restarting node for which it has sent a Resv message."The Introduction says a RecoveryPath is sent "for every Path message it has previously received from the restarting node"; 4.5.1 restricts it to LSPs for which a Resv was sent. LSPs whose Path was received but whose Resv was not yet sent (setup in progress at the restart) are covered by one text and not the other. Section 4.5.2.3 also says unresynchronised Path messages with a Recovery_Label "MUST be treated as being received during the Recovery Period" at its end, which reads as the opposite of the intended "as received after it" (i.e. as new setups per RFC 3473).ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-02795.1, 8"A new bit within the existing Flags field of each object is defined. ... 0x02: RecoveryPath Flag"The new flag in the MESSAGE_ID_ACK, MESSAGE_ID_NACK and MESSAGE_ID_LIST objects (fields RFC 2961 defines as "MUST be zero on transmission and ignored on receipt") is not mentioned in the IANA Considerations and no registry is created for these flag fields; 4.4.1 also calls the R bit both "RecoveryPath Desired" and "RecoveryPath Receive Desired".editorialnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0277 (RFC 5063, Section 5.3.1, 4.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Received Path state containing a MESSAGE_ID object whose Epoch
   value matches the Epoch received in the most recent Hello message
   is considered as updated after the upstream neighbor has
   restarted.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Received Path state containing a MESSAGE_ID object whose Epoch
   value matches the Epoch received from the restarted neighbor in
   any MESSAGE_ID object since the restart was detected is
   considered as updated after the upstream neighbor has restarted.

Notes
-----
   Per RFC 2961 the Epoch is carried in MESSAGE_ID objects; the

RFC 5420: Encoding of Attributes for MPLS LSP Establishment Using Resource Reservation Protocol Traffic Engineering (RSVP-TE)

Depth: deep. Errata: 2 errata: 1 held, 1 rejected. Status: Proposed Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 4420. Updates: RFC 3209, RFC 3473. Updated by: RFC 6510.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02835, 9"each transit LSR MUST examine the attributes in the LSP_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES object and MUST NOT forward the object without acting on its contents. / Subsequent instances of these objects within a Path message SHOULD be ignored and MUST be forwarded unchanged."Section 9 applies to both objects: a second LSP_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES object is to be ignored and forwarded unchanged, which Section 5 forbids (no forwarding without acting on the contents). A second instance can therefore carry required attributes that some transit LSRs silently pass on without examination, defeating the purpose of the 0bbbbbbb C-Num. Later RFCs: RFC 6510 Section 2 (updates RFC 5420) repeats the rule for subsequent instances ('SHOULD be ignored and MUST be forwarded unchanged') and its BNF admits repetition, so the conflict remains.contradictionnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-02843, 14"Prior to the change, the Length field indicated the length of the Value field only. After the change ... the Length field indicates the length of the whole TLV."The Length semantics changed incompatibly from RFC 4420 without a new C-Type or any means of detection; a receiver cannot tell an RFC 4420 encoding (for the 4-octet Attribute Flags TLV, Length 4) from an RFC 5420 one (Length 8) except by heuristics. The document gives no guidance on handling a Length that does not fit the object (e.g., Length less than 4 or larger than the remaining object).ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-02857.3.2, 7.2"To report non-compliance, an LSR MAY clear the corresponding bit in the Attributes subobject."The Attributes subobject is pushed by the reporting LSR itself with all bits defaulting to zero (7.3.4), so "clear" has no effect; the intended statement is that the LSR leaves the bit clear. Section 7.2 states the length constraints in lower case ("must be a multiple of four and must be at least eight") without saying how a receiver treats a violating subobject.editorialnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point

RFC 5495: Description of the Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic-Engineered (RSVP-TE) Graceful Restart Procedures

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Informational.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-06986"After a node restarts its control plane, it should ignore and silently drop all RSVP-TE messages (except Hello messages) it receives from any neighbor to which no HELLO session has been established."Hello is optional in RFC 3209 and the paragraph assumes every neighbor supports it. Read literally, a restarted node never processes Path or Resv messages from a neighbor that does not run Hello (or with which Hello is not configured), so LSPs through such neighbors can never be re-established. The rule needs to be limited to neighbors with which a Hello session existed before the restart (or that are known to support Hello), and to the period before the Hello session is established or a configured time expires.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-06995.2.1"After the restarting node restarts, it starts a Recovery Timer. Any RSVP state that has not been resynchronized when the Recovery Timer expires should be cleared."In RFC 3473 9.5.2 the Recovery Period is per neighbor and starts when the Hello session with that neighbor is re-established, using the Recovery Time that neighbor advertised. Here a single timer starts at restart, before any neighbor is known, which in the delayed-restart scenarios (the subject of this document) would clear state for LSPs whose neighbor has not yet restarted, contrary to the later advice to wait for the delayed neighbor with a configured Restart Timer.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

-------------

   established.

Corrected Text
--------------

   before the restart and to which no HELLO session has yet been
   re-established.

Notes
-----
   Avoids permanent isolation from neighbors that do not use Hello.

Proposed erratum RA-0699 (RFC 5495, Section 5.2.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------

Corrected Text
--------------

   the restart, the restarting node starts a Recovery Timer for the
   state shared with that neighbor [RFC3473].

Notes
-----
   Aligns with RFC 3473 9.5.2; this document states it does not
   modify those procedures.

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07005"LSP2 is soft preempted at R1 as it has a numerically lower priority value, and both bandwidth reservations cannot be satisfied on the R1-R4 link."In the example LSP1 has setup/hold priority 0 and LSP2 has priority 7. LSP2 is preempted because it has the numerically higher priority value (the lower preemption priority), consistent with 2.2 ("higher numeric priority TE LSPs are intrusively displaced ... by lower numeric priority TE LSPs"). The paragraph's end also refers to "the new TE LSP T2", a name not defined in the example (LSP2).errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07016.1"If this timer expires, the preempting node SHOULD send an RSVP PathTear and either a ResvTear message or a PathErr with the 'Path_State_Removed' flag set."Section 7 describes the same timer expiry as a hard preemption "by sending a fatal Path Error message, a PathTear message, and either a ResvTear message or a PathErr message with the 'Path_State_Removed' flag set", and 6.1 also describes hard preemption with a fatal PathErr. The 6.1 rule omits the fatal PathErr (RFC 5711 preemption error), so the head-end may not learn that the LSP was preempted rather than torn down. Section 7 also says an unrecognised flag should be passed in "the subobject", whereas the flag is carried in the SESSION_ATTRIBUTE object.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RA-07023.2"The TLV has meaning only in a Path message. / If the P-flag in the Actions field in the LSP_TUNNEL_INTERFACE_ID object in a Resv message is set"The IGP Instance Identifier TLV is defined for Path messages only, and Section 3.1.2 says the Actions field "has meaning only on a Path message" and "MUST be ignored on receipt" in a Resv. Two type values are defined in this document: / 1 IGP Instance Identifier TLV ... 4 IPv6 Numbered Component Link Identifier TLV"Four TLV types are listed, not two. The same TLV is also called "Target IGP Identification TLV" (3.2 heading), "IGP Identification TLV" and "IGP Instance TLV" (3.2 text), and "IGP Instance Identifier TLV" (3.1.2, 3.3, 3.4). RA-07043.6, 3.3"If the B-flag is set ... exactly one of these TLVs MUST be present in the LSP_TUNNEL_INTERFACE_ID object in both the Path and Resv / 38 16 Component link identifier missing"Error value 16 ("Component link identifier missing") appears only in the ingress (ResvErr) table. The egress table has no value for a Path message with the B-flag set and no Component Link Identifier TLV (or with more than one), so an egress must choose between 14 ("not valid") and 16 outside the listed set. Neither table covers a missing TLV that an egress could detect first.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-07053.4"multiple instances of the LSP_TUNNEL_INTERFACE_ID object are permitted in the same Path and Resv messages. The text does not say that an absent TLV counts as 0xffffffff when testing for "different" identifiers, nor how a Resv carrying several objects is matched to the Path objects (the TLV SHOULD NOT be sent in a Resv, Section 3.2, so the Reverse Interface IDs carry no identifier to match on). With two Path objects for two IGP instances, the ingress cannot tell which Resv object answers which.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-07063.7"this means that a node that does not understand the object SHOULD ignore the object but forward it, unexamined and unmodified. Thus, there are no issues with transit LSRs supporting the pre-existing or new Class Types"The class-number rule of RFC 2205 covers nodes that do not know class 193 at all. A transit node that implements RFC 3477 knows class 193 but not C-Types 2 to 4; RFC 2205 3.10 treats an unknown C-Type of a known class as an error. RFC 6510: Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) Message Formats for Label Switched Path (LSP) Attributes Objects

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 4875, RFC 5420.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-12343, 3.1, 3.2"When an LSP Attributes object is present before the first S2L_SUB_LSP object, the LSP Attributes object represents the operational status of all S2L sub-LSPs identified in the message. Subsequent instances of the object ... SHOULD be ignored"A Resv can carry several flow descriptors (several FILTER_SPECs, e.g. FF or SE make-before-break of the same P2MP tunnel with different LSP IDs). The RFC 5420 rule that this section quotes and keeps says the object "is associated with the FILTER_SPEC object that precedes it" and "Only one instance of the LSP_ATTRIBUTES object is meaningful within the context of a FILTER_SPEC object". The new rule makes an object placed before the first S2L_SUB_LSP (that is, in the first flow descriptor) apply to "all S2L sub-LSPs identified in the message", including those of the other flow descriptors (other LSPs), and makes the per-LSP objects of the later flow descriptors "SHOULD be ignored". The branch-node rule ("SHOULD be moved to follow the first received S2L_SUB_LSP object and then SHOULD be duplicated for ... each subsequent S2L_SUB_LSP object") has the same scope problem, and does not say what happens to per-S2L objects already present after later S2L_SUB_LSP objects of the same received Resv (ignored under the first rule, overwritten or kept under the second). The BNF of 3.1 and 3.2 never allows both a per-LSP object and per-S2L objects in one flow descriptor, while the text describes that combination.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12352, 2.1"LSP_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES objects are RECOMMENDED to be placed immediately after the SESSION_ATTRIBUTE object if it is present, or otherwise immediately after the LABEL_REQUEST object."The Section 2.1 BNF places [ <LSP_REQUIRED_ATTRIBUTES> ... ] [ <LSP_ATTRIBUTES> ... ] after [ <PROTECTION> ] [ <LABEL_SET> ... ] [ <SESSION_ATTRIBUTE> ], so without a SESSION_ATTRIBUTE the BNF order puts PROTECTION and LABEL_SET between LABEL_REQUEST and the attribute objects, not "immediately after the LABEL_REQUEST object" as the quoted recommendation says. Section 2 also says "Path message formatting is unmodified from the narrative description" while presenting a BNF that adds repetition ("...") to both objects.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-1234 (RFC 6510, Section 3, 3.1, 3.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   When an LSP Attributes object is present before the first
   S2L_SUB_LSP object, the LSP Attributes object represents the
   operational status of all S2L sub-LSPs identified in the message.

Corrected Text
--------------
   When an LSP Attributes object is present in a flow descriptor
   before the first S2L_SUB_LSP object of that flow descriptor, the
   LSP Attributes object represents the operational status of all
   S2L sub-LSPs identified in that flow descriptor (i.e., associated
   with the same FILTER_SPEC).

Notes
-----
   RFC 5420 Section 9, quoted in this section: "the LSP_ATTRIBUTES
   object is placed in the flow descriptor and is associated with
   the FILTER_SPEC object that precedes it". The same scope applies
   to the branch-node rule in the next sentences.

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02862.1"The size of the ERO subobject limits the size of the Hop Attributes TLV to 250 bytes."An ERO subobject Length is 8 bits and (RFC 3209 4.3.3) a multiple of 4, so its maximum is 252 octets; after the 4-octet subobject header (L/Type, Length, Reserved and R bit) at most 248 octets remain for Hop Attributes TLVs (each with its own 4-octet RFC 5420 header). 250 is not reachable.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-14312.2, 2.3"Unknown flags SHOULD trigger the generation of a PathErr with Error Code "Unknown Attributes Bit" as defined in [RFC5420], Section 5.2. / When the R bit is not set, a node MUST examine the attributes TLV present in the subobject following the rules described in [RFC5420], Section 4.2."2.2 asks for a PathErr on any unknown flag in an Attribute Flags TLV carried in the Hop Attributes subobject, independent of the R bit. 2.3 sends a node to RFC 5420 4.2 when R is clear, and RFC 5420 4.2 says the opposite: "An LSR that supports the Attribute Flags TLV but does not recognize a bit set in the Attribute Flags TLV MUST forward the TLV unchanged" (no error). With R clear (attributes "not required"), an implementation following 2.2 tears the LSP down for an unknown optional flag, one following 2.3 ignores it, which defeats the purpose of the R bit. Only with R set (RFC 5420 5.2) do the two sections agree.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RFC 8169: Residence Time Measurement in MPLS Networks

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-02873.1"The Length field of the PTP sub-TLV contains the number of octets of the Value part of the TLV and MUST be 20. / The 10-octet-long Port ID field contains the identity of the source port."The sizes do not add up. The Value as described is Flags + PTPType (4 octets) + Port ID (10 octets, the IEEE 1588 portIdentity) + Sequence ID (2 octets) = 16 octets, not 20; 20 is the value length plus the 4-octet Type / Length header, which the sentence explicitly excludes. Figure 2 in turn draws Port ID over one and a half rows (6 octets), giving a 12-octet value. Text, figure and Length value are mutually inconsistent, so two implementations can build different PTP sub-TLVs and reject each other's RTM messages.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-02884.4.1"| Type | Length |I| Reserved | / Type value (5) has been assigned by IANA in the RSVP-TE "Attributes TLV Space" sub-registry"TLVs in the LSP_ATTRIBUTES "Attributes TLV Space" use the RFC 5420 format with a 16-bit Type and a 16-bit Length; Figure 7 draws an 8-bit Type and an 8-bit Length. A parser following RFC 5420 and one following Figure 7 disagree on where the I bit and the sub-TLVs start. In addition, the I bit is a field of the single RTM_SET TLV (only one is allowed per object), but the procedure sets it in "the node's RTM_SET TLV" at each hop, so each node overwrites the indication of the nodes downstream unless the rule is read as "set if any node set it", which is not stated. Figure 10 is captioned "IPv4 Sub-TLV Format" for the unnumbered sub-TLV.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07073.2, 7.2, 7.3"the PTP sub-TLV in the Value field of the RTM message for an RTM message of the PTP Type (Type 1; see Section 7.3)."The RTM message Type is taken from the "MPLS RTM TLV Registry" (Section 7.2, Table 2), where 1 is "No payload" and PTP messages are Types 2, 3 and 4 (PTPv2 over Ethernet, IPv4, IPv6). IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 4090.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-12453.1.1, 3.1.2"MESSAGE_ID: A MESSAGE_ID object as defined by [RFC2961]."Figures 1 and 2 draw MESSAGE_ID as a single 32-bit word, but the text says it is a MESSAGE_ID object, which in RFC 2961 Section 4.1 is 12 octets (object header, Flags and Epoch, Message_Identifier). The figures therefore give a wrong size for the Extended Association ID (20 + 12 instead of 20 + 4 octets for IPv4), and do not say whether the RSVP object header (Length, Class-Num 23, C-Type 1) is included. The B-SFRR-Active figures draw RSVP_HOP and TIME_VALUES as variable-length objects with "//", so the embedded-object convention differs between the two figures.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12463.4.1, 3.4.2"Any previously received MESSAGE_IDs from the MP are activated on the PLR. As a result, the PLR starts sending Srefresh messages containing the specific Message_Identifier(s)"In RFC 2961 a node lists in its Srefresh the Message_Identifiers it generated itself for the state it sends (the PLR its Path-state MESSAGE_IDs from the B-SFRR-Ready object in the Path; the MP its Resv-state MESSAGE_IDs from the object in the Resv). The sentence ties the PLR's Srefresh to the identifiers received from the MP, and item 5 of Section 3.4.2 ties the MP's Srefresh to the identifiers "received from the PLR node". Read literally, each side would refresh with the other side's identifiers, which the receiver does not know as its own state and would NACK. The epoch to use (the one in the embedded MESSAGE_ID or the sender's current epoch) is also not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-12473.4, 3.4.2"For the Summary FRR-capable LSPs that are assigned to the same bypass tunnel, a common RSVP_HOP and SENDER_TEMPLATE MUST be used."A SENDER_TEMPLATE contains the LSP ID, which differs between LSPs, so a common SENDER_TEMPLATE is impossible; Section 3.4.2 (item 3) only replaces the tunnel sender address. The intended rule is presumably a common RSVP_HOP and a common tunnel sender address. The grouping rules also differ: Section 3 requires the same outgoing protected interface, the same bypass tunnel and the same tunnel sender address; Section 3.1.3 requires the same bypass tunnel and egress link and "not already rerouted", without the sender address.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-12483.1, 3.2"The Association Type, Association ID, and Association Source MUST be set as defined in [RFC4872] for the ASSOCIATION object."RFC 4872 defines the Association ID only for its recovery types (the LSP ID of the protected or working LSP); no value is given for the B-SFRR-Ready and B-SFRR-Active types, so senders will choose differently and the MP cannot tell whether the field is significant. The B-SFRR-Active Reserved field (3.2.1, 3.2.2) has no "MUST be zero / ignored" rule, unlike the B-SFRR-Ready one, and Section 3.3.2 says the MP "first ensures the existence of the bypass tunnel and that the Bypass_Group_Identifier is not already FRR Active" without saying what the MP does when the check fails (omit the object from the Resv, reject the LSP, or send an error).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-12495"Existing mechanisms for maintaining the integrity and authenticity of RSVP messages [RFC2747] can be applied."Security gap: RFC 2747 protects messages hop by hop. The B-SFRR-Ready object travels in the protected LSP's Path and Resv across every node between PLR and MP, and the B-SFRR-Active object in the bypass tunnel's Path across every node of the bypass; nodes that do not support the object forward it unchanged (Section 4), and any of them can alter group identifiers, the replacement RSVP_HOP or the tunnel sender address without breaking hop-by-hop integrity. One such object moves the state of a whole group of LSPs (Section 5 itself notes the larger impact). No end-to-end protection between PLR and MP is offered (see also RFC 4090 Section 9).errornone: RFC has no errata
RA-12503.2.1, 3.2.2, 4"Replacement RSVP_HOP object to be applied to all LSPs associated with each of the following Bypass_Group_Identifiers."The RSVP_HOP and TIME_VALUES objects follow the Bypass_Group_Identifiers in the figures, so "following" should read "preceding" (3.2.1 uses "preceding" for TIME_VALUES and "following" for RSVP_HOP; 3.2.2 uses "following" for both). Section 4 attributes the Extended ASSOCIATION object to RFC 4872, while it is defined in RFC 6780 (C-Types 3 and 4 of the class that RFC 4872 defines).editorialnone: RFC has no errata

RFC 5440: Path Computation Element (PCE) Communication Protocol (PCEP)

Depth: deep. Errata: 8 errata: 6 verified, 2 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 7896, RFC 8253, RFC 8356, RFC 9488, RFC 9756.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00745"All PCEP messages MUST be sent using the registered TCP port for the source and destination TCP port."Read literally a PCC could not use an ephemeral source port, and two sessions between the same pair could not coexist. RA-11219.16, 7.5"numbering them from 0 as the least significant bit."Section 9.16 states that the NO-PATH-VECTOR flags are numbered "from 0 as the least significant bit" and, a few lines later, that each bit is tracked by "Bit number (counting from bit 0 as the most significant bit)". The three flags are bits 29, 30 and 31, so the two readings put "PCE currently unavailable" at 0x00000001 or 0x80000000 on the wire. All other PCEP flag registries in this document count from the most significant bit, and later registrations in this registry (e.g., bits 10, 11, 19 to 28) assume that convention.contradictionnone: RFC has 8 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11227.4.1, 7.7, 7.15"In the case of the reoptimization of a TE LSP, the bandwidth of the existing TE LSP MUST also be included in addition to the requested bandwidth if and only if the two values differ."Section 7.4.1 (R bit) requires, for every non-zero-bandwidth LSP, that "the existing bandwidth of the TE LSP to be reoptimized MUST be supplied in a BANDWIDTH object", while Section 7.7 requires the Object-Type 2 BANDWIDTH "if and only if the two values differ", i.e. forbids it when they are equal. A PCE cannot tell from the absence of Object-Type 2 whether the PCC follows 7.7 (same bandwidth) or omitted a mandatory object (7.4.1). RA-11237.4.2, 7.15"If a PCC/PCE receives a PCRep/PCReq message that contains an RP object referring to an unknown Request-ID-number, the PCC/PCE MUST send a PCErr message with Error-Type="Unknown request reference"."Every PCReq introduces a new Request-ID-number, so read literally a PCE would answer every request with an "Unknown request reference" error and count it toward MAX-UNKNOWN-REQUESTS. RA-11247.2"the entire PCEP message MUST be rejected and the PCE MUST send a PCErr message ... Note that if a PCReq includes multiple requests, only requests for which an object with the P flag set is unknown/unrecognized MUST be rejected."The same paragraph requires rejecting the entire message and, in the next sentence, only the affected requests of a multi-request PCReq. Section 7.15 (Error-Types 3 and 4) supports the per-request reading ("The corresponding path computation request MUST be cancelled"). An implementation must choose, and the PCC cannot tell from the PCErr (which carries RP objects) which requests survived unless the rule is fixed.contradictionnone: RFC has 8 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11257.11"Most of the fields of the LSPA object are identical to the fields of the SESSION-ATTRIBUTE object (C-Type = 7) defined in [RFC3209] and [RFC4090]."The LSPA object carries Exclude-any, Include-any and Include-all affinities. RA-11267.3, Appendix B"Keepalive timer: minimum period of time between the sending of PCEP messages (Keepalive, PCReq, PCRep, PCNtf) to a PCEP peer."Section 7.3 defines the Keepalive field as the "maximum period of time (in seconds) between two consecutive PCEP messages sent by the sender", which is what the DeadTimer of the peer relies on; Appendix B calls it the "minimum" period. The document does not say whether a PCErr 1/1 precedes the Close, nor what "malformed" covers (bad lengths, objects out of grammar order, a second Open). RA-11287.4.1"Upon receiving a path computation reply from a PCE with the same Request-ID-number, the PCC SHOULD silently discard the path computation reply."The paragraph first requires a PCC that resends an unanswered request to reuse the same Request-ID-number, then says a reply "with the same Request-ID-number" SHOULD be silently discarded, without saying the same as what. Read literally, the PCC discards the reply to its own retransmission. The intent is presumably a second reply for a Request-ID-number already answered (the PCE "SHOULD treat the request as a new request", so a retransmission can produce two replies). It also conflicts with Section 7.4.2, which makes a reply to an unknown (already answered) request an "Unknown request reference" error rather than a silent discard.ambiguitynone: RFC has 8 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11297.13.3"the PCE sends a PCErr message for this request (see Section 7.2), the PCE MUST cancel the whole set of related path computation requests and MUST send a PCErr message with Error-Type="Synchronized path computation request missing"."When one request of a synchronized set is rejected (e.g., an unsupported object with the P flag set), the remaining requests are cancelled with Error-Type 7 "Synchronized path computation request missing", although no request is missing; it is not said whether one PCErr per cancelled request or one for the set is sent, which RP objects it carries, or whether REQ-MISSING TLVs are used. The SyncTimer value is only RECOMMENDED in Appendix B (60 s) and its expiry is "a protocol error" without a stated error code in 7.13.3 (Error-Type 7 in 7.15).ambiguitynone: RFC has 8 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11306.5, 6.8, 7.2, 7.15"For each reply that is bundled into a single PCReq message, an RP object MUST be included"Replies are bundled into a PCRep message, not a PCReq. Further: 6.8 "exactly one CLOSE object (see Section 6.8)" should cite Section 7.17 (already erratum 5382); 7.2 gives a maximum object content length of 65528 bytes, which cannot be carried in a message whose 16-bit Message-Length includes the 4-byte common header (the largest object is 65528 octets including its header, i.e. 65524 of content); 7.15 describes Error-Type 9 with "Error-value=1" while the tables in 7.15 and 9.12 define no Error-value for Error-Type 9; "Error-Type-1" is written for "Error-Type=1" twice. Errata: Erratum 5382 (held) corrects the Section 6.8 reference listed among the further slips; the PCReq / PCRep error is not in any erratum.editorialnone: RFC has 8 errata, none on this point (related: erratum 5382 (Held for Document Update), editorial); proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-1120 (RFC 5440, Section 7.15, 7.4.2, 9.12; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Error-value=2: O bit of the RP object set (request rejected)

Corrected Text
--------------
   Error-value=2: O bit of the RP object cleared (request rejected)

Notes
-----
   Section 7.4.2 ("O bit cleared") and the IANA registration in
   Section 9.12 ("O bit of the RP object cleared") agree with each
   other; Section 7.15 says "set".

Proposed erratum RA-1121 (RFC 5440, Section 9.16, 7.5; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   IANA manages the space of flags carried in the NO-PATH-VECTOR TLV
   defined in this document, numbering them from 0 as the least
   significant bit.

Corrected Text
--------------
   IANA manages the space of flags carried in the NO-PATH-VECTOR TLV
   defined in this document, numbering them from 0 as the most
   significant bit.

Notes
-----
   The same section gives both conventions; the choice changes the
   wire value of the three flags defined in Section 7.5. MSB-0
   numbering matches the other PCEP flag registries and later
   allocations.

Proposed erratum RA-1122 (RFC 5440, Section 7.4.1, 7.7, 7.15; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Also, for all TE LSPs except zero-bandwidth LSPs, when the R bit
   is set, the existing bandwidth of the TE LSP to be reoptimized
   MUST be supplied in a BANDWIDTH object (see Section 7.7).

Corrected Text
--------------
   Also, for all TE LSPs except zero-bandwidth LSPs, when the R bit
   is set and the existing bandwidth of the TE LSP to be reoptimized
   differs from the requested bandwidth, the existing bandwidth MUST
   be supplied in a BANDWIDTH object with Object-Type 2 (see Section
   7.7); when it is absent, the existing bandwidth is equal to the
   requested bandwidth.

Notes
-----
   Section 7.4.1 makes the existing bandwidth mandatory for
   non-zero-bandwidth reoptimization; Section 7.7 makes it present
   "if and only if the two values differ".

Proposed erratum RA-1123 (RFC 5440, Section 7.4.2, 7.15; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If a PCC/PCE receives a PCRep/PCReq message that contains an RP
   object referring to an unknown Request-ID-number, the PCC/PCE
   MUST send a PCErr message with Error-Type="Unknown request
   reference".

Corrected Text
--------------
   If a PCC receives a PCRep message, or a PCC or PCE receives a
   PCNtf message, that contains an RP object referring to an unknown
   Request-ID-number, it MUST send a PCErr message with
   Error-Type="Unknown request reference".

Notes
-----
   Section 7.15 limits Error-Type 8 to a PCC receiving a PCRep;
   Section 7.4.2 extends it to PCReq received by a PCE, where every
   Request-ID-number is new.

Proposed erratum RA-1124 (RFC 5440, Section 7.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If the PCE does not understand an object with the P flag set or
   understands the object but decides to ignore the object, the
   entire PCEP message MUST be rejected

Corrected Text
--------------
   If the PCE does not understand an object with the P flag set or
   understands the object but decides to ignore the object, the path
   computation request that contains the object MUST be rejected
   (other requests carried in the same PCReq message are processed
   normally)

Notes
-----
   The second sentence of the paragraph and Section 7.15 reject only
   the affected request; the first sentence rejects the whole
   message.

Proposed erratum RA-1125 (RFC 5440, Section 7.11; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Most of the fields of the LSPA object are identical to the fields
   of the SESSION-ATTRIBUTE object (C-Type = 7) defined in [RFC3209]
   and [RFC4090].

Corrected Text
--------------
   Most of the fields of the LSPA object are identical to the fields
   of the SESSION_ATTRIBUTE object (C-Type = 1) defined in [RFC3209]
   and [RFC4090].

Notes
-----
   Only the C-Type 1 SESSION_ATTRIBUTE (with resource affinities)

   Include-any fields that LSPA reuses.

Proposed erratum RA-1126 (RFC 5440, Section 7.3, Appendix B; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Keepalive timer:  minimum period of time between the sending of
   PCEP messages (Keepalive, PCReq, PCRep, PCNtf) to a PCEP peer.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Keepalive timer:  maximum period of time between the sending of
   PCEP messages (of any type) to a PCEP peer.

Notes
-----
   Section 7.3 ("maximum period of time ... between two consecutive
   PCEP messages") and Section 6.3 ("any PCEP message acts as a
   Keepalive message") contradict Appendix B and the UP-state text
   of Appendix A.

Proposed erratum RA-1127 (RFC 5440, Section 7.15, Appendix A; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If a malformed message is received, the receiving PCEP peer MUST
   send a PCErr message with Error-Type=1, Error-value=1.

Corrected Text
--------------
   If a malformed message is received during the PCEP session
   establishment phase, the receiving PCEP peer MUST send a PCErr
   message with Error-Type=1, Error-value=1. If a malformed message
   is received once the session is established, the receiving PCEP
   peer MUST close the session with a Close message with Reason=3
   (Reception of a malformed PCEP message).

Notes
-----
   Appendix A (UP state) and Close reason 3 handle malformed
   messages after establishment differently from Section 7.15.
   Error-value 8 ("PCEP version not supported") is registered in
   Section 9.12 but never described.

Proposed erratum RA-1128 (RFC 5440, Section 7.4.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Upon receiving a path computation reply from a PCE with the same
   Request-ID-number, the PCC SHOULD silently discard the path
   computation reply.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Upon receiving a further path computation reply from a PCE for a
   Request-ID-number for which a reply has already been received,
   the PCC SHOULD silently discard that reply.

Notes
-----
   Retransmissions reuse the Request-ID-number, and the PCE treats
   them as new requests, so duplicate replies are possible; the text
   does not identify the duplicate, and 7.4.2 treats a reply with no
   pending request as an error.

Proposed erratum RA-1129 (RFC 5440, Section 7.13.3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   the PCE MUST cancel the whole set of related path computation
   requests and MUST send a PCErr message with
   Error-Type="Synchronized path computation request missing".

Corrected Text
--------------
   the PCE MUST cancel the whole set of related path computation
   requests and MUST send a PCErr message, carrying the RP objects
   of the cancelled requests, with Error-Type="Synchronized path
   computation request missing".

Notes
-----
   Error-Type 7 is named for missing requests but is also used here
   for requests cancelled because another member of the set was
   rejected; the RP objects to include are not stated.

Proposed erratum RA-1130 (RFC 5440, Section 6.5, 6.8, 7.2, 7.15; type: Editorial):

Original Text
-------------
   For each reply that is bundled into a single PCReq message, an RP
   object MUST be included

Corrected Text
--------------
   For each reply that is bundled into a single PCRep message, an RP
   object MUST be included

Notes
-----
   Also: 7.2 "The maximum object content length is 65528 bytes" vs
   Message-Length (16 bits, including the 4-byte common header);
   7.15 "Error-Type=9, Error-value=1" vs tables without values for
   Error-Type 9.

RFC 5520: Preserving Topology Confidentiality in Inter-Domain Path Computation Using a Path-Key-Based Mechanism

Depth: deep. Errata: 4 errata: 2 verified, 2 held. Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07143.2.3"<request>::= <RP> <segment-computation> | <path-key-expansion>"Under the RBNF precedence rules, concatenation binds tighter than alternation, so the rule reads as "<RP> <segment-computation>" or "<path-key-expansion>", i.e. a path-key expansion request without an RP object, contradicting Section 4 ("the Path-Key bit of the RP object MUST be set"). The section is also introduced as "The format of a PCReq message including a PATH-KEY object is unchanged" although it changes the definition of <request>; and <segment-computation> drops nothing from RFC 5440 but omits [<XRO>] and other later additions, so it cannot be applied mechanically.ambiguityerratum 3582 (Verified), editorial
RA-07157.3"Bit Number Hex Name Reference 23 0x000017 Path-Key (P-bit) [RFC5520]"The "Hex" column gives 0x000017, which is the bit number 23 written in hexadecimal, not the value of the bit in the RP Flags field. A reader may take 0x000017 as a mask and set bits 27, 29, 30 and 31 (counting from 0 as in RFC 5440 7.4.1) instead of bit 23. Section 3.2.1 defers the position to this table.ambiguityerratum 1777 (Verified), editorial

Depth: deep. Errata: 3 errata: 3 verified. Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07162.1.1"4 Unnumbered Interface ID |X| Type = 3 | Length | Reserved | Attribute |"The type table and Section 4.1 assign 4 to Unnumbered Interface ID, 32 to Autonomous system number and 34 to SRLG (as in RFC 3477 and RFC 4874), but the subobject figures show Type = 3 for Unnumbered Interface ID, Type = 4 for the AS number and Type = 5 for SRLG. The Attribute descriptions repeat the wrong numbering: Interface is "valid only for subobject types 1, 2, and 3", Node "for subobject types 1, 2, 3, and 4", so they would allow the Node attribute on the AS number subobject (4 in the figure) and refer to a type 3 that does not exist.contradictionerratum 1775 (Verified), technical; erratum 2705 (Verified), editorial
RA-07172.2.2"If the path computation fails and a PCErr is returned with a NO-PATH object, the PCE MAY include an IRO to report the hops that could not be complied with"A failed path computation is reported in a PCRep carrying a NO-PATH object (RFC 5440 7.5; Section 2.1.1 of this document says so for the XRO); a PCErr does not carry NO-PATH. RA-07183.1.1"The format and definition of PKS when it appears as an XRO subobject are as defined in [RFC5520], except for the definition of the L bit. RA-00787.3.2, 7.3.4"Length (16 bits): indicates the total length of the TLV in octets."RFC 5440 7.1 defines TLV Length as the length of the value only. 7.3.2 (SYMBOLIC-PATH-NAME) says "total length", corrected by erratum 6289; 7.3.4 (RSVP-ERROR-SPEC TLV) has the same wording and no erratum, so it is still wrong in the RFC. Errata: Erratum 8370 (verified) already corrects Section 7.3.4 in the same way as erratum 6289 corrects 7.3.2.errorerratum 6289 (Verified), technical; erratum 8370 (Verified), technical
RA-00797.2"This means that the PCC may need to issue two PCUpd messages on detecting a wrap."A PCC sends PCRpt, not PCUpd; the sentence should say two PCRpt messages (acknowledging the last SRP-ID-number before the wrap).errorerratum 5376 (Verified), technical

RA-00816.4"<request>::= <RP> <END-POINTS> [<LSP>] [<LSPA>] [<BANDWIDTH>] [<metric-list>] ..."The grammar does not place CLASSTYPE relative to LSP; the erratum proposing an order was rejected because the fix needs a consensus document.ambiguityerratum 6627 (Rejected), technical
RA-11317.3.1"IPv4 Tunnel Endpoint Address: contains the egress node's IPv4 address, as defined in [RFC3209], Section 4.6.1.1, for the LSP_TUNNEL_IPv4 Sender Template Object."The tunnel endpoint address is a field of the LSP_TUNNEL_IPv4 SESSION object (RFC 3209 4.6.1.1), not of the Sender Template (4.6.2.1, which carries the sender address and LSP ID). RA-11325.8.1, 5.8.3, 9.1, 10.2"A PCC MUST send each LSP State Report to each stateful PCE that is connected to the PCC. / it MUST NOT advertise LSP existence and state to a PCE if the LSP is delegated to a PCE in a different group."5.8.1 and 5.8.3 require every report to go to every connected stateful PCE; 9.1 and 10.2 (repeated text) forbid reporting an LSP to a PCE in a different administrative group than the PCE holding its delegation, and 9.1 also asks for a knob to stop advertising LSPs not controlled by any PCE, and 5.6 lets local configuration choose the synchronised set. A PCC that implements PCE grouping cannot satisfy both MUSTs; the unconditional wording of 5.8.1 / 5.8.3 should be qualified by the policy of 9.1.contradictionnone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11335.7.1, 5.7.3, 6.2"If the PCE does not accept the LSP delegation, it MUST immediately respond with an empty LSP Update Request that has the Delegate flag set to 0."An "empty LSP Update Request" is never defined. The PCUpd grammar of 6.2 requires SRP, LSP and an ERO, and 6.2 gives an empty ERO its own meaning ("the PCE cannot find a valid path"), for which the PCC applies local policy that may "tear down the LSP". 6.2 also says "Each LSP Update Request that the PCC acts on results in an LSP setup operation". A PCC receiving a PCUpd with D=0 and an empty ERO must treat it as a delegation return (5.7.3), but the text does not say that the ERO / attribute content of such a message is to be ignored rather than applied, nor whether the refusal of 5.7.1 consumes an SRP-ID-number that the PCC must acknowledge with a PCRpt (6.2: "A PCC MUST respond with an LSP State Report to each LSP Update Request it processed").ambiguitynone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point
RA-11346.2, 5.8.3, 7.3.3"If the PCUpd cannot be satisfied (for example, due to an unsupported object or a TLV), the PCC MUST respond with a PCErr message indicating the failure (see Section 7.3.3)."The sentence requires a PCErr but points to 7.3.3, which defines the LSP-ERROR-CODE TLV carried in the LSP object of a PCRpt. 5.8.3 requires an unacceptable update to be reported "by including the LSP-ERROR-CODE TLV ... in the LSP object in the PCRpt message", and 7.3.3 says "When an LSP Update Request fails, an LSP State Report MUST be sent". Whether a failed update is answered with PCErr, PCRpt with LSP-ERROR-CODE, or both is left open, and no PCEP-ERROR value is defined for "update cannot be satisfied" (RFC 5440 error types 2 / 3 / 4 concern unsupported or unknown objects in general).contradictionnone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point
RA-11355.4"If this is not the case and LSP delegation or LSP Update operations are attempted, then a PCErr with Error-type=19 (Invalid Operation) and error-value 1 (Attempted LSP Update Request for a non-delegated LSP) (see Section 8.5) MUST be generated."The error value named for an attempted delegation (a PCRpt with D=1 on a session without U both ways, detected by the PCE) is the one defined for an Update Request on a non-delegated LSP (detected by the PCC), so the same code point is sent in both directions with different meanings, and the receiver of 19/1 cannot tell which case occurred. RA-11363.1.1, 3.1.2, 5.7.4, 5.7.5, 6.1, 9.1"Unfortunately, this visibility in terms of global LSP state may result in a number of issues for some demand patterns"The preceding paragraph says that LSP state is available only locally on each LER; "this visibility" should be "this lack of visibility". 3.1.2 "indirectly proportional to the amount of over-provisioning" should be "inversely proportional". Other slips: 3.1.1 "within in the network"; 3.1.3 "both PCC stability LSP Update rate capacity" (missing "and"); 5.7.4 says the State Timeout is "greater than" the Redelegation Timeout "(as MANDATORY)" while 5.7.2.2 requires "greater than or equal to"; 5.7.5 "redelegated immediately to the PCC" (returned to the PCC); 6.1 "LSP-ERROR-TLV" for LSP-ERROR-CODE TLV; 9.1 "multiple candidate PCEs for and a delegation preference".editorialnone: RFC has 9 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

-------------
   IPv4 Tunnel Endpoint Address:  contains the egress node's IPv4

   IPv4 Tunnel Endpoint Address:  contains the egress node's IPv4

Proposed erratum RA-1132 (RFC 8231, Section 5.8.1, 5.8.3, 9.1, 10.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   A PCC MUST send each LSP State Report to each stateful PCE that
   is connected to the PCC.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Subject to the policies described in Section 9.1, a PCC MUST send
   each LSP State Report to each stateful PCE that is connected to
   the PCC.

Notes
-----
   Sections 9.1 and 10.2 require a PCC that groups PCEs by
   administrative domain not to advertise LSPs to PCEs of another
   group, and allow an operator to exclude LSPs not controlled by
   any PCE; Sections 5.8.1 and 5.8.3 state the reporting obligation
   without these exceptions. The same sentence appears in both
   sections.

Proposed erratum RA-1136 (RFC 8231, Section 3.1.1, 3.1.2, 5.7.4, 5.7.5, 6.1, 9.1; type: Editorial):

Original Text
-------------
   Unfortunately, this visibility in terms of global LSP state may
   result in a number of issues for some demand patterns,
   particularly within a common setup and hold priority.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Unfortunately, this lack of visibility in terms of global LSP
   state may result in a number of issues for some demand patterns,
   particularly within a common setup and hold priority.

Notes
-----
   Section 3.1.1 describes the absence of global LSP state, so the
   sentence as written inverts its meaning. Section 3.1.2:
   "indirectly proportional" should read "inversely proportional".
   Section 5.7.4 "greater than" should match the "greater than or
   equal to" of Section 5.7.2.2.

Proposed erratum RA-0297 (RFC 8232, Section 3.2, 4.2; type: Technical):

-------------
   If State Synchronization is required, then prior to completing
   the initialization phase, the PCE MUST mark any LSPs in the
   LSP-DB that were previously reported by the PCC as stale.

Corrected Text
--------------
   If full State Synchronization is required, then prior to
   completing the initialization phase, the PCE MUST mark any LSPs
   in the LSP-DB that were previously reported by the PCC as stale.
   (Section 4.2:) During incremental State Synchronization, LSPs are
   not marked stale; an LSP deleted at the PCC is reported in a

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00823.4"of the TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 [RFC6460] and"RFC 6460 (Suite B profile) does not define these cipher suites; RFC 5289 does.editorialerratum 5180 (Held for Document Update), editorial
RA-11373.3 (Figure 5)"Figure 5: Both PCEP speakers support connection with or without PCEPS, but PCE cannot start TLS negotiation / Send Error Type=25,Value=3 (Failure, connection without TLS is not possible)"Section 3.2 defines Error-value 3 for a speaker "not willing to exchange PCEP messages without the solicited TLS connection" and 4 for one that is willing. A PCE that by the caption allows connections without PCEPS should send value 4, not 3; the figure shows the opposite and, with value 3, the PCC would not attempt the fallback that the caption's scenario implies.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11383.2"it MUST first try to establish PCEPS by sending a StartTLS message, and in case it receives a PCErr message from the PCE, it MAY retry to establish a connection without PCEPS"The fallback is allowed on any PCErr, including Error-Type 25 Error-value 3 ("connection without TLS is not possible") and 25/1 or 25/2, although the same section later ties the retry to the peer's stated willingness ("has learned in the last exchange the peer's willingness to re-establish the session without TLS"). The two rules give different triggers for a downgrade, and the broader one makes an injected PCErr (Section 7) sufficient.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-11393.4"Support for and negotiation of compression is OPTIONAL."Security gap: Section 3.1 tells implementations to follow RFC 7525, and RFC 7525 Section 3.3 says TLS-level compression should be disabled because of compression attacks (CRIME). Making its negotiation OPTIONAL without qualification conflicts with that recommendation for a protocol whose messages mix attacker-influenced and secret path data.errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11403.3, 3.4"Once the TLS connection has been successfully established, the PCEP speaker MUST start the OpenWait timer"Security gap: StartTLSWait ends when StartTLS is received and OpenWait starts only once TLS is up, so no timer covers the TLS handshake itself. A peer (or an unauthenticated client, Section 7 notes the higher handshake cost) can stall the handshake and hold the connection and its state indefinitely.errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-11415"it would consider it as an unknown message and would behave according to the existing error mechanism of [RFC5440], i.e., it would send a PCErr message with Error-Type 2 (Capability not supported) and close the session."RFC 5440 Section 6.9 sends a PCErr (capability not supported) for an unrecognised message but closes the session only when unknown messages arrive at MAX-UNKNOWN-MESSAGES or more per minute. The description of the existing mechanism adds a session close that RFC 5440 does not require. (RFC 5440 6.9 also writes "Error-value=2" where Error-Type 2 is meant.)errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11423.4"The DNS names and the IP addresses can be contained in the Common Name Identifier (CN-ID) [RFC6125] or the subjectAltName entries."RFC 6125 defines CN-ID only for DNS domain names and does not cover IP addresses; matching an IP address against the subject CN has no defined comparison rules (text form, IPv6 notation). With R=0 the request falls under Section 5.3, which mandates PCErr 19/8 for "a non-zero PLSP-ID and the R flag in the SRP object set to zero" and 6/9 for a missing ERO; with R=1 it is a deletion under Section 5.4. Error-value=8" is not limited to R=0, unlike the two checks before it, so read literally it also applies to deletion and take-over requests, which carry only the PLSP-ID. RA-11445.3, 8.5"it MUST send a PCErr message with Error-type=24 (PCE instantiation error) and Error-value=1"Section 5.3 names Error-type 24 "PCE instantiation error" three times, while the IANA registration in Section 8.5 (and the registry) names it "LSP instantiation error".editorialnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-1143 (RFC 8281, Section 5.3, 6; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If the PCC receives a PCInitiate message without a
   SYMBOLIC-PATH-NAME TLV, then it MUST send a PCErr message with
   Error-type=10 (Reception of an invalid object) and Error-value=8
   (SYMBOLIC-PATH-NAME TLV missing).

Corrected Text
--------------
   If the PCC receives a PCInitiate message for LSP instantiation (R
   flag set to zero and PLSP-ID set to zero) without a
   SYMBOLIC-PATH-NAME TLV, then it MUST send a PCErr message with
   Error-type=10 (Reception of an invalid object) and Error-value=8
   (SYMBOLIC-PATH-NAME TLV missing). (And in Section 6: "...
   includes just the SRP and LSP objects, with the R flag in the SRP
   object set to zero, and carries the PLSP-ID ...; the
   Error-value=8 and ERO checks of Section 5.3 do not apply to this
   request.")

Notes
-----
   Section 5.3 limits the non-zero PLSP-ID and missing ERO checks to
   R=0 but not the SYMBOLIC-PATH-NAME check; Section 6 defines a
   take-over request with a non-zero PLSP-ID and no ERO without
   stating its R flag. With R=0 it meets two Section 5.3 error
   conditions; with R=1 it is a deletion. Erratum 6301 fixes the
   grammar of this request but not these conditions.
