Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 verified. Status: Proposed Standard. Obsoletes: RFC 6006. Updated by: RFC 9353.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03073.13"The total PCEP message length, including the common header, is 16 bytes."The maximum PCEP message length is (2^16)-1 octets (16-bit Message-Length field), not 16 bytes. Fixed by erratum 5622; RFC 8623 Section 8 already uses the corrected wording.errorerratum 5622 (Verified), technical
RA-03083.7, 3.8"If the PCE does not understand the P2MP flag in the RP object, then the PCE would send a PCErr message with Error-Type=2 (Capability not supported) as per [RFC5440]."A PCE that does not understand the N bit cannot recognise the request as P2MP: RFC 5440 7.4.1 requires unassigned RP flags to be ignored, so a back-level PCE treats the request as P2P and fails, if at all, on the END-POINTS Object-Type 3 or 4 (an unknown or unsupported object, Error-Type 3 or 4 of RFC 5440), not with Error-Type 2. Section 3.8 then says such a PCE "SHOULD reject the request", which a back-level PCE cannot be required to do. A PCC therefore cannot rely on Error-Type 2 to detect a PCE without P2MP support.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-03093.10"To remove old leaves, the PCC MUST build a P2MP request using END-POINTS with leaf type 2. If no type-2 END-POINTS exist, then the PCE MUST send Error-Type 17, Error-value 1"A PCE cannot tell from a request without type-2 END-POINTS that a removal was intended, so the condition for 17/1 is not decidable as written. The conditions for 17/2 and 17/3 ("no END-POINTS with leaf type 3 or 4, or in the presence of END-POINTS with leaf type 1 or 2") are given only in prose and do not say which value applies when both type 3 and type 4 are absent. The same paragraph says "if a PCC receives a request", where the receiver of a PCReq is the PCE.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-03103.10"For old leaves, the PCC MUST provide the old path as a list of RROs that immediately follows each END-POINTS object. / Case 1 ... END-POINTS for leaf type 1 / RRO list"New leaves (type 1) have no old path, and Cases 2, 7, 8 and 9 show type-1 END-POINTS without an RRO list, but Cases 1 and 3 show an RRO list after the type-1 END-POINTS. The examples disagree about whether an RRO list may (or must) follow a type-1 END-POINTS object.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-03113.3.1, 3.5"By default, the path returned by the PCE SHOULD use the compressed format. / If the E-bit (ERO-Compress bit) was set to 1 in the request, then the path will be formed by an ERO followed by a list of SEROs."Section 3.3.1 makes the compressed format the default for replies regardless of the request, while Section 3.5 ties the compressed format to E = 1 in the request. It is not stated whether a PCE may return SEROs to a PCC whose request had E = 0, nor whether E in the reply must mirror E in the request.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-03123.13, 3.15"the receiver side of the fragmented message may start a timer once it receives the first piece ... Error-Type=18; Error-value=1: if a PCE has not received the last piece of the fragmented message"The timer value is not given, and only the PCE side (request fragmentation) has an error value; a PCC that does not receive the last fragment of a fragmented PCRep has no defined error (RFC 8623 later adds 18/2 to 18/4 for reports, updates and initiations only). "Response ID" in Section 3.13.2 is undefined; the RP object carries a Request-ID-number.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0308 (RFC 8306, Section 3.7, 3.8; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   o  If the PCE does not understand the P2MP flag in the RP object,
   then the PCE would send a PCErr message with Error-Type=2
   (Capability not supported) as per [RFC5440].

Corrected Text
--------------
   o  A PCE that does not understand the P2MP flag in the RP object
   ignores it (Section 7.4.1 of [RFC5440]) and is expected to reject
   the request because the P2MP END-POINTS Object-Type is not
   recognised or not supported (Error-Type 3 or 4 [RFC5440]). A PCC
   SHOULD NOT send P2MP requests to a PCE that has not advertised
   the P2MP capability (Sections 3.1.1 and 3.1.2).

Notes
-----
   The described behaviour (Error-Type 2) cannot be produced by a
   PCE that does not implement this document; the observable
   behaviour is governed by the unknown-object rules of RFC 5440.

   A generic "Inconsistent END-POINTS" error will be used if a PCE
   receives a request that has an inconsistent END-POINTS setting
   ... (and state the exact condition for each of Error-values 1 to

RFC 8408: Conveying Path Setup Type in PCE Communication Protocol (PCEP) Messages

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 8664.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03135"If the PCE does not support the intended PST, it MUST send a PCErr message with Error-Type = 21 ... Error-value = 1 (Unsupported path setup type) and close the PCEP session."A single request or update with a PST outside the negotiated set tears down the whole session, including all other LSPs' state and delegations; the text does not distinguish a PST that the peer never advertised (a protocol violation) from one that is advertised but not usable for this LSP. Later documents (RFC 9603 5.2.1, for SRv6) answer the comparable case with a per-LSP error and keep the session, so behaviour for unknown PSTs now differs by document.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-03143"If there are no sub-TLVs, then the TLV Length field MUST be equal to four bytes plus the size of the PST list, excluding any padding bytes."The Length counts the PST-list padding when sub-TLVs follow but not when they do not, and excludes only the padding of the final sub-TLV. Senders that count the final padding (the general RFC 5440 7.1 habit of padding the value) produce a Length that the strict check of this section rejects with 10/11 and session close.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 8623: Stateful Path Computation Element (PCE) Protocol Extensions for Usage with Point-to-Multipoint TE Label Switched Paths (LSPs)

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 9756.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-031512"Security considerations for the LSP instantiation mechanism are as per [RFC8231]."The LSP instantiation mechanism (PCInitiate) is defined in RFC 8281, not RFC 8231; RFC 8231 has no instantiation security text. The preceding bullet already refers to RFC 8231 for the other stateful operations, so the reference appears to be a copy error.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03167.1.1, 6.1, 7.2"the PCE MUST respond with a PCErr message carrying error-type 6 ... error-value 14 ("P2MP-LSP-IDENTIFIERS TLV missing") and close the PCEP session."A PCRpt with N set but no P2MP-LSP-IDENTIFIERS TLV requires the session to be closed, while the comparable omissions of the mandatory S2LS object (6/13, Section 6.1), the END-POINTS object (6/3) and an S2LS / LSP O-field mismatch (10/22, Section 7.2) only require a PCErr. No reason is given for the difference, and the text does not say whether the rest of the PCRpt (other state reports) is processed in the non-closing cases.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03176.1, 6.6.2"<end-point-actual-path-pair-list>::= [<END-POINTS>] [<S2LS>] <actual-path> ... / END-POINTS for leaf type 3 (modify) S2LS (O=UP) RRO list"The PCRpt grammar requires an <end-point-intended-path-pair-list> (each pair ending in an ERO/SERO) before any actual-path pair, but the Section 6.6.2 examples carry an END-POINTS / S2LS group followed only by an RRO list, and interleave RRO groups and empty-ERO groups. A strict RBNF parser rejects the examples; a parser built from the examples accepts messages the grammar does not.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03185.1, 6.6.1"Each P2MP TE LSP Update Request in a PCUpd message MUST contain all LSP parameters that a PCE wishes to set / The update message does not need to encode the full P2MP tree in this case."Section 5.1 requires a PCUpd to carry all parameters the PCE wishes to set (as RFC 8231 does for P2P, where the ERO replaces the path), while Section 6.6.1 shows an update carrying only the leaves of type 3 being changed. The text does not state that leaves absent from a PCUpd keep their current paths, nor how a PCC distinguishes a partial update from a full replacement of the tree.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03199"If the PCC supports the extensions as per this document (understands the N (P2MP-CAPABILITY) and M (P2MP-LSP-UPDATE-CAPABILITY) flags in the LSP object) but did not advertise this capability"The N (P2MP-CAPABILITY) and M flags are flags of the STATEFUL-PCE-CAPABILITY TLV (Section 5.2), not of the LSP object, whose N flag means "P2MP" (Section 7.1). The section also covers only a receiver that itself did not advertise the capability; a receiver that advertised it while the sender did not (the sender violating the first MUST NOT) is not given an error, and the trigger is "a PCUpd message" rather than a PCUpd with the LSP N flag set.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03207.1, 8"The receiver needs to wait for additional fragments until it receives an LSP with the same PLSP-ID and with the F-bit set to 0."No timer is given for "does not receive the last part" (18/2 to 18/4), and the text does not say whether messages for other LSPs may be interleaved between fragments, or what happens when a fragment of a second update for the same PLSP-ID (different SRP-ID-number) arrives before the first is complete.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-03216.1, 7.1.1"Error-value=3 ("END-POINTS object missing") (defined in [RFC5440]. / Tunnel ID: Remains constant over the lifetime of a tunnel."A closing parenthesis is missing in Section 6.1; in Section 7.1.1 the IPv6 TLV field list describes "Tunnel ID" a second time after "P2MP ID", apparently a leftover.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

RFC 8664: Path Computation Element Communication Protocol (PCEP) Extensions for Segment Routing

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 verified. Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 8408. Updated by: RFC 9756, RFC 9933.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00844.3.1 vs 5.2.1"If the F bit is set to zero (see below), then the NT field has no meaning and MUST be ignored by the receiver."The text is inverted (the erratum: when F is one, NT has no meaning). Even corrected it conflicts with 5.2.1, where a PCC "MUST validate that the Length field, S bit, F bit, and NT field are consistent" and answers F = 1 with NT not 0 with 10/11; the F flag text says "The F bit MUST be set to 1 if NT=0; otherwise, it MUST be set to zero". Errata: Erratum 6753 (verified) corrects "zero" to "one" but keeps "MUST be ignored"; the conflict with Section 5.2.1 remains, so the proposal below goes further than 6753.contradictionnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point (related: erratum 6753 (Verified), technical); proposed erratum below
RA-11456.3"If the PCEP speaker is a PCC, then the implementation SHOULD also allow the operator to view the values of the L-Flag and N-Flag that were sent"The SR-PCE-CAPABILITY sub-TLV (Section 4.1.2, IANA Section 8.9) defines only the N-Flag and the X-Flag; there is no L-Flag in it (the L-Flag of this document is the loose-hop bit of the SR-ERO subobject). Both bullets of Section 6.3 name the L-Flag where the X-Flag (unlimited MSD) is meant, and the X-Flag determines whether the MSD value means anything.errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11465.2.2"If the subobjects contain MPLS labels, then the PCC looks up the offset of the first subobject's label in its SRGB or SRLB. This gives the first SID."For an ERO of MPLS labels, the first label is treated as a label of the PCC's own SRGB or SRLB, whose SID determines the next hop, and only the remaining labels are pushed as given. The text does not say what the PCC does when the first label is in neither block (e.g., a dynamically allocated adjacency label, a binding label, or a special-purpose label that 5.2.1 says the PCC "MAY accept"), nor whether the label found for the first SID is pushed (prefix SID with the next hop's label) or popped (own adjacency SID). No PCErr value is assigned for an unresolvable first label (Error-value 14 "Unknown SID" is defined for SID indexes).ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-11474.3.1, 5.1, 8.4, Appendix A"At least one SID and NAI MUST be included in the SR-ERO subobject, and both MAY be included.""At least one SID and NAI" reads as requiring both; the intent (Section 4.3: "at least one of them MUST be present") is SID or NAI. The capability sub-TLV is also named three ways: SR-PCE-CAPABILITY (Sections 4.1.2, 8.5, 8.6), "PCE-SR-CAPABILITY" (Error-value 12, Sections 5.1 and 8.4) and "SR-CAPABILITY-TLV" (Appendix A); and Section 4.1.2 calls the sub-TLV a "TLV" ("The codepoint for the TLV type is 26").editorialnone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-0084 (RFC 8664, Section 4.3.1 vs 5.2.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If the F bit is set to zero (see below), then the NT field has no
   meaning and MUST be ignored by the receiver.

Corrected Text
--------------
   If the F bit is set to one (see below), then the NAI is absent
   and the NT field MUST be zero; the receiver validates NT, F, S
   and Length as described in Section 5.2.1.

Notes
-----
   Erratum 6753 corrects "zero" to "one" but keeps "MUST be
   ignored", which conflicts with Section 5.2.1 (a PCC MUST check
   that NT, F, S and Length are consistent and reject F = 1 with NT
   not 0) and with the F flag definition ("The F bit MUST be set to
   1 if NT=0; otherwise, it MUST be set to zero").

Proposed erratum RA-1146 (RFC 8664, Section 5.2.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If the subobjects contain MPLS labels, then the PCC looks up the
   offset of the first subobject's label in its SRGB or SRLB. This
   gives the first SID. The PCC pushes the labels in any remaining
   subobjects onto the packet

Corrected Text
--------------
   If the subobjects contain MPLS labels, then the PCC looks up the
   first subobject's label in its own label forwarding state (for
   example, its SRGB, its SRLB, or dynamically allocated adjacency
   labels) and forwards as that local label would be forwarded, with
   the labels in any remaining subobjects pushed below. If the first
   label cannot be resolved, the PCC MUST send a PCErr message with
   Error-Type = 10 and Error-value = 14 ("Unknown SID").

Notes
-----
   Adjacency SIDs are often allocated outside an SRLB; the text
   covers only the SRGB and SRLB and names no error when the first
   label cannot be resolved.

Proposed erratum RA-1147 (RFC 8664, Section 4.3.1, 5.1, 8.4, Appendix A; type: Editorial):

RFC 8685: Path Computation Element Communication Protocol (PCEP) Extensions for the Hierarchical Path Computation Element (H-PCE) Architecture

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 9756.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03224.2"If the domain path computation succeeds, the parent PCE sends a PCRep message ... Otherwise, it sends a PCReq message that carries the NO-PATH object to the child PCE."The negative reply is a PCRep carrying NO-PATH (Section 5 and Section 3.8), not a PCReq. The same paragraph calls the flag the "Domain Path Request bit", while Section 3.3.1 and the IANA registry name it "S (Domain Sequence bit)".errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03233.2.1, 4.1"If the PCE understands the H-PCE PCReq message but did not advertise its H-PCE capability, it MUST send a PCErr message with Error-Type=28 / the peer PCE SHOULD send a PCErr message to the child PCE and MUST specify Error-Type=28 (H-PCE Error) and Error-Value=1"Section 3.2.1 makes the 28/1 PCErr a MUST, Section 4.1 makes sending it a SHOULD (with a MUST only on the error values). Neither section says what happens to the request itself (whether it is also answered, or silently dropped) or whether the session stays up.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03243.2.1.1"the receiving PCE will ignore the H-PCE related parameters because they are all encoded in TLVs in standard PCEP objects."Not all H-PCE parameters are TLVs: the OF codes 12 to 14 (Section 3.4.1) are values of the OF object, METRIC types 20 and 21 (Section 3.5) are values of the METRIC T field, and the SVEC O bit and the NO-PATH-VECTOR bits are flags. A legacy PCE does not ignore an unknown OF code or METRIC type with the P flag set; Section 3.4.2 itself sends such cases to the RFC 5440 / RFC 5541 error procedures. The backward-compatibility claim is therefore true only for the H-PCE-CAPABILITY, H-PCE-FLAG and Domain-ID TLVs.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03253.4.1, 3.5"A path P passes through K unique domains {Dpi, (i=1...K)}. / If a domain is re-entered, then the domain should be double counted."MTD ("Minimize the number of Transit Domains") is defined by K, the number of unique domains including ingress and egress, while the Domain Count metric (T=20) counts a re-entered domain twice. The two quantities differ for paths with re-entry, and neither says whether ingress and egress domains count. The MBN formula counts domain transitions between consecutive links, which equals the number of border nodes only when each transition has a single border node (area boundaries), not for inter-AS links with an ASBR on each side, and it does not say to which domain an inter-AS link belongs.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-03263.2.2"Type=1: The Domain ID field carries a 2-byte AS number. Padded with trailing zeros to a 4-byte boundary."It is not stated whether the TLV Length includes the padding of the Domain ID (Length 8) or excludes it as RFC 5440 7.1 TLV padding (Length 6), nor whether Area-Len for type 4 counts octets of the area address. Both encodings are found.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-14323.4.1, 3.5"D(Li) = 1 if link Li and Li+1 belong to different domains; D(Lk) = 0 if link Lk and Lk+1 belong to the same domain. / B(P) = sum{D(Lpi), (i=1...K-1)}."MBN is named "Minimize the number of Border Nodes", but B(P) counts the places where two consecutive links of the path belong to different domains, i.e. domain transitions. In an area-based network a transition passes one border node (the ABR), but an inter-AS transition passes two (the ASBRs at each end of the inter-AS link), and the inter-AS link itself belongs to no single domain, so D() is undefined for it. The definition also mixes indices (D(Lpi) defined through D(Li) and D(Lk)). The Border Node Count metric (T=21, "number of border nodes crossed") is defined in words only, so B(P) and the metric can differ for the same path.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-14332.1.3"A PCC may be able to limit the number of domains crossed by applying a limit on these metrics. See Section 3.4 for details."The Domain Count and Border Node Count metrics and their use as bounds are specified in Section 3.5 (METRIC Object); Section 3.4 specifies objective functions.editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-14343.2.1"If both peers attempt to set the P-flag, then the session establishment MUST fail, and the PCEP speaker MUST respond with a PCErr message using Error-Type 1 (PCEP session establishment failure)"No Error-value is given; the Error-Type 1 values of RFC 5440 describe malformed or unacceptable Open messages and session parameters, none of which names a role conflict. The opposite case, two PCEs that both include the TLV with P clear (each expecting to be the parent, or neither asking), is not addressed, although "The parent PCE MUST include this TLV and unset the P-flag" makes it indistinguishable from a parent-to-parent session.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-14351.2, 3.3.1, 4.2, 9.2"This document uses the terminology defined in [RFC4655] and [RFC5440], and the additional terms defined in Section 1.4 of [RFC6805]. / Refer to Section 3.7 of [RFC7897] for details."The terminology of RFC 6805 and RFC 4655, and the ERO domain subobjects of RFC 7897 that carry the domain sequence requested by the S bit (3.3.1, 4.2), are needed to implement this document, but RFC 4655, RFC 6805 and RFC 7897 are listed as informative references. RFC 7897 Section 3.7 (ERO) exists, so the pointer is correct; its classification is not.editorialnone: RFC has no errata
RA-14364.1, 6.1.2"the peer PCE SHOULD send a PCErr message to the child PCE and MUST specify Error-Type=28 (H-PCE Error) and Error-Value=2 / If a parent PCE receives requests from an unauthorized child PCE, the request SHOULD be dropped."Section 4.1 answers a child the peer "does not want to act as the parent for" with PCErr 28/2, while Section 6.1.2 drops requests from an "unauthorized" child. The text does not say how an unwanted child differs from an unauthorized one, nor whether "dropped" means silently discarded (leaving the child to time out) or not computed but still answered.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03275"Range MUST be greater than 0, and it MUST be such that (Start-Assoc-ID + Range) does not cross the largest Association ID value of 0xffff.""Does not cross" does not say whether Start-Assoc-ID + Range = 0xffff is allowed. The range covers Start-Assoc-ID .. Start-Assoc-ID + Range - 1, so a sum of 0xffff ends at 0xfffe and is valid, and a sum of 0x10000 would include the reserved value 0xffff; an implementation reading "cross" as "reach" rejects a valid Open with 1/1.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03286.3.1"Any subsequent PCRpt message SHOULD include only the associations that are being modified or removed."Removal is signalled by the R flag, so a later PCRpt that omits an association means "unchanged". During State Synchronization the associations "MUST be included", but the text does not say whether an association missing from a synchronization report (for an LSP already known from a previous session or an incremental synchronization) means removal.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-03295.1"the local PCEP speaker MUST remove any associations that are not in the new operator-configured range (by disassociating any LSPs that are part of it (and notifying the PCEP peer of this change))."The rule applies to every session established with the Association Source, but the text does not say what happens when two sessions (for example to two PCEs) announce different ranges for the same source, or when the session later goes down (whether the configured associations come back).ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

-------------
   it MUST be such that (Start-Assoc-ID + Range) does not cross the
   largest Association ID value of 0xffff.

--------------
   it MUST be such that (Start-Assoc-ID + Range) is less than or
   equal to 0xffff, i.e., the last Association ID in the range
   (Start-Assoc-ID + Range - 1) is not greater than 0xfffe.

RA-03303, 4"If a PCE wishes to gain control over an LSP, it sends a PCUpd message with the C flag set to 1 in the SRP object."The PCUpd grammar of RFC 8231 requires a <path> (ERO and attributes) for each LSP; this document does not say what the ERO of a control request carries (empty, the current path, or anything) nor that the PCC must not act on it. RFC 8751: Hierarchical Stateful Path Computation Element (PCE)

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Informational.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07263 vs RFC 8231 7.3, RFC 8232 3.3.2"The SPEAKER-IDENTITY-ID TLV (defined in [RFC8232]) is included in the LSP object to identify the ingress (PCC). The PCEP-specific identifier for the LSP (PLSP-ID [RFC8231]) used in the forwarded PCRpt by the C-PCE to the P-PCE is the same as the original one used by the PCC."(1) RFC 8232 defines no "SPEAKER-IDENTITY-ID" TLV; its Speaker Entity Identifier TLV is SPEAKER-ENTITY-ID (type 24), and RFC 8232 3.3.2 defines it only for the OPEN object, so its use in the LSP object has no specification (the usage comes from the cited Internet-Draft). (2) PLSP-IDs are allocated per PCC (RFC 8231: unique per PCC for the lifetime of the session). A C-PCE that forwards reports from several PCCs on its single session to the P-PCE, keeping the original PLSP-IDs, will present duplicate PLSP-IDs on that session, where the P-PCE identifies LSPs (in PCRpt, PCUpd and delegation) by PLSP-ID. The document does not say that the P-PCE must key LSPs by (speaker identity, PLSP-ID), nor how a PCUpd from the P-PCE identifies the PCC.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07273, 5.6"To indicate the support for stateful H-PCE operations described in this document, a PCEP speaker MUST include both TLVs in an Open message. (3) / This PCEP speaker will also include both the TLVs; in this case, a PCEP peer could falsely assume that the stateful H-PCE feature is also supported. (5.6)"The capability indication required in Section 3 is the same signal sent by speakers that support stateful PCE and H-PCE separately but not the stateful H-PCE relay, as Section 5.6 admits, so the MUST conveys nothing a peer can rely on. No flag, error or fallback is defined; a C-PCE that delegates to a parent that does not relay simply loses control of the LSP until it revokes the delegation.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0726 (RFC 8751, Section 3 vs RFC 8231 7.3, RFC 8232 3.3.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The SPEAKER-IDENTITY-ID TLV (defined in [RFC8232]) is included in
   the LSP object to identify the ingress (PCC).

Corrected Text
--------------
   The SPEAKER-ENTITY-ID TLV (defined in [RFC8232] for the OPEN
   object) is included in the LSP object to identify the ingress
   (PCC); the P-PCE identifies an LSP by the pair
   (SPEAKER-ENTITY-ID, PLSP-ID), and the C-PCE includes the TLV in
   every LSP object it sends to or relays from the P-PCE (PCRpt,
   PCUpd, PCInitiate).

Notes
-----
   Without a composite key, LSPs of different PCCs with equal
   PLSP-IDs cannot be distinguished at the P-PCE.

RFC 8779: Path Computation Element Communication Protocol (PCEP) Extensions for GMPLS

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 9756.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03342.5.2.5"O: Old label. ... If the L bit is set, this bit SHOULD be set to 0 and ignored on receipt. / A LABEL-SET TLV with the O and L bits set MUST trigger a PCErr message with Error-Type=10 (Reception of an invalid object) and Error-value=29"The definition of the O bit tells the receiver to ignore O when L is set; the following paragraph makes the same combination an error (10/29). A receiver cannot do both.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03352.5.2.1-2.5.2.3"This TLV MAY be ignored, in which case a PCRep with NO-PATH SHOULD be returned, as described in Section 2.5.1."The address TLVs are defined for the Generalized END-POINTS object, and their "MAY be ignored ... NO-PATH" handling only fits a PCReq. RFC 9050 7.3.1 reuses them in the CCI object (PCInitiate / PCRpt), where NO-PATH does not exist; the handling there comes from RFC 9050 (31/5) and is not a property of these TLVs.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-07282.5.2.5"There MUST NOT be more than two LABEL_SET TLVs present with the O bit set. If there are two LABEL_SET TLVs present, there MUST NOT be more than one with the U bit set ... For a given U bit value, if more than one LABEL_SET TLV with the O bit set is present, the first TLV MUST be processed, and the following TLVs that have the same U and O bits MUST be ignored."The first sentences make two O-bit LABEL_SETs with the same U value invalid (and "If there are two LABEL_SET TLVs present" omits "with the O bit set", so read literally it also restricts the O-clear TLVs that "Several ... MAY be present"); the last sentence then defines processing for exactly that invalid case (first wins, rest ignored) instead of an error, and no error value covers a third O-bit TLV. A receiver cannot tell whether to reject (which error) or to process the first.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07292.6, 3"If the PCE does not assign labels, then it sends a response with a NO-PATH object, containing a NO-PATH-VECTOR TLV with the bit "No label resource in range" set. (2.6) / Error-Type 29 (Path computation failure) is used to reflect constraints not understood by the PCE ... If the constraints are understood, but the PCE is unable to find those constraints, NO-PATH is to be used. (3)"Section 3's rule sends a PCE that does not do label assignment (a constraint it does not support) to PCErr 29, while 2.6 sends it to NO-PATH with a bit that says the label range had no free resource, which misleads the PCC. Conversely Error-values 29/3 "Label set constraint could not be met" and 29/4 "Label constraint could not be met" describe exactly the "understood but cannot be met" case that Section 3 assigns to NO-PATH; neither value, nor 4/6, 4/9, 10/24, 10/25, 10/26 or 10/27 of Table 7, is referenced by any procedure, so when to send them is undefined.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07302.1.2"If the PCEP speaker supports the extensions of this specification but did not advertise the GMPLS-CAPABILITY capability, upon receipt of a message from the PCE including an extension defined in this document, it MUST generate a PCEP Error (PCErr) with Error-Type=10 ... Error-value=31 (Missing GMPLS-CAPABILITY TLV)"The trigger is described from the wrong side: the error name says the TLV is missing, which concerns the session where it was not exchanged, but the condition is that the receiver itself "did not advertise" and the message came "from the PCE" (a PCE receiving GMPLS objects in a PCReq is not covered). The intended rule is presumably: either speaker receiving any object or TLV of this document on a session where the GMPLS-CAPABILITY TLV was not exchanged in both directions sends 10/31. As written, a receiver that does not implement the extensions cannot apply it at all, and one that did advertise but whose peer did not is not covered.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07312.3, 2.4"BANDWIDTH object types 3 and 4 have a variable length. The 16-bit Bandwidth Spec Length field indicates the length of the Generalized Bandwidth field. ... Optional TLVs"Optional TLVs follow the variable-length Generalized Bandwidth (and Reverse) fields, but no padding is defined between them; PCEP TLVs are 4-octet aligned (RFC 5440 7.1). If a Bw Spec length is not a multiple of 4 (RSVP TSpec bodies normally are, but the field allows any value), the TLV start is undefined; the same applies to the Generalized Load Balancing object (2.4) and to the "Min Bandwidth Spec" fields whose figure shows them as one word each although they are variable.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03365.1"The Operator-configured Association Range MUST be set for this association-type to mark a range of Association Identifiers that are used for operator-configured associations"RFC 8697 5.1 makes the OP-CONF-ASSOC-RANGE TLV a SHOULD for types that are both dynamic and operator-configured and lets each Association Type define a default range; this document makes the range a MUST but defines no default. When a peer's Open has no range for the Disjoint type, the receiver cannot tell whether an Association ID it receives is operator-configured or dynamic, and so cannot apply the 26/4 / 26/8 checks of RFC 8697 6.4. "MUST be set" also does not say whether it is a configuration requirement or a requirement to send the TLV.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03375.3"If the OF-List TLV is included in the ASSOCIATION object, the first OF-code inside the OF object MUST be one of the disjoint OFs defined in this document."The OF-codes are inside the OF-List TLV, not an OF object (the OF object of RFC 5541 is a separate object in PCReq/PCRep).editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-03385.6, 5.1"In case of a PCRpt message, the PCE MUST return a PCErr message with Error-Type 26 (Association Error) and Error-value 7 (Cannot join the association group)."For a strict (T) group the same condition (disjointness impossible) gives 26/7 when the LSP is reported, but a PCUpd with an empty ERO when it arises from a network event. Whether a member whose join was refused stays delegated without a path, and whether a later topology change must re-admit it, is not said. An LSP reported in a PCRpt is already set up, so "cannot join" leaves the PCC with an LSP outside the group it was configured for.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RA-03405.5.1, 7.3"Also, the CC-ID is unique in each PCEP session (5.5.1) / the value is unique within the scope of the PCE and is constant for the lifetime of a PCEP session. With re-delegation (5.5.5) a new PCE takes over instructions by CC-ID, so the CC-ID of one PCE can collide with one a second PCE already uses on the same PCC; no error is defined for a CC-ID that is already in use with different content.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

(6.1)"Section 5.5.1 lets the O bit determine the role, while 6.1 checks the O bit against the role (31/3) and says the role is identified via the addresses in the LSP-IDENTIFIERS TLV. Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 8253.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-12513"MUST prefer to negotiate the latest version of the TLS protocol; see Section 4.2.1 of [RFC9846]. / Appendix E.5 of [RFC9846] requires applications not use early data without a profile that defines its use."The section references into RFC 9846 follow the numbering of RFC 8446. In RFC 9846, Section 4.2.1 is "Cryptographic Negotiation" (version negotiation is 4.3.1, "Supported Versions"), Appendix E.5 is "Security Restrictions Related to Backward Compatibility" (the requirement "Application protocols MUST NOT use 0-RTT data without a profile that defines its use" is in Appendix F.5, "Replay Attacks on 0-RTT"), and the first NOTE cites "Appendix F.5" for "TLS 1.3 can be used without early data", which F.5 does not say (Section 2.3 / 4.3.10 describe early data as optional). In RFC 8446, 4.2.1 was "Supported Versions" and E.5 "Replay Attacks on 0-RTT".errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12521, 3"All other provisions set forth in [RFC8253] are unchanged, including connection initiation, message framing, connection closure, certificate validation, peer identity, and failure handling."Keeping RFC 8253 3.4 step 1 unchanged keeps "Immediately negotiate a TLS session according to [RFC5246]" and the mandatory-to-implement TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, a TLS 1.2 cipher suite that cannot be negotiated in TLS 1.3 (RFC 9846 B.4: TLS 1.2 suites "cannot be used with TLS 1.3"). Together with the new rule that implementations "MUST prefer to negotiate the latest version", it is unclear whether a PCEPS implementation that supports only TLS 1.3 is compliant (8253 allows "TLS v1.2 or later") or whether TLS 1.2 support with that suite remains required. "The latest version" is also not qualified as the latest version supported by both peers and permitted by local policy. RFC 5246, cited normatively, is obsoleted by RFC 9846 of the same date.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

RFC 2710: Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) for IPv6

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 3590, RFC 3810, RFC 9777.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07503, 5, 6, 9"To be valid, the Report message MUST come from a link-local IPv6 Source Address, be at least 24 octets long, and have a correct MLD checksum."Every message must carry a link-local source, but a node joining its solicited-node group for Duplicate Address Detection has no usable link-local address yet, and Section 5 requires Reports for solicited-node addresses; the document does not say which source such a Report uses or whether a router accepts it (RFC 3590 later updated this RFC to allow the unspecified address). The receive validity rules also omit the Hop Limit 1 and Router Alert conditions that Section 3 imposes on senders, so an off-link Report with a spoofed link-local source and Hop Limit > 1 is "valid". Section 9 relies on the link-local check alone to defend against off-link forgery. Later RFCs: RFC 3590 Section 4 (updates RFC 2710) settles the main point: Reports and Done messages are sent from the unspecified address when no link-local address is available, and routers silently discard them. The receive checks (Hop Limit 1, Router Alert) are not addressed.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-07516"This event is significant only in the "Listerners Present" state and when the router is a Querier.""Listerners" for "Listeners"; "Multicast- Address-Specific" (Section 5) has a stray space; "link-layer multicast address that can be generated" (Section 4) should be plural.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

RFC 3590: Source Address Selection for the Multicast Listener Discovery (MLD) Protocol

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 2710.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-14374, 5, 6"For hosts and routers, all received MLD messages from an unspecified source address are silently discarded. This is the required behavior from [RFC 2710] and is not changed by this document. (6) / these messages will be dropped if the implementation does not consider the unspecified address to be link-local in scope. (5)"Section 6 states that discarding MLD messages from :: is required by RFC 2710 for hosts and routers, but Section 5 says the treatment by RFC 2710 implementations "is dependent upon how the implementation treats the unspecified address", i.e. not required. Section 4 gives receive rules only for Queries (any node) and for Reports / Done at routers; it does not say that a host must ignore a Report from :: for MLDv1 report suppression (RFC 2710 4: a host that hears another host's Report for a group cancels its own). A host that suppresses its Report on hearing a :: Report from a node in DAD, while the router discards that Report, leaves the group without a recorded listener until the next Query cycle. The "no new security impacts" conclusion rests on the Section 6 statement.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-14383, 5"MLD reports are to be sent using an unspecified source address prior to DAD being started (3) / RFC 2710 implementations discarding these packets will have no affect on the packet's sender (5)"Section 3 places the :: Reports "prior to DAD being started", while the first paragraph of Section 3 and Section 4 tie them to the period when no valid link-local address exists (during DAD of the link-local address). "no affect" should be "no effect"; "The discrepancies ... has led" should be "have led".editorialnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below

Proposed erratum RA-1437 (RFC 3590, Section 4, 5, 6; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   For hosts and routers, all received MLD messages from an
   unspecified source address are silently discarded.  This is the
   required behavior from [RFC 2710] and is not changed by this
   document.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Routers MUST silently discard all received MLD messages from the
   unspecified address, and hosts MUST silently discard Queries from
   the unspecified address and MUST NOT use a Report from the
   unspecified address to suppress their own Reports.

Notes
-----
   Section 5 states that RFC 2710 implementations may or may not
   drop such messages. A Report sent from "::" during DAD can cancel
   another host's pending Report while being discarded by the
   router.

Proposed erratum RA-1438 (RFC 3590, Section 3, 5; type: Editorial):

Original Text
-------------
   This document fixes this problem by specifying that MLD reports
   are to be sent using an unspecified source address prior to DAD
   being started

Corrected Text
--------------
   This document fixes this problem by specifying that MLD reports
   are to be sent using the unspecified source address while no
   valid link-local address is available (i.e., before and during
   DAD of the link-local address)

Notes
-----
   Section 4 is the normative rule; Section 3 should match it.

RFC 4604: Using Internet Group Management Protocol Version 3 (IGMPv3) and Multicast Listener Discovery Protocol Version 2 (MLDv2) for Source-Specific

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 3376, RFC 3810.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07582.2.3, 3.6"A router compliant with this document would never generate an IGMPv1, IGMPv2, or MLDv1 query for an address in the SSM range; thus, this situation only occurs either if the router is not SSM-aware, or if the host and the router disagree about the SSM address range"Section 2.2.3 is about IGMPv1 Queries and IGMPv2 / MLDv1 General Queries, which carry no group address, so "a query for an address in the SSM range" does not describe them, and a host reverts the whole interface to the older version on receiving one. Under RFC 3376 7.3.1 / RFC 3810 8.3.1 an SSM-aware router MUST query with the lowest version present on the link, so a third, compliant case (an older-version router on the link, Section 3.6) also makes hosts revert and lose SSM service. Section 3 has no rule that forbids SSM-aware routers from sending older-version General Queries, and the host rule "SHOULD log an error if it receives an IGMPv1, IGMPv2, or MLDv1 query for an SSM address" cannot apply to General Queries.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07592, 8"The 232/8 IPv4 address range is currently allocated for SSM by IANA [IANA-ALLOCATION]."The reference list names this entry [IANA-ALLOC]; the citation tag does not match. The reference sections are numbered 6 and 8 (there is no section 7).editorialnone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0758 (RFC 4604, Section 2.2.3, 3.6; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   A router compliant with this document would never generate an
   IGMPv1, IGMPv2, or MLDv1 query for an address in the SSM range;
   thus, this situation only occurs either if the router is not
   SSM-aware, or if the host and the router disagree about the SSM
   address range (for instance, if they have inconsistent manual
   configurations).

Corrected Text
--------------
   A router compliant with this document would never generate an
   IGMPv2 or MLDv1 Group-Specific Query for an address in the SSM
   range. A host also reverts to older-version mode on receiving an
   IGMPv1 Query or an IGMPv2 or MLDv1 General Query, which a
   compliant router sends when an older-version router is present on
   the link (Section 3.6); SSM service is then lost on that link.

Notes
-----
   The "never generate" claim holds for group-specific queries only;
   General Queries are interface-wide and are mandated in
   compatibility mode by RFC 3376 7.3.1 and RFC 3810 8.3.1.

RFC 4610: Anycast-RP Using Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM)

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07623, 4, 5.1"a source should be considered internal to a domain when it is discovered by an Anycast-RP through a received Register message, regardless of whether the Register message was sent by a DR, another Anycast-RP member, or the router itself."Sections 3 and 4 describe copying only for a Register "received from an IP address not in the Anycast-RP list" sent by a remote DR. The case of a source directly connected to a member of the Anycast-RP set, where that member is also the DR, is not described: under RFC 4601 / 7761 a DR that is itself the RP does not send a Register, so no Register is "received" and no copies reach the other members, whose receivers then never learn the source. Section 5.1's "or the router itself" implies that the member originates Registers (to the other members) for such sources, but no rule says so.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07633"If the Register is not addressed to the Anycast-RP address, an error has occurred and it should be rate-limited logged."It is not said whether such a Register (from a non-member, addressed to a member's own address) is still processed as an ordinary Register, dropped, or processed but not copied to the other members.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-07644"An implementation MUST safeguard against inconsistently configured Anycast-RP sets in each RP by copying the Time to Live (TTL) from a Register message to the Register messages it copies and sends to other RPs."The TTL meant is presumably that of the outer (unicast) IP header of the received Register; whether it is copied as received or decremented first, and what happens when it reaches 1, is not stated. Copying it unchanged bounds a loop only through the hop-by-hop decrement between RPs.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-0762 (RFC 4610, Section 3, 4, 5.1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   o RP1 is configured with RP2 and RP3's IP address.  Since the
   Register message did not come from one of the RPs in the
   anycast-RP set, RP1 assumes the packet came from a DR.

Corrected Text
--------------
   (Add) o If an RP in the Anycast-RP set is itself the DR for a
   directly connected source, it MUST send Register messages for
   that source to all other RPs in the Anycast-RP set, using its own
   IP address as the source address, following the Register state
   machine of [N1] as a DR would.

Notes
-----
   Under RFC 4601 a DR that is the RP does not register, so no
   Register is received and none is copied. Section 5.1 ("or the
   router itself") implies the intended behaviour but no procedure
   states it.

RFC 5015: Bidirectional Protocol Independent Multicast (BIDIR-PIM)

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 verified. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 8736, RFC 9436.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03643.5.3.5, 3.6, 3.7.2"DFT = BOperiod + OPlow; MC = 0 / DFT = OPlow_int; MC = 0 / Interval: The backoff interval in milliseconds to be used by routers with worse metrics than the offering router."The state table uses "BOperiod" and "OPlow_int", neither of which is defined in Section 3.6 (which defines Offer_Period, Backoff_Period, OPlow, OPhigh). For a router receiving a Backoff it is not said whether BOperiod is the Interval carried in the received Backoff message (the natural reading of 3.7.2) or the local Backoff_Period; for the DF sending Backoff ("DFT = BOperiod") it is presumably the local value. If a receiver uses a local value shorter than the DF's, it re-offers and takes over (Offer, MC reaches Election_Robustness) before the DF sends Pass, giving two acting DFs. 3.5.2.1 also uses "Offer_Interval" for the Offer_Period of 3.6.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-03653.5.3.1, 3.7.1"Used by the DF to record the identity and advertised metrics of the router that has made the last offer, for use when sending the Path message."PIM has no Path message; the Pass message is meant. Section 3.7.1: "A standard checksum IP checksum is used" (doubled word). Errata: Erratum 3762 covers "Path message"; the doubled word in 3.7.1 is not in any erratum.editorialerratum 3762 (Verified), editorial
RA-14393.5.2, 3.5.3.2, 3.7.1"When a router is participating in a DF election for an RPA on the interface that its MRIB indicates as the RPF Interface, then that router MUST always advertise an infinite metric in its election messages."The election messages carry a 32-bit Sender Metric Preference and a 32-bit Sender Metric (3.7.1, also the Offering and New Winner fields of 3.7.2 and 3.7.3), but the document never gives the encoding of an "infinite" metric. PIM-SM, to which 3.5.1 defers for comparison, has no wire value either, and its Assert carries a 31-bit preference after the RPT bit, so implementations that reuse assert encodings may send 0x7FFFFFFF / 0xFFFFFFFF while others send 0xFFFFFFFF / 0xFFFFFFFF. A receiver that tests for one value treats the other as a very poor but finite metric, so it cannot recognise that the sender has no path (for example on the RPA's own link, where both routers must advertise infinity), and the Lose state's "no router on the link has a path to the RPA" (3.5.3.1) cannot be detected reliably.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point
RA-14403.5.3.5, 3.5.3.4"Lose | Recv Pass for us: -> Offer DF = Sender; DFT = OPlow; MC = 0 (Figure 3) / On receipt of a Pass message, set the DF to be the target of the message and record its metrics. (3.5.3.4)"In Figure 3 a router in Lose, Win or Backoff state that receives a Pass naming itself as the new winner goes to Offer with "DF = Sender", i.e. records the router that has just resigned ("The old DF stops performing its tasks at the time the Pass message transmission is made", 3.5.2.2) as the acting DF, while 3.5.3.4 defines the DF on receipt of a Pass as its target. Until its Offers complete, the router therefore sends Joins (RPF_DF, 3.1.4) to a router that has stopped being DF, and the old DF, now in Lose with DF = Best, sees the receiver's Offers. Whether "Sender" is intended (conservative: no DF is assumed) or "Target" (as 3.5.3.4) is not stated, and in the Offer state the same event leads directly to Win.ambiguitynone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-0364 (RFC 5015, Section 3.5.3.5, 3.6, 3.7.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   DFT = BOperiod + OPlow; MC = 0

Corrected Text
--------------
   DFT = Backoff Interval (from the received Backoff message) +
   OPlow; MC = 0   [and define OPlow_int as OPlow in Section 3.6]

Notes
-----
   Section 3.6 defines neither value; the Interval field of the
   Backoff message (3.7.2) is otherwise unused by the state machine.

RFC 6513: Multicast in MPLS/BGP IP VPNs

Depth: deep. Errata: 2 errata: 1 verified, 1 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updated by: RFC 7582, RFC 7900, RFC 7988.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03705.1.3"1. The PEs in the candidate set are numbered from lowest to highest IP address, starting from 0. ... The result is taken modulo n, where n is the number of PEs in the candidate set."The candidate set is defined as a set of triples <route, Upstream PE, Upstream RD>, one per route with the same prefix, so one PE can appear several times (one route per RD). Step 1 numbers "PEs", but whether a PE appearing under two RDs is numbered once or twice, and so whether n counts PEs or routes, is not stated; PEs that differ select different upstream PEs, and steady-state duplication or loss follows. The default procedure also defines ordering only for "a 32-bit IP address", leaving IPv6 Upstream PEs (and mixed sets) to the implementer.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-03715.1.3"Another procedure, which SHOULD be implemented, is to use the Installed UMH Route as the Selected UMH Route."Three procedures are given (one MUST and default, one MUST but disabled, one SHOULD) without a mechanism for PEs to agree which is in use; the text itself notes that mixing them leads to "steady state duplication of traffic" unless wrong-PE discard (9.1.1) is in place. Consistency is left to configuration.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-14415.3.3, 5.3.1, 9.3.2"If a PE has pruned a C-source from a shared C-multicast tree, and it needs to "unprune" that source from that tree, it does so by withdrawing the route that pruned the source from the tree."Section 5.3.1 states that "There is no C-multicast route corresponding to the PIM function of pruning a source off the shared tree", and Section 9.3.2 that "there is no need to have any kind of C-multicast route that has the semantics of a PIM Prune(S,G,rpt) message"; the only C-multicast route types are source tree join and shared tree join (5.3.1). Section 5.3.3 nevertheless describes un-pruning by withdrawing "the route that pruned the source", a route the document says does not exist. An implementer cannot tell whether some route (for example a Source Active A-D route, whose withdrawal 9.3.2 describes) is meant, or whether the paragraph is a leftover.contradictionnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-14425.1.3"The default procedure, which MUST be implemented, is to select the route whose corresponding Upstream PE address is numerically highest"The UMH Route Candidate Set has one entry per route (one per RD), so the same Upstream PE can appear several times with different Upstream RDs (a PE with two VRFs of the MVPN, or a multihomed site advertised under two RDs). The default procedure then has a tie between routes with the same, highest Upstream PE, and the text gives no tie-breaker, although the Selected Upstream RD goes into the NLRI of the C-multicast route (5.3.1) and so decides which route the Upstream PE receives. The claim that "all PEs will have the same default Upstream PE selection" holds for the PE but not for the Selected UMH Route and RD.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-14437.4.2.2"| Type | Length | Reserved | / Length (16 bits): 16 / Reserved (8 bits)"In both S-PMSI Join figures (the generic TLV and the Type 1 message) the Length field is drawn over 15 bit positions (bits 8 to 22) and the following field (Value, Reserved) over 9 (bits 23 to 31), while the text gives Length 16 bits and Reserved 8 bits. The text and the Length value 16 (1 + 2 + 1 + 3 x 4 octets) agree with each other, so the figures are wrong, but an implementer working from the figures misplaces the field boundary.contradictionnone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below
RA-14447.4.2.1, 7.4.2.2"traffic for a particular C-flow can be switched back to the MI-PMSI simply by ceasing to send S-PMSI Joins for that C-flow. / If a PE (other than the transmitter) does not receive any packets over the S-PMSI P-tunnel for this amount of time, the PE will prune itself"The S-PMSI Join is refreshed every S-PMSI_INTERVAL (60 s), but no hold time is defined after which a receiver forgets a binding whose Joins have stopped; the only receiver timer, S-PMSI_TIMEOUT (3 minutes), runs on data packets. A receiver that applies the "discard from the wrong P-tunnel" logic of 7.1.2 / 9.1.1 therefore has no defined moment at which it starts accepting the flow on the MI-PMSI again after the transmitter "ceases to send S-PMSI Joins", other than waiting for the data timeout.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-144512.1.1"the optional GRE key field is used to identify a particular MVPN. In this case, each PE would have to advertise a key field value for each MVPN; each PE would assign the key field value that it expects to receive."No mechanism is given for advertising the GRE key: the PMSI Tunnel attribute for ingress replication carries an MPLS label as its demultiplexor (6.4.5, RFC 6514 5), and neither document defines a field for a GRE key. Two PEs using IP-in-GRE unicast P-tunnels therefore cannot learn each other's keys by protocol, and the receiver cannot otherwise tell which MVPN an unlabelled GRE packet belongs to.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point
RA-14463.2.2, 6.4.5, 8"Moreover, the use of ingress replication by any PE for an MVPN implies that all other PEs MUST use ingress replication for this MVPN."The requirement is stated without scope. Section 6.4.5 lets ingress replication instantiate "any kind of PMSI" (so one PE might use it for an S-PMSI while I-PMSIs use mLDP or RSVP-TE), and Section 8 instantiates every inter-AS segment of a segmented P-tunnel as a unicast P-tunnel while the intra-AS segments may use any technology. Read literally, a single ingress-replicated S-PMSI, or an ASBR-ASBR segment, would force every PE of the MVPN onto ingress replication; whether the MUST applies only to I-PMSIs, per AS, or to PEs only is not stated.ambiguitynone: RFC has 2 errata, none on this point

Proposed erratum RA-1441 (RFC 6513, Section 5.3.3, 5.3.1, 9.3.2; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   If a PE has pruned a C-source from a shared C-multicast tree, and
   it needs to "unprune" that source from that tree, it does so by
   withdrawing the route that pruned the source from the tree.

Corrected Text
--------------
   (Paragraph deleted.  Sources are not pruned from a shared
   C-multicast tree by C-multicast routes; see Sections 5.3.1 and
   9.3.2.)

Notes
-----
   Apparently a leftover from an earlier draft that had a
   C-multicast route with Prune(S,G,rpt) semantics. The source-tree
   switch is handled by Source Active A-D routes (Section 9.3.2, RFC
   6514 Section 13).

Proposed erratum RA-1442 (RFC 6513, Section 5.1.3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The default procedure, which MUST be implemented, is to select
   the route whose corresponding Upstream PE address is numerically
   highest, where a 32-bit IP address is treated as a 32-bit
   unsigned integer.

Corrected Text
--------------
   The default procedure, which MUST be implemented, is to select
   the route whose corresponding Upstream PE address is numerically
   highest, where a 32-bit IP address is treated as a 32-bit
   unsigned integer; if several routes have that Upstream PE, the
   one whose Upstream RD is numerically lowest is selected.

Notes
-----
   The tie-break proposed is one possibility; any deterministic rule
   shared by all PEs would do, since the Selected Upstream RD is
   carried in the C-multicast route.

Proposed erratum RA-1150 (RFC 6514, Section 5, 8; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   A router that supports the PMSI Tunnel attribute considers this
   attribute to be malformed if either (a) it contains an undefined
   tunnel type in the Tunnel Type field of the attribute, or (b) ...

Corrected Text
--------------
   A router that supports the PMSI Tunnel attribute considers this
   attribute to be malformed if the router cannot parse the Tunnel
   Identifier field of the attribute as a tunnel identifier of the
   tunnel type specified in the Tunnel Type field of the attribute.
   A tunnel type unknown to the router is not an error; such a route
   is not used for joining a P-tunnel. When a router determines that
   the attribute is malformed, the router SHOULD treat this Update
   as though all the routes contained in this Update had been
   withdrawn, whether or not the Partial bit is set.

Notes
-----
   Applies to both the PMSI Tunnel attribute (Section 5) and the PE
   Distinguisher Labels attribute (Section 8). RFC 7606 later gives
   treat-as-withdraw as the general default, but does not revise the
   "undefined tunnel type" rule of this section.

RFC 6625: Wildcards in Multicast VPN Auto-Discovery Routes

Depth: deep. Errata: 1 errata: 1 held. Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 6514. Updated by: RFC 7582, RFC 7900, RFC 8534.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03733.2.1"Otherwise, if there is an installed S-PMSI A-D route originated by PE2, whose NLRI contains (C-,C-), then (C-S,C-G) matches that route."The "Otherwise" chain makes the match exclusive: a (C-S,C-G) state matches only the most specific installed S-PMSI route from its upstream PE. Erratum 5605 (held) argues that several routes can match at once (for example while switching from a (C-,C-) to a (C-S,C-G) S-PMSI), and the AD note points to the later changes in RFC 7582, RFC 7900 and RFC 8534. A receiver that joins only the best match may lose packets while the ingress moves the flow between trees. Later RFCs: RFC 8534 Section 3 (updates RFC 6625) keeps a single match for reception but has it ignore S-PMSI routes without tunnel information, and adds a separate match for tracking; the tunnel-switch case is not addressed.ambiguityerratum 5605 (Held for Document Update), technical
RA-14474.3"Specifically, if a PE receives a (C-S,C-*) S-PMSI A-D route, and the PE can determine that C-G is not an SSM group address, the PE SHOULD "ignore" this S-PMSI A-D route."A (C-S,C-*) route carries no C-G (the group is the wildcard), so the condition cannot be evaluated on the received route. The rule can only be meant per flow: the route is not used for a (C-S,C-G) whose C-G is not an SSM address, which is what the matching rules of 3.1 and 3.2.1 already say ("AND if C-G is an SSM group address"). Read literally, the sentence is either never applicable or invites a PE to drop the whole route because some flow it is interested in is ASM. The same section also switches to "then PE1 applies the procedures" although no PE1 is introduced there.errornone: RFC has 1 errata, none on this point; proposed erratum below

RA-14494.4, 3.2.2"The PE has a currently originated a C-multicast Shared Tree Join route for (C-*,C-G) (4.4)"Stray "a" ("has a currently originated a"). In 3.2.2 "(C-,C-G) matches a non-wildcard S-PMSI A-D route (as detailed in Section 12.3 of [MVPN-BGP])" is unclear: RFC 6514 12.3 does not define a match between (C-,C-G) and a non-wildcard route; it describes when a PE with only a Shared Tree Join joins an (C-S,C-G) S-PMSI tunnel (via Source Active routes). Proposed erratum RA-1447 (RFC 6625, Section 4.3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   Specifically, if a PE receives a (C-S,C-*) S-PMSI A-D route, and
   the PE can determine that C-G is not an SSM group address, the PE
   SHOULD "ignore" this S-PMSI A-D route.

Corrected Text
--------------
   Specifically, a (C-S,C-*) S-PMSI A-D route is never matched
   (Sections 3.1 and 3.2.1) by a (C-S,C-G) whose C-G is not an SSM
   group address; for such C-flows the PE SHOULD "ignore" this
   S-PMSI A-D route.

Notes
-----
   A (C-S,C-*) route has a wildcard group, so "C-G is not an SSM
   group address" cannot be determined from the route. The matching
   rules in Sections 3.1 and 3.2.1 already restrict (C-S,C-*)
   matches to SSM groups; the sentence should be phrased per C-flow.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-03754, 5.1.3"This document defines a new Transitive IPv4-Address-Specific Extended Community Sub-Type: "Inter-Area P2MP Next-Hop". / these routes MUST carry the Inter-Area P2MP Segmented Next-Hop Extended Community."The community is registered as "Inter-Area P2MP Next-Hop" but is called "Inter-Area P2MP Segmented Next-Hop Extended Community" everywhere else, and once "P2MP Next-Hop Extended Community". Section 4 also reads "may be the loopback address or the PE, ABR, or ASBR" for "of the PE, ABR, or ASBR".editorialnone: RFC has no errata
RA-077014.5, 16, 5.1.2, 5.2.2"then an ingress ABR will advertise into the backbone area an S-PMSI A-D route. This route is constructed following the procedures in Section 7.1.2.1. / in the P2MP RSVP-TE specification [RFC3209]"There is no Section 7.1.2.1; the S-PMSI A-D route for global table multicast that the ABR originates is specified in Section 7.2.2.1 (which the egress-ABR paragraph just before correctly cites). Section 16 cites RFC 3209 as "the P2MP RSVP-TE specification"; P2MP RSVP-TE is RFC 4875 (already in the references). The headings of 5.1.2 and 5.2.2 say "Routes Re-advertised by PE or ASBR" while both sections specify re-advertisement by ingress and egress ABRs.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07716.2.2, 7.1, 9, 5.2"If the value of this octet is 0x01, 0x02, or 0x03, then this Leaf A-D route was originated in response to an S-PMSI or I-PMSI A-D route. If the value of this octet is either 0x00 or 0xff, and octets 3 through 10 contain either all 0x00 or all 0xff"The rule distinguishes MVPN Route Keys (an embedded MCAST-VPN NLRI starting with its route type) from global-table keys (an 8-octet RD of all 0x00 or 0xff), but Sections 5.2, 6.2.1, 7.2.1 and 9 apply the same "third octet 0x01, 0x02 or 0x03" test to VPLS. A Leaf A-D route answering a VPLS A-D route carries that route's NLRI as Route Key; if it is encoded as in RFC 4761 3.2.2 or RFC 6074 3.2.2, it begins with a 2-octet Length whose first octet is 0x00 and whose second is not, so the key matches neither case and the receiving ABR or ingress PE has no rule for it. Section 14.4 similarly speaks only of "the received service S-PMSI A-D route" although 14.2 applies to I-PMSI and VPLS A-D routes too. Later RFCs: RFC 8534 Section 5.2 (updates RFC 7524) adds a third Leaf A-D Route Key form (RD first, with a route distinguisher that is neither 0 nor all ones), which this test classifies as neither case.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata

RFC 7761: Protocol Independent Multicast - Sparse Mode (PIM-SM): Protocol Specification (Revised)

Depth: deep. Errata: 4 errata: 2 verified, 1 held, 1 rejected. Status: Internet Standard (STD 83). Obsoletes: RFC 4601. Updated by: RFC 8736, RFC 9436.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-00894.4.2, 4.11"set KeepaliveTimer(S,G) to RP_Keepalive_Period;"The RP pseudocode sets the (S,G) Keepalive Timer to RP_Keepalive_Period alone, while section 4.11 says the KAT "is set to max(Keepalive_Period, RP_Keepalive_Period) when a Register-Stop is sent". With default timers RP_Keepalive_Period (3 x Register_Suppression_Time + Register_Probe_Time = 185 s) is shorter than Keepalive_Period (210 s), so the two readings differ. RA-11544.7.1"From this list of matching RPs, find the ones with highest priority. Eliminate any RPs from the list that have lower priorities."The direction of "highest priority" is not stated. An implementer reading 4.7.1 alone may pick the numerically highest C-RP priority and map groups to a different RP than the rest of the domain, which breaks the requirement that all routers "map a particular multicast group address to the same RP". RA-1156Abstract, 4.5, 4.6, 6.3, Appendix A"In addition, if the Hello message from a neighbor was authenticated (see Section 6.3), then all Join/Prune messages from that neighbor MUST also be authenticated."The Abstract and Appendix A state that "authentication using IPsec" has been removed from RFC 4601 for lack of deployment, yet 4.5 and 4.6 keep normative requirements tied to authenticated Hellos, and 6.3 points to RFC 5796 (a normative reference), which is IPsec ESP / AH authentication of PIM link-local messages. RA-11574.6 (Summary of Assert Rules, items 5 and 7), 4.6.1"An assert loser that receives a Join(,G) with an Upstream Neighbor Address that is its primary IP address on that interface expires the (,G) Assert Timer and all (S,G) assert timers that do not have corresponding Prune(S,G,rpt) messages"The (S,G) Assert state machine of 4.6.1 has the event "Receive Join(S,G) on interface I" but no event for a Join(,G); only the (,G) machine reacts to Join(,G). RA-11584.9.5.1"There are, however, a number of combinations that have a valid interpretation but that are not generated by the protocol ... including both an (S,G) Join and an (S,G,rpt) Prune in the same message is usually redundant."The text lists an (S,G) Join together with an (S,G,rpt) Prune among the combinations "not generated by the protocol", but the summary table marks that pair "yes" ("Allowed and expected") in both the Join(S,G) row and the Prune(S,G,rpt) row; the "?" marking ("not expected ... RFC 8534: Explicit Tracking with Wildcard Routes in Multicast VPN

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard. Updates: RFC 6514, RFC 6625, RFC 7524, RFC 7582, RFC 7900.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-12535.2, 6"The Route Key field of the NLRI will have the format shown in Figure 1 (as defined in Sections 4.3 and 4.4 of [RFC6514])."RFC 6514 Section 4.4 defines the Leaf A-D Route Key as the NLRI of the route being responded to, i.e. an embedded MCAST-VPN NLRI starting with its Route Type and Length octets. Figure 1 (titled "NLRI of S-PMSI A-D Route") instead starts with the RD and has no Route Type or Length octets, mirroring the RFC 7524 Section 6.2.2 global-table layout. Both readings are implementable and they produce different octets: one sender embeds "type 3, length, RD, S, G, originator" (identical in shape to the key of a response to a (C-S,C-G) S-PMSI route), another sends "RD, S, G, PE address". Receivers that classify keys with the RFC 7524 third-octet test see an RD-first key whose third octet is 0x00 (high octet of the RD type) and whose RD is neither all zeros nor all ones, which matches neither case of that test. The document also uses "wildcard Leaf A-D route" for two different things: a per-flow route tracking a (C-*,C-G) flow (Source Length 0) and a route responding to a wildcard S-PMSI A-D route.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12543"When applying the rules of Sections 3.2.1 or 3.2.2 of [RFC6625], it is REQUIRED to ignore any S-PMSI A-D route that has no PTA, or whose PTA specifies "no tunnel information present"."The change applies to every implementation of RFC 6625 matching, also those that never use LIR-pF, but RFC 6625 Section 3.2 itself still reads "if there is an installed S-PMSI A-D route ... then (C-S,C-G) matches that route" for any installed route. An implementer working from RFC 6625 alone selects a (C-S,C-G) route with "no tunnel information present" (sent only to request explicit tracking, Section 4 procedure 1) as the match, finds no tunnel in it and does not join the wildcard or I-PMSI tunnel on which the ingress actually sends the flow. The open-ended clause for "other RFCs that update [RFC6625]" leaves the effect on future matching rules to the reader.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12555.2, 6"If the match for tracking/reception is a wildcard S-PMSI A-D route, the egress node may originate a wildcard Leaf A-D route in response, as well as originating one or more non-wildcard Leaf A-D routes."For Ingress Replication the per-flow Leaf A-D route MAY carry label 0 or "no tunnel information present", in which case the ingress uses "the label that the egress PE specified in the PTA of the Leaf A-D route that it originated in response to the LIR flag of the match for reception". That route exists only if the egress originated the response to the wildcard route, which this paragraph makes optional ("may"); with LIR-pF set the LIR flag is also set (Section 2), so RFC 6514 already requires that response, and the "may" contradicts it. The ingress behaviour when neither a per-flow label nor a wildcard response exists is not given.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-12562, 7"This document defines a new flag in the Flags field of the PMSI Tunnel attribute. This new flag is known as the "Leaf Information Required per Flow" flag (LIR-pF)."The position of the flag in the Flags octet is given only by the IANA entry "Value: 2", which in the RFC 7902 registry is a bit number counted from the most significant bit (LIR is bit 7, mask 0x01), so the mask is 0x20. The body text never states the bit number or mask, and "Value: 2" is easily read as the mask 0x02.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-12571"These routes are known as (C-,C-S) S-PMSI A-D routes, (C-S,C-) S-PMSI A-D routes, or (C-,C-) S-PMSI A-D routes""(C-,C-S)" should be "(C-,C-G)": the source is the wildcarded element and the group is kept.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-12583, 4, 5.2, 6"In the absence of such a specification, the LIR-pF flag SHOULD BE ignored.""SHOULD BE" is not a BCP 14 keyword form (SHOULD be); "LIR-pf" (Section 3) for "LIR-pF"; "as specified in Section 5.2)." has a stray parenthesis (Section 4); "after it has already received the S-PMSI A-D that is the match" lacks "route" (Section 5.2); "a group address(G)" lacks a space.editorialnone: RFC has no errata

Proposed erratum RA-1253 (RFC 8534, Section 5.2, 6; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   The Route Key field of the NLRI will have the format shown in
   Figure 1 (as defined in Sections 4.3 and 4.4 of [RFC6514]).

Corrected Text
--------------
   The Route Key field of the NLRI will have the format shown in
   Figure 1. (Unlike the Route Key defined in Section 4.4 of
   [RFC6514], it does not contain the Route Type and Length octets
   of an S-PMSI A-D route; it has the layout of the Route Key
   defined in Section 6.2.2 of [RFC7524].)

Notes
-----
   The citation of RFC 6514 Sections 4.3 and 4.4 suggests the
   embedded-NLRI form, while Figure 1 (whose caption, "NLRI of
   S-PMSI A-D Route", also does not describe it) shows an RD-first
   form without Route Type and Length. Receivers that use the RFC
   7524 Section 6.2.2 third-octet test cannot classify the Figure 1
   form, since its third octet is 0x00 and its RD is neither all
   zeros nor all ones. The term "wildcard Leaf A-D route" is also
   used both for a per-flow (C-*,C-G) route and for a response to a
   wildcard S-PMSI A-D route.

Proposed erratum RA-1254 (RFC 8534, Section 3; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   When applying the rules of Sections 3.2.1 or 3.2.2 of [RFC6625],
   it is REQUIRED to ignore any S-PMSI A-D route that has no PTA, or
   whose PTA specifies "no tunnel information present".

Corrected Text
--------------
   (No text change needed; the RFC 6625 Section 3.2 text should
   carry a note pointing to this rule, since the rule changes RFC
   6625 behaviour for all implementations, not only those supporting
   LIR-pF.)

Notes
-----
   Implementers following RFC 6625 Section 3.2 without this document
   select a no-tunnel S-PMSI A-D route as the match for reception
   and fail to join the tunnel that carries the flow.

Proposed erratum RA-1257 (RFC 8534, Section 1; type: Technical):

Original Text
-------------
   These routes are known as (C-*,C-S) S-PMSI A-D routes, (C-S,C-*)
   S-PMSI A-D routes, or (C-*,C-*) S-PMSI A-D routes,

Corrected Text
--------------
   These routes are known as (C-*,C-G) S-PMSI A-D routes, (C-S,C-*)
   S-PMSI A-D routes, or (C-*,C-*) S-PMSI A-D routes,

Notes
-----
   The wildcard route with the source replaced by a wildcard is the
   (C-*,C-G) S-PMSI A-D route of RFC 6625.

RFC 9026: Multicast VPN Fast Upstream Failover

Depth: deep. Errata: none (the RFC has no errata). Status: Proposed Standard.

IDSectionQuoteIssueSeverityErratum
RA-07724.4.2"then it MUST be re-advertised in eBGP with a MED attribute (MULTI_EXIT_DISC) set to the highest possible value (0xffff). / If the route was received over eBGP and its MED attribute is set to 0xffff"MULTI_EXIT_DISC is a four-octet unsigned integer (RFC 4271 4.3, 5.1.4); its highest value is 0xFFFFFFFF, not 0xffff. An ASBR that sends the highest possible value and a peer ASBR that tests for 0xffff (or the reverse) will not recognize each other's standby marking, so the Standby route is mapped back to iBGP with a normal LOCAL_PREF and may be preferred over the primary.errornone: RFC has no errata; proposed erratum below
RA-07734.1"routes that carry the Standby PE BGP Community must have the LOCAL_PREF attribute set to the value lower than the value specified as the LOCAL_PREF attribute for the route that does not carry the Standby PE BGP Community. / The new Upstream PE must set the LOCAL_PREF attribute for that C-multicast route to the same value as when the Standby PE BGP Community was included in the advertisement."On failover the downstream PE (not "the new Upstream PE", which receives rather than originates the C-multicast route) resends the route without the Standby PE community. Keeping the standby LOCAL_PREF (zero is RECOMMENDED) on a route that no longer carries the community breaks the preceding rule that non-standby routes have the higher LOCAL_PREF: another downstream PE's Standby route for the same NLRI now has an equal LOCAL_PREF, which is the race the rule was introduced to prevent. It is not clear which PE the sentence addresses or what value is intended.contradictionnone: RFC has no errata
RA-07743.1.6"The BFD Discriminator attribute MUST be considered malformed if its length is smaller than 11 octets or if Optional TLVs are present but not well formed."11 octets is BFD Mode, BFD Discriminator and an IPv4 Source IP Address TLV; it is not a valid minimum for an IPv6 Source IP Address TLV (23) and it is more than the 5 octets a mode other than P2MP (which does not need the TLV) would require. The Source IP Address TLV carries no address-family field, so the family is inferred from Length (4 or 16) only. "Not well formed" is not defined for unknown TLV types. The paragraph also says "the UPDATE message SHALL be handled using ... Attribute Discard", where the attribute, not the UPDATE, is discarded.ambiguitynone: RFC has no errata
RA-07754.4.1, 3"Standby C-multicast route (C-multicast route carrying the Standby extended community) (4.4.1) / The procedure described here is optional one (3)"The Standby PE marker is a BGP (well-known) Community, 0xFFFF0009 (4.1, 7.1), not an extended community. Also 3: "is optional one"; 4.4.1: "In additional to".editorialnone: RFC has no errata
